SERMONS VI (last) (339-396) ON VARIOUS TOPICS
(MAUR. 339 + MAUR. 40
Topic: The weight of being a bishop. Location: Hippo. Date: Anniversary of Augustine's episcopal ordination. Very varied dates are proposed.

1. Today, brothers, invites me to reflect more carefully on the burden I carry. Although I must think day and night about her weight, I don't know how this anniversary date throws her over my senses, so I can't help thinking about her. And to the extent that the years progress, or, rather, return, and bring us closer to the last day, which, without a doubt, must sometime come, the thought of the account that I must give to God our Lord for all of you seems to me more and more vivid and penetrating and more painful. Between each one of you and me, this is the difference: you almost only have to give an account of yourself, while I have to give an account of myself and of all of you. Consequently, the burden is greater, which, well carried, brings greater glory; but, exercised without fidelity, it precipitates the most terrible of tortures. What, above all, should I do today, except to entrust to you the danger in which I find myself, so that you may be my joy? The danger in which SERMO

I find myself nothing other than paying attention to how you praise me, without worrying about how you live. He under whose gaze I speak, better yet, under whose gaze I think, knows that the praise of the people delights me less than the way those who praise me live torments and disturbs me. I don't want praise from those who live badly; I hate them, I detest them; They cause me pain, not pleasure. If I said that I did not want the praise of those who live well, I would be lying; If I say that I love them, I fear that I desire vanity more than solidity. What should I say, then? I neither fully love them nor fully stop loving them. I do not want them fully, so that human praise does not put me in danger; I do not stop loving them completely, so as not to be ungrateful to those to whom I preach. 2. My burden is what you just heard when the prophet Ezekiel was read. As if the invitation that the same date makes me to think about it were not enough, a reading has also been read that instills great fear in me, so that I think about what I carry on me, because, if the one who imposed it on me does not carry it with me, I will succumb. This is what you have heard: If I bring the sword upon a territory and he places a watchman who can see the sword coming, he will warn and announce it; If, when the sword comes, the watchman is silent and the sword kills the sinner, the sinner will certainly die for his wickedness, but I will claim his blood at the hand of the watchman. If, on the contrary, when he sees the sword coming he blows the trumpet and announces it, and the one to whom he announces it does not listen, he will die in his evil.

dad, but the watchman will have saved his life. And I have made you, son of man, a watchman for the children of Israel. He himself explained what he understood by sword, what by watchman, and what by death; He did not allow our negligence to take the excuse of the obscurity of reading. I have placed you, he says, as a lookout. If I say to the sinner: "You will die," and you remain silent and he dies in his sin, he will certainly die deservedly and justly for his sin, but I will claim his blood at your hand. If you, on the other hand, say to the sinner: "You will die," and he does not listen, he will die in his wickedness, but you will have saved your life. And he added the words that he wanted to be said to the people of Israel: You will say therefore to the children of Israel: What is it that is said among you: 'Our iniquities weigh on us, we are consumed in our sins; how can we live?' This is what the Lord says: I do not want the death of the wicked, but rather that he turn from his evil way and live. This is what he wanted me to announce to you. If I don't do it, I will have to give a bad account as a lookout. If, however, I announce it to you, I have done my part. There you; I'm already sure. But how can you be sure, who are in danger and about to die? I do not want my glory to be associated with your torment. Certainly, security has been granted to me, but charity makes me solicitous. See that I speak, and you know well that I have always spoken; You know that I have never been silent. This is what God says: "I do not want the death of the wicked, but rather that he be converted."

Sarcina autem mea est, quam moda audistis, cum Ezechiel propheta legeretur (cf. Ez 33,2-11). Parum est enim, quia dies ipse admonet nos [113] eamdem sarcinam cogitare; insuper etiam talis lectio recitatur, quae nobis incutiat magnum timorem, ut quid portemus cogitemus; quia nisi nobiscum qui imposuit portet, deficimus. Ecce audistis: Tena, inquit, super quam induxero gladium, et posuerit sibi exploratorem qui uideat gladium superuenientem, et dicat, et denuntiet; ueniente autem gladio taceat til: explorator, et superueniens gladius super peccatorem occidat; peccator quidem pro sua iniquitate morietur, sanguinem autem eius de manu exploratoris inquiram. Sed quomodo securi uos, periclitantes et morituri? Nolumus sit our glory with our poetry. Data est quidem securitas, sed facit solicitos caraitas. "from your bad path and live." What was the wicked saying? He mentioned the words of the wicked and wicked: Our iniquities weigh upon us and we waste away in our sins; how can we live? The patient loses hope, but the doctor gives it back to him. The man said to himself: How can we live? God tells you: "You can live." Although every man is a liar, only God is truthful; Erase what man said and write what God said. Don't despair; you can live, relying not on your past evils, but on your future goods. You will erase evil if you turn away from evil. With change all things are destroyed, both good and bad. From a holy life you went to a bad life: you erased the first. See where you tend and what you will receive; you have two treasures ready; whatever you send, that you will find; God is a faithful guardian, and will return you according to your work. 3. There are, however, others who do not perish from despair. It is not said: Our evils weigh upon us and we consume ourselves in our sins; how can we live? But they deceive themselves in another way: they flatter themselves with the infinite mercy of God, so as to never have to correct themselves. This is what they say: "Although we do evil, although we commit iniquities, although we live in lust and crime, although we despise the poor and the needy, although we are puffed up with pride, although there is no pain in our hearts for the evils we have spoken of, will God allow so many people to perish and deliver so few? There are two,

Therefore, the dangers: one, the one we heard from the prophet's mouth, and another that the Apostle did not remain silent about. Indeed, against those who perish in despair, as if they were gladiators destined to die by the sword, longing for pleasures and living in evil and despising their souls as already condemned without remission, they repeat what they say to themselves: Our evils weigh on us and we consume ourselves in our sins, how can we live? But what the Apostle says is another thing: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, mercy, and long-suffering? Against those who say that God is good and merciful and will not allow such a large crowd to perish, saving a few—certainly, if he did not want them to exist, they would not even live; Although they commit so much evil and continue to live, if God were displeased that they lived, He would instantly make them disappear from the earth -, against them the Apostle says: Do you not know that God's patience is to lead you to penitence? You, however, according to the hardness and impenitence of your heart, store up wrath for yourself against the day of wrath and the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who will reward each one according to his works. Who is he saying this to? To those who think that God is so good that he will reward us. He will certainly reward each one according to his works. What are you up to? You treasure. That? Gonna. Pile up wrath upon wrath, increase your treasure; What you have treasured will be returned to you, the one to whom you entrust it will not let you down. Aeger desperat, sed medicus spem promittit. Homo sibi said: Quomodo possumus uiuere? Deus dicit, Potes uiuere. Si omnis homo mendax (Ps 115,11), deus solus uerax: deleat quod dixit homo, et scribat quod dixit deus. Noli [114] desperare, potes uiuere, non de praeteritis malis tuis, sed de futuris bonis tuis: delebis mala, si recedes a malo. Omnia siue bona siue mala mutatione delentur. De uita bona inclinasti te ad malam, delesti bonam. Vide quo adtendas, quid percipias: thesauri duo sunt tibi praeparati; quod miseris, hoc inuenies; fidelis custos est deus, reddet, tibi quod feceris. 3. virginity or marital chastity; stay away from theft, homicide, crime; remember the needy, for you are also needy; remember the poor, because you are poor too; No matter how much you swim in riches, you are clothed in rags of flesh; If, thinking and doing these things, you send them to the good treasury for the day of judgment, the one who defrauds no one and repays each person according to his works will say to you: “Take what you sent, since there is plenty; When you sent it, you didn't notice it, but I kept it to return it to you. In fact, brothers, everyone who sends something to a treasure knows that he is sending it; but, once sent, you no longer see it. Suppose your treasure is underground with only one access or crack to get into; Little by little you introduce what you earn, but you stop seeing it. If the earth keeps what you give it and you don't see it again, won't he who made heaven and earth keep it for you? 4. Lighten up, therefore, brothers; Lighten my load by helping me carry it: live well. Today I have to feed those who are poor like me, and I have to behave humanely with them; I offer you my word as a delicacy. It is impossible for me to feed everyone with palpable and visible bread; Where I get to feed you, I get from there to feed myself; I am a servant, not a father of a family. I serve you from the same thing that I live on: from the treasure of the Lord, from the banquet of that father of a family who, being rich, became poor for us so that we could become rich with his poverty. If I served you bread, it would have to be broken; each one

You would take a piece, and no matter how much it was useful, only a small portion would reach each of you. On the other hand, what I say has everything each and every one of them in particular. Have you divided the syllables of my words among yourselves? Does each of you take away a word from this long sermon? Each of you heard it in its entirety. But pay attention to how you heard it; I am only the one who gives it to you, not the one who will ask you to account. If I don't give it and keep the money to myself, the Gospel terrifies me. He could say: "Why do I have to annoy men and say to the wicked: Do not do evil, live like this, act in this other way, stop doing that?" Who orders me to be a burden to men? I have already been told how I should live; I will live as I have been commanded and as I have been ordered. I take responsibility for what I have received; Why should I have to account for others? The Gospel terrifies me. In fact, no one would surpass me in desire to live in that full security of contemplation, free of temporal worries; There is nothing better, nothing sweeter, than scrutinizing the divine treasure without any noise; It is a sweet and good thing; On the other hand, preaching, arguing, correcting, edifying, caring for each person, is a great burden, a great weight - and a great fatigue. Who wouldn't flee from this fatigue? But the Gospel terrifies me. A certain servant approached and said to his master: “I knew that you were a hard man, that you reap where you did not sow. I kept your money, I didn't want to give it away; take what is yours, judge if anything is missing; If everything is there, don't bother me. But

uirginitatem, uel pudicitiam coniugalem; a fraud, ab homicide, ab scelere alienus sis; memineris egentis, quia et tu eges; memineris pauperis, quia et tu pauper es, [115] quamtumlibet abundes diuitiis, pannis carnis indutus es: si haec cogitans et haec agens mittis in thesaurum bonum per diem iudicii, ille qui neminem fraudat, et reddet unicuique secundum opera sua, dicet tibi: Tolle quod misisti, quia abundat; quando mittebas, non uidebas, sed ego seruabam quomodo redditurus eram. Pascendos habemus hodie compauperes nostros, et cum eis communicanda est humanitas: uobis autem fercula mea uerba ista sunt. Pascere omnes pane tractabili et uisibili non sufficio: inde pasco, unde pascor; minister sum, paterfamilias non sum; inde uobis appono, unde et ego uiuo, de thesauro dominico, de epulis illius patrisfamilias, qui propter nos pauper factus est, cum diues esset, ut eius paupertate nos ditaremur (2 Cor 8,9). Si panem uobis poneem, fracto

pane singular frusta ablaturi eratis; et si ego multum poneem, perparum ad singulos perueniret. Modo autem quod dico, et omnes totum habent, et singuli quique totum habent. Numquid enim verbi mei Inter vos syllabas divisistis? Numquid ipsius producti sermonis singula uerba abstulistis? Vnusquisque uestrum totum audiuit. Sed uideat quomodo audiuit, quia erogator sum, non exactor. Si non erogem, et pecuniam seruem, terret me euangelium. Possem enim dicere: Quid mihi est, taedio esse hominibus? I will say miquis: Inique agere nolite, sic uiuite, sic agite, sic agere desistite. Quid mihi est, oneri esse hominibus? Accepi quomodo uiuam: uiuam quomodo iussus sum, quomodo praeceptus sum. Adsignem quod accepi: de alus reddere rationem quo mihi? Euangelium me terret. Nam ad istam securitatem otiosissimam nemo me uinceret: nihil est melius, nihil dulcius, quam diuinum scrutari nullo strepente thesaurum: dulce est, bonum est; praedicare autem, arguere, corripere, aedificare, pro unoquoque satagere, magnum onus, magnum pondus, magnus [116] labor. Quis non refuge istum laborem? Sed terret euangelium. Processit seruus quidam, et ait domino suo: Sciebam te hominem molestum meteré ubi non seminasti (Luke 19,21); seruaui pecuniam tuam, nolui eam erogare: tolle quod tuum est; if aliquid minum est, judica; si integrum est, noli mihi molestus esse. The master said to him: "Bad servant, through your mouth I condemn you." -Because? —If you said I was greedy, why didn't you worry about my earnings? —I didn't give it away for fear of losing it. —Is that what you say? Frequently, this is said: —Why are you correcting him? It's time wasted, he doesn't listen to you. —But I, he says, didn't want to give so as not to lose your money. He answered: «You should have given my money, so that I could demand it when I returned with the interest; I put you, he said, as a giver, not as an exacter; "You should have worried about giving, leaving it to me to collect." Fearing something similar, let each one see how he has received it. If I, the one whose turn it is to give, am afraid, should the one who receives be calm? Whoever was bad yesterday, be good today. This is what I give you: "Whoever was bad yesterday, be good today." Yesterday was bad, and he did not die; If he had died in his wickedness, he would have gone to the place from which he would not return. Yesterday was bad and today it lives; Be profitable to live, do not live badly. Why do you want to add today's evil to yesterday's evil? You want to have a long life; Don't you want it to be good? Who endures something bad for a long time, even if it is a meal? Has mental blindness hardened to such an extent, to such an extent has the inner man become deaf, that he wants to have everything good except himself? Do you want to have a farm? I deny that you want to have it bad. You want to have a wife or a house, but only if they are good. Why review each specific thing? You don't want to have bad stomachs, and do you want to have bad life? As if bad calyxes caused you more harm than a bad life! If your bad heels hurt you because they squeeze you, you sit down, you take off your shoes, you throw them away, or you repair them, or you change them,

so as not to damage the toe, and then you put your shoes back on. But you don't worry about correcting your bad life, which makes you lose your soul. I see clearly where the origin of your error is: the pain that hurts you causes you pain, while the life that hurts you causes you pleasure. In one case there is pain and in another satisfaction; but what produces satisfaction for the moment, later causes more intense pain, while what for the moment produces healthy pain, later causes joy with infinite pleasure and inexhaustible joy. 5. See one and the other: the one who lives in pleasure and the one who lives in pain; The rich lived among pleasures and the poor among pains; the first feasted, the second suffered; that one was treated with respect by the family around him, this one was licked by the dogs; that one became harder in his banquets, this one could not even be satisfied with crumbs. The pleasure passed, the need passed; The goods of the rich and the evils of the poor passed away; Evil came to the rich and good came to the poor. What is past is past forever; What came after, never diminished. The rich burned in hell, the poor rejoiced in the bosom of Abraham. First the poor man had desired a crumb from the rich man's table; Then the rich man desired a drop from the poor man's finger. His penury ended in satiety; His pleasure turned into endless pain. May you all have this, I want us all to have this together. In fact, what food could I offer you if I invited you all and this church was full of tables for diners? These are temporary things. give it back, who will take it from us? If God is with us, who can be against us? When we were still sinners, he gave us the death of Christ; Now that we live justly, is it going to disappoint us? From the dregs of the flesh, a certain desire for greatness had infiltrated the disciples of Christ the Lord, our apostles, and the smoke of vanity had already begun to reach their eyes. Well, as we read in the Gospel, a dispute arose between them about who would be the greatest. But the Lord, a doctor who was present, stopped that tumor. When he saw the evil that had given rise to that dispute, he put some children before him and said to the apostles: Whoever does not act like this child will not enter the kingdom of heaven. In the person of the child he recommended humility. My left is not my turn to grant it to you; My Father has it prepared for others. For whom is it prepared if it is not prepared for the disciples? And he rightly puts forward his humility when he says: My Father has prepared it for others; Since he personally prepared it, he said that it was prepared by his Father, so that here again he would not give the impression of being vain and, consequently, not build the humility, which motivated everything he had said. And, truly, the Father does not prepare what the Son does not prepare, nor does the Son prepare what the Father does not prepare, since he says: I and the Father are one; and also: Whatever the Father does, the Son also does equally. He was a master of humility in word and deed; In fact, as for the word, from the beginning of creation, he never remained silent nor ceased to teach humility through the angels and the prophets; and he also deigned to teach it by his example. Our creator came in humility, created among us; He who made us and was made for us: God before time, man in time, to free man from time. He came, like a great doctor, to cure our swelling. From east to west, the human race lay like a great sick person, and required a great doctor. He sent his assistants first, and then he arrived when some had already lost hope. He did like the doctors: when they send their assistants, es meatn non est meum daré vobis; alus paratum est a Patre meo (ib., 20,23). Quibus paratum est, si discipulis non paratum est? Qui illic sedebunt, si apostoli non sedebunt? Alus paratum est, [641] non vobis paratum est: aliis, non superbis. Et bene et ipse humilitatem praetendit, cum diceret, Aliis paratum est a Patre meo; cum utique ipse praepararet, a Patre suo dixit praeparari: ne et hic arrogans esse videretur, et non aedificadoret ad humilitatem, propter quam ista omnia loquebatur. Ñeque enim parat Pater, quod non parat Filius, aut parat Filius quod non parat Pater, cum ipse dicat: Ego et Pater unum sumus (lo 10,30); ipse etiam dicat: quaecumque Pater facit, haec eadem et Filius similiter facit (ib., 5,19). Doctor humilitatis sermone et opere: sermone enim semper ab initio creaturae numquam tacuit, per angelos, per prophetas, docere hominem humilitatem; Docere dignified is etiam exemplo suo.

Venit humilis creator noster, creatus Inter nos: qui fecit nos, qui factus est propter nos: deus ante tempora, homo in tempore, ut hominem liberaet a tempore. Venit sanare tumorem nostrum magnus medicus. Ab oriente usque in occidentem genus humanum tamquam magnus iacebat aegrotus, et magnum medicum requirebat: misit primo pueros suos medicus iste, et venit ipse postea, cum a nonnullis desperaretur. Quomodo et medicus quando mittit pueros suos, quasi ad aliquid facile

because it is something easy; but, when the danger is serious, they come. The human race was in great danger, entangled in all vices; The fountain of pride flowed in a special way: and he came to cure it with his example. Be ashamed of being still proud, you man, for whom God humbled himself. Great would have been the humility of God even if he had only been born through you; but he even deigned to die for you. He was on the cross, hidden in man, when the Jews, his persecutors, shook their heads before him and said to him: If he is the Son of God, let him come down from the cross and we will believe in him. He, despite this, preserved his humility, and that is why he did not descend; It was not that he had lost power, but that he taught patience. Think of its effectiveness and its power, and see how easily he who could rise from the grave could descend from the cross. But he did not want to send humility and patience to you without teaching them to you personally; In order to send them to you with words, he had to teach them to you and praise them with his example. Let us look in this regard at the person of the Lord; Let us look at his humility, let us drink the chalice of his humility, let us hold close to him and think of him. It is easy to think of greatness, easy to enjoy honors, easy to listen to flatterers and flatterers. To endure insult, to listen patiently to an insult, to pray for those who insult you: this is the cup of the Lord, this is his banquet. Have you been invited by someone older than you? Think that it is convenient for you to prepare that same thing. faciendum: cum periculum magnum fuerit, ipse venit; sic magno periculo laborabat genus humanum, vitiis omnibus involutum, máxime a superbiae fonte manante: et ideo venit curare ipsam superbiam exemplo suo. Erubesce adhuc superbire, homo, propter quem humiliatus est deus. Multum se humiliasset deus, si tantummodo nasceretur propter te: dignitus est etiam morí pro te. Hic ergo erat in cruz in homine, quando agitabant caput ante cruzem persecutors Iudaei, et dicebant: si filius (568) dei est, descendat de cruz, et credimus ei (cf. Mt 27,40.42). Ule autem servabat humilitatem, ideo non descendebat: non perdiderat potentiam, sed demonstrabat patientiam. Nam ipsum effectum virtutemque eius cogitate, et videte quam facile potuit de crossover descendéré, qui potuit de sepulcro resurregere. Sed tibi humilitas, tibí patientia, si non erat demonstranda, non erat praecipienda: si autem praecipienda erat verbo, demonstranda et commendanda erat exemplo.

Hoc ergo attendamus in domino: humilitatem eius videamus, calícem humilitatis eius bibamus, ad eum nos artemus, eum meditemur. Facile est cogitare sublimitates, facile est honoribus gaudere, facile est assentatoribus et adulatoribus aures praebere. Ferré convicium, patienter [642] audire opprobrium, orare pro contumelioso, hic est domini calix, hoc est convivium domini. Invitatus is a major? Cogita quia talia te oportet praeparare (cf. Prov

6. When the Apostle describes what the bishop should be, he begins by saying: He who desires the episcopate desires a good work. What does this mean? It seems as if he had inflamed everyone with the desire to attain the episcopate. Will those who desire it be better than those who have reservations? Will those who usurp what is due with a certain arrogance be better than those who escape what is due out of fear? By no means; It's not about that; He did not teach that we should aspire to reach the episcopate. Pay attention to what he said, if I can explain what I think. What the Apostle affirms is clear for those who understand it, and dark and dark for the proud and ambitious. What he said is this: He who desires the episcopate desires a good work. Desiring the episcopate is not wanting to be a bishop; It is to desire a good work. But does he want to be a bishop who does not do good work, but rather his own work? This guy does not want the episcopacy. This is what I said shortly before: look for the name, not the reality. —I want to be a bishop. Oh if I were a bishop! "I wish you were!" Are you looking for the name or the reality? If you seek reality, you desire a good work; If you seek the name, you can have it even with bad works, but to your greater torment. "What should I say, then?" That there are bad bishops? By no means; there aren't any. Without a doubt, I dare say that there are no bad bishops, because, if they are bad, they are not bishops. You make me return to the name again, and you tell me: "He is a bishop, because he sits in the chair." —Scarecrows also guard the vines.

7. Among other things, he said: Husband of one wife. But how much better than none? He said how far you could go: not to go beyond one; but much better if you don't have any. Have your children submissive; pata, that, if you have children, they are submissive to you, and do not seek to have them if you do not have them. He encouraged disciplining children, with a view to ruling the house: He who does not know how to command his house, how can he diligently take care of the Church of God? They are words of the Apostle himself. But how will the bishop be childless, if he is a good bishop? In the name of Christ, helped with his grace, your bishop did not want to have carnal children to have spiritual ones. It is up to you to be obsequious to him, to obey him worthily and to serve him with a worthy service; Thus he will have submissive children, many in exchange for a few, celestials in exchange for land, co-heirs instead of heirs. 8. I have spoken of good bishops and bad bishops; I have said what we should be and what we should avoid. But what concerns you, people of God? Something also concerns you. I want you to be built on rock, for a temple to God to be built, for you to become qualified to receive God, for your hope not to fluctuate between doubts, for you to be founded on solid rock. Whatever we are, you have to be safe. Certainly it is good for us to be good bishops who preside as they should and not only in name; this is good for us. Those who are like this are promised a great reward. But, yes

6. Apostolus describe episcopum hoc primo posuit: qui episcopatum desiderat, bonum opus concupiscit (1 Tim 3,1). Quid est hoc? Quasi inflammavit omnes ad desiderandum episcopatum, et meliores erunt ambitores quam verecundi, et meliores erunt arrogantia quadam sibi etiam indebita usurpantes, quam etiam debita timore vitantes? Absit hoc, non est istud: non hoc docuit, ut ambiamus ad episcopatum pervenire. Be quid dixit, intendite, if potuero I will explain what I felt. Apostoli sensus est lucidus intellegentibus, supetbis et ambitoribus caligmosus et obscurus. Hoc ergo apostolus ait: qui episcopatum desiderat, bonum opus concupiscit. Non est desiderare <episcopatum>, episcopatum desiderare: bonum opus concupiscere est. Sed episcopus vult esse, qui non facit bonum opus, sed suum opus? Non episcopatum iste desiderat. Hoc est, quod paulo ante said: nomen quaerit, non rem. Episcopus flew esse: or yes essem episcopus! Utinam esses! Nomen quaeris, an rem? Si rem quaeris, bonum opus concupiscis: si nomen quaeris, potes habere et in opere malo, sed peiore supplicio. Quid ergo dicemus? sunt episcopi mali? Absit, non sunt: ​​prorsus audeo dicere, non sunt episcopi mali; quia si mali, non episcopi. Your iterum ad nomen you revoke me, et say: Episcopus est, nam sedet cathedra. Est et faeneus custos in vinea.

(569) 1. Dixit inter cetera: unius uxoris virum (ib., 2): sed quanto melius nullius? Quousque progrediendum sit, dixit, ut non plus ab una; Be multo melius, if you need one. Filios habentem obsequentes (ib., 4): ut, si habet, obsequentes habeat; non ut conetur habere, si non habet. Disciplinam enim commendavit in filios, propter domum regendam: qui enim domui suae praeesse nescit, quomodo ecclesiae <cdei> diligentiam habebit? (ibid., 5). Ipsius apostoli verba sunt. Et quomodo erit episcopus? Denique episcopus vester in nomine Christi, adiutus gratia Christi, filios carnales habere noluit, ut spirituales habeat. Ad vos pertinet digne e¡ obsequi, digne oboedire, dignified servitio I will serve; et habebit filios obsequentes, pro paucis tam multos, pro terrenis supernos, pro heredibus coheredes. [643] 8. Diximus de episcopis bonis, et de episcopis malis: diximus quod esse debenmus, et quod esse vitemus. Sed quid ad vos, o populus dei? Aliquid et ad vos. Volumus enim vos in petra aedificari, templumdeo surgere, ad capiendum deum idealos fieri, spem vestram non in incerto fluctuare, sed in solido collocare. Qualescumque nos sumus, vos securi esse debentis. Equidem bonum est nobis, ut boni praepositi_ episcopi esse debenamus, non tantum vocemuí, hoc bonum est nobis: talibus enim magna merces promittitur. Sed si non fuerimus tales, sed mali, quod absit, fuerimus, et honores nostros propter nosmetipsos

We are not like that, but—whatever God forbid—bad; If we seek our honor for ourselves, if we neglect the precepts of God without taking your salvation into account, greater torments await us the greater the promised rewards. Far be it from us; pray for us. The higher the place we are, the greater the danger we are in. We think, in fact, about the account we must give of both the honors and the curses that men bestow upon us. Many honor us, many criticize us and many curse us. Those who honor us put us in greater danger than those who curse us. Human honor tickles our pride, while the curses of men exercise us in patience. There I fear falling, here I lay firm foundations. For a certain servant of God tells me: Do not fear the insults of men. The Lord Jesus Christ also says: Blessed are you if men curse you and say, lying, all kinds of evil against you because of me. Well, if someone curses you and tells the truth, it is not that he speaks evil, because he says what he really is. Here we are talking about those who speak badly because they say false things. What did the Lord promise us? Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven. Whoever speaks ill of me increases my reward, while whoever flatters me wants to reduce it. But what shall I say, brothers? Should I desire that you speak ill of me so that my reward may increase? I do not want my reward to increase with mal para quaesierimus, praecepta dei neglexerimus, salutem vestram pro nihilo habuerfcnus, maiora supplicia nos expectant, quam praemia quae promissa sunt. Sed absit a nobis, et orate pro nobis: quanto enim in altiore loco, mucho in maiore periculo sumus. Cogitamus enim quam rationem reddamus de obsequiis hominum, quam de maledictis hominum. Multi nobis obsecuntur, multi nobis detrahunt, nobisque maledicunt. Plus nos faciunt periclitari, qui obsecuntur, quam qui maledicunt: obsequium enim hominum titillat superbiam nostram, maledicta hominum exercent patientiam nostram: alibi timeo lapsum, alibi munio firma<: men>tum. Nam opprobria hominum, ait mihi quidam servorum dei, nolite metuere (Is 51:7). Dicit et dominus Iesus Christus: beati eritis, cum vobis maledixerint homines, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, menientes, propter me (Mt 5,11).

Nam si qui maledicunt, et vera dicunt, non (570) male dicunt, quia vera dicunt; sed male dicunt, qui false dicunt. Nobis autem quid promisit dominus? Gaudete et exultate, quia merces vestra copiosa est in caelis (ib., 12). Auget mercedem meam maledicus meus: minuere vult mercedem meam adulator meus. Sed quid dicam, brothers? Ut augeatur merces nostra, optere debenmus, ut maledici sitis? Nolumus malo vestro nostram augeri mercedem. Be-
The episcopal ministry

you. Speak well, obey; Even if I remain in danger, you will not suffer detriment. And what happens if a town gets a bad bishop? The Lord and Bishop of bishops has given you assurances, so that your hope does not rest on a man. Behold, as bishop, I speak to you in the name of the Lord; what I am, I do not know; how much less do you know! In a way, I can sense what I will be like in an hour; but how can I know what I will be from now on? Peter boasted, and stood naked before him; He did not know that he was sick, but it was not hidden from the doctor. He said, he boasted and even dared to promise: I will go with you until death. I will give my life for you. And that doctor, taking the pulse of the vein of his heart, said: Are you going to give your life for me? Truly I tell you: before the rooster crows, you will have denied me three times. 9. So, then, may the Lord grant me, with the help of your prayers, to be and persevere, being until the end what all of you who love me well want me to be and what he wants me to be who called me and commanded me; Let him help me to fulfill what he commanded me. But whatever the bishop is, your hope must not rest on him. I put aside my person; I speak to you as a bishop: I want you to be a cause of joy for me, not of swelling. I can congratulate absolutely no one who I find placing hope in me; needs correction, not confirmation; It has to change, not stay where it is. If I cannot warn you, it causes me pain; On the other hand, if I can do it, I already nedici estote, obsequimini; nos periclitemur, et vos non deminuamini. Quid ergo, si populus incurrat in episcopum malum? Dominus et episcopus episcoporum fecit securum, ne spes vestra in homine sit. Ecce in nomine domini episcopus vobis loquor: qualis sim ego, nescio: quanto minus vos? Quid enim sim ad horam, possum utcumque will feel: quid quandoque futurus, unde scio? Quomodo praesumsit Petras, et demonstratus est sibi Petras; [644] aeger se nesciebat, sed medicum non latebat. Dixit, praesumsit, ausus est polliceri: tecum usque ad mortem (Lk 22:33). Animam meam pro te ponam (lo 13.37). Et ille mediais venam cordis inspiciens: animam tuam, inquit, pro me ponis? Amen dico tibi, prius quam gallus cantet, ter me negabis (ib., 38). 9.

Dominus itaque praestet, a<d>iuvantibus nos orationibus vestris, et hoc nos esse, et hoc usque in finem perseverare, quod nos vultis esse, omnes qui nobis bene vultis, et quod nos vult esse ille, qui nos vocavit et iussit: adiuvet nos implere quod iussit. Sed qualescumque sumus, spes vestra non sit in nobis. Mihi derogo, ut episcopus hoc loquar: gaudere de vobis voló, non inflari. Omnino quemeumque invenero spemponentem in me, non illi gratulor: emendandus est, non firmandus: mutandus est, non stabilendus. Si monere non possum,
The episcopal ministry

No. Now I speak in the name of Christ to you, people of God; I speak to you in the Church of God, I speak to you, any servant of God: your hope is not in us, it is not in men. If we are good, we are servants; If we are bad, we are servants; but, yes we are good, we are faithful servants, servants of truth. Pay attention to what we serve you: if you are hungry and do not want to be ungrateful, observe from which pantry the delicacies are taken. Don't worry about the plate on which what you are eager to eat is put. In the great house of the father of the family there is not only gold and silver tableware, but also clay. There are silver, gold and clay vessels. You only see if he has bread and whose bread it is and who gives it to the person who serves it. Look at him of whom I am speaking, the giver of this bread that is served to you. The same is the bread: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. So, then, we serve you Christ in his place; we serve you, but under his orders; so that he may come to you and be the judge of our service. If, for example, the bishop is a thief, he must never tell you from this chair: "Steal"; He will not tell you anything other than this: "Do not steal." This he receives from the Lord's pantry. If he wanted to tell you anything beyond this, you would reject him and say: “This is not from the Lord's larder; "They are your things." Whoever speaks lies, speaks about his own. Tell yourself, then, according to God: "Do not steal, do not be an adulterer, do not commit murder"; tell it to yourself according to God, so that you feel fear, so that you do not become proud, so that you turn away from

love the world, so that you put your hope in the Lord. That's what God has to tell you. If he personally doesn't comply, what is your business? Christ is the Lord your God, and he gave you assurance by saying: The scribes and the Pharisees - the image of those who preside - have sat in the seat of Moses; Do what they tell you, but do not do what they do, for they say, but do not do. What should you reply to these words? What are you going to excuse yourself with at the judgment of Christ? Perhaps you say: "I did wrong because I saw that my bishop was not living well." You will be answered: “You chose a companion with whom to condemn yourself, not with whom to free you. You imitated someone who lived badly; Why did you prefer to imitate him rather than listen to me, who spoke through his mouth? Did I not tell you in my Gospel that, when you saw that those who preside do wrong, you should do what they tell you, but not do what they do? If you had listened to me through them, you would not have perished through them. 10. Therefore, if even the bad can say good things, let us now reply to Christ and say to him with the intention of learning, not of despising or annoying him: "Lord, if the bad can say good things - which is why you warned us and commanded us to act as they told us, but not to do what they do -; If, then, evil people can say good things, how do you say in another place: Hypocrites, how can you speak good things when you are evil? Pay attention to this complicated matter until it is resolved with their help. Again I propose the question. Christ says: "Do what they tell you, but do not do what they tell you."

doleo; si autem monere possum, iam non doleo. Sicut moda in nomine Christi loquor populo dei, loquor in ecclesia dei, loquor qualiscumque servus dei: spes vestra non sit in nobis, spes vestra non sit in hominibus. Boni sumus, ministeri sumus; mali sumus, minister sumus. Be good, fideles ministers, I will see ministers. Quod ministramus, attendite: si esuritis, et ingrati esse non vultis, de cuius cellario proferatur advertite. In quali vasculo tibi ponatur, quod tu avidus es comedere, non ad te pertineat. In magna domo patris familias, non tantum vasa áurea (571) et argentea, sed et fictilia sunt (2 Tim 2,20). Argenteum vas est, aureum vas est, fictile est: tu utrum habeat panem attende, et cuius iste sit pañis, quo donor ministretur. Ipsum advertite, de quo loquor, quo donor minister tur hic pañis. Ipse est pañis: ego sum pañis vivus, qui de cáelo descendí (lo 6,51). Ministramus ergo vobis Christum pro Christo, ipsum sub ipso; ut ipse ad vos perveniat, ipse sit iudex ministerii nostri. Nam si fur est episcopus, numquam tibi dicturus est de exedra ista: Fac furtum; sed non est tibi dicturus nisi: Noli faceré furtum. Hoc enim accipit de cellario domini. Si aliquid aliud dicere voluerit, respuis illum, et dicis: Non est hoc de cellario domini, tua mihi dicis: Qui loquitur mendacium, de suo loquitur (ib., 8,44). Dicat ergo tibi secundum deum: Ne furtum facías, ne adulterium, ne homicidium; dicat tibi secundum deum, ut timeas, ut non extollaris, ut a

saeculi amore avertaris, ut spem tuam in domino ponas. Haec tibi dicat secundum deum. Ipse si non facit, quid ad te? [645] Dominus deus tuus Christus est, securum te fecit. Scribae, inquit, et pharisaei in imagine praepositorum sederunt cathedram Moysi: quae dicunt, jache: quae autem faciunt, faceré nolite; dicunt enim, et non faciunt (Mt 23,3). What ad hoc dicturus is? Where are you in judicio Christi excusaturus? Dicturus is: Ideo feci male, quia vidi episcopum meum non vivere bene. Respondetur tibi: Elegisti tibi, cum quo damneris, non cum quo libereris. Ipsum imitatus is male vivostem: quare ipsum imitatus es potius, et non me audisti per ipsum? Ego enim tibi in gospel meo non dixeram, ut, quando vides praepositos malo, quae dicunt facías, quae autem faciunt non facias? Me per illos audires, et per ipsos non perires. 10. Si ergo et mali possunt dicere bona, et nunc responderamus Christo, et dicamus, discendi causa, non contemnendi aut exagitandi: Domine, si mali possunt dicere bona — unde ammonuisti, et praecepisti dices: Quae dicunt, facite, quae autem faciunt faceré nolite — si mali ergo possunt dicere bona, quomodo alio loco say: hypocritae, non potestis bona loqui, cum sitis mali? (ib., 12,34). Attendite rem ligatam, (572) quousque illius adiutorio cernatis solutam. Iterum propono quaestionem. Christus dicit: Quae dicunt, facite: quae autem faciunt, faceré
The episcopal ministry

They do, well they say, but they don't do. Why else but because they speak good and do evil? Consequently, we should do what they tell us and we should not do what they do. But in another place he says: Are grapes gathered from brambles, or figs from thistles? Every tree is known by its fruit. What to say then? How are we to obey? How are we to understand it? Behold, they are thistles, they are brambles. Do it. You command me to gather grapes from the brambles; In one place you command me and in another you forbid me, how should I obey? Listen, understand. When I say, "Do as they tell you, but do not do as they do," notice what I said before: They have sat in the seat of Moses. That's what I said. When they say good things, they are not saying them, but the chair of Moses. He speaks of teaching instead of doctrine; It is not that the teaching speaks, but the doctrine of Moses, which is present in his memory, but not in his works. On the other hand, when they speak, that is, when they talk about their own thing, what do they hear? How can you speak good things, when you are evil? Listen to another similarity. Do not pick grapes from brambles, for brambles can never bear grapes. But have you not noticed how, as the vine shoot grows, it reaches the hedge and mixes with the brambles, and produces its fruit among them and the clusters hang from them? You are hungry, you pass by and see the bunch hanging from the brambles; You don't take it. You are hungry and you want to catch it; pick it up; stretch out your hand carefully and cautiously; avoid the thorns, pick the fruit. You have to do the same when a bad or nolite man: dicunt enim, et non faciunt. Quid ergo, nisi quia dicunt bona, et faciunt mala? Ideoque quae dicunt, debenmus faceré; quae faciunt non debenmus faceré. Alio loco: numquid colliguiit of spisis grapes, aut of tribulis ficus? (ib., 7,16). Omnis arbor ex fructu cognoscitur (Luke 6:44). Quid ergo, quomodo obtemperabimus? Whatmodo intellegemus? Ecce vepres sunt, spinae sunt. Facite. Iubes me colligere uvam de spinis: alibi iubes, alibi veins: quomodo obtemperabo? Audi, intelligence. Cum dico: Quae dicunt facite, quae autem faciunt faceré nolite, attende prius quid dicam: Cathedram Moysi sederunt, dixi. Quando dicunt bona, non ipsi dicunt, sed cathedra Moysi. Cathedram pro doctrina posuit: non quia cathedra loquitur, sed doctrina Moysi: in memoria eorum est, in operibus non est.

Quando autem ipsi dicunt, quando ipsi loquuntur, hoc est, quando de suo loquuntur, quid audiunt? quomodo potestis bona loqui, cum sitis mali? (cf. Mt 12:34). Nam alliam similarityinem attendite. De spinis nolite uvam carpere: non enim potest aliquando uva nasci de spinis. Sed non attendistis palmitem vitis crescendo iré in sepem, et involvere se in spinis, et Ínter [646] spinas germen promere, botrum summittere? Esuris, et transís, et vides botrum pendentem inter spinas: non facis, non carpís. Esuris, et carpere vis: carpe, manum diligenter et caute extende: spinas cave, fructum carpe. Sic etiam when

Terrible presents to you the doctrine of Christ: listen to it, take it, do not despise it. If he is a bad man, the thorns are himself; If it says good things, it is a cluster hanging from the brambles, but not produced by them. So if you're hungry, pick it up, but keep an eye out for the thorns. In fact, if you begin to imitate his works while listening to him willingly, you have stretched out your hand without caution; you encountered the thorns before reaching the fruit. You come out wounded, torn; The fruit of the grape no longer benefits you, but the thorns, which have their own roots, are a hindrance to you. To avoid making a mistake, look where you pick the fruit: there is the branch. Direct your gaze to the branch and notice that it belongs to the vine, that it comes out of the vine, that it grows from the vine, but that it ends up in the middle of the brambles. Should the vine remove its branches? In the same way, the doctrine of Christ, growing and developing, mixed with good trees and bad brambles. The good ones preach it and the bad ones preach it. You observe where the fruit comes from, where what nourishes you originates and where what stings you originates; In sight both things are mixed, but the root separates them. 11. Do the tablets of our Lord, from whom he bought us, remove all cause for dispute? You say that the Church of Christ is found in Africans and in Africa; I say that the Church of Christ is spread throughout all peoples. This is the thing; This is the origin of the dispute between the brothers. You litigate in favor of one party; You litigate to continue in that part. I contradict you so that you possess the entirety. Understand that it is a lawsuit that seeks harmony, a lawsuit of charity. I do not say to you: «You have been defeated; retreat." From the beginning, the dividers of the inheritance displeased our Lord Jesus Christ. In fact, one of the crowd said to him who was preaching the truth to the people: Lord, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me. And the Lord did not want to confirm the division, because he had come to seek unity, as we have just heard now in the Gospel about unity: I have other sheep that are not of this fold; It is convenient that he bring them, so that there may be one flock and one shepherd. The Lord, then, who loved unity and hated division, said to that man: Tell me, O man, who has made me a divider of the inheritance among you? I tell you: Beware of all greed. He did not want to be a divider of the inheritance; He had come to gather unity and make all lands a single inheritance. Read your inheritance documents; read as he had begun to say. Theme: Jesus Christ, man and God and head of the Church. Place: Cartago, in the Restituta basilica. Date: December 12 of the year 418 or 419. 1. As far as I have been able to glimpse in the sacred pages, brothers, our Lord Jesus Christ is considered and named in three ways when he is announced both in the law and the prophets and in the apostolic letters or in the facts worthy of faith that we know from the Gospel. The first of them, prior to the assumption of the flesh, is as God dominum meum interpello, ego interpello Christum contra fratrem meum. Non quomodo ill; non ei dico: domine, <Ldic~> fratri meo dividedat mecum hereditatem; sed dico: Domine, dic fratri meo teneat mecum hereditatem. Ergo quod interpellavi dominum contra fratrem meum, non est contra fratrem meum, sed pro fratre meo: nolo illum exheredem, nolo solus possidere; scio enim quia quod possideo non fiet angustum, si multi mecum [649] possideant. Quod possideo, caritas vocatur, quae numerous possessore amplius dilatatur.
DE EO QUOD CHRISTUS TRIBUS MODIS IN SCRIPTURIS INTELLEGITUR; AGAINST ARIANS HABITUS

CAPUT I.—1. Christus in Scripturis dictus tribus modis.—Dominus noster Iesus Christus, fratres, quantum animadvertere potuimus paginas sanctas, tribus modis intellegitur et nominatur, quando praedicatur, sive per Legem et Prophetas, sive per Apostolic Epistles, sive per fidem rerum gestarum, quas in Evangelio cognoscimus. Primus modus est, Perhaps, this sermon began with a commentary, now lost, on Psalm 21, according to C. Lambot, who does not exclude that it may have been retouched by Saint Caesarius.

and in reference to divinity, equal and coeternal to that of the Father. The second refers to the moment in which he has already assumed the flesh, as soon as it is read and understood that the same one who is God is man and the same one who is man is God, according to a certain property of his excellency, by which he is not equated with other men, but is mediator and head of the Church. The third way is what we call in a certain way the total Christ, in the fullness of his Church, that is, head and body, according to the fullness of a certain perfect man, of whom each one of us in particular is a member. Such is what is proclaimed to believers and offered as knowable to the wise. In such a short space of time it is not possible for me to remember or explain the numerous testimonies of Scripture with which to prove the three ways mentioned; but I can't leave everything without trying. Thus, by bringing to mind some of those testimonies, you yourselves can see and find in the Scriptures the rest, which the pressure of time does not allow me to mention. 2. The first way of indicating our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, through whom all things were made, refers to that outstanding and dazzling text of the gospel according to Saint John: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God; she was at the beginning with God; everything was done by her, and without her nothing was done. All that was made was life in her; secundum Deum et divinitatem illam Patri coaequalem atque coaeternam ante assumptionem carnis. Alter modus est, cum assumpta carne iam idem Deus qui homo, et idem homo qui Deus, secundum quamdam suae excellentiae proprietatem, qua non ceteris coaequatur hominibus, sed est mediator et caput Ecclesiae, esse legitur et intellegitur. Tertius modus est quodam moda totus Christus, in plenitudine Ecclesiae, id est, caput et corpus, secundum plenitudinem perfecti cuiusdam viri, in quo viro singuli membra sumus. Quod credentibus praedicatur, et prudentibus agnoscibile offertur. Non omnia testimonia Scripturarum tam fines angusto tempore sive recolere sive explicae possumus, quibus omnia tria ista genera probemus: sed tamen non omnia possumus improbata relinquere, ut quibusdam commemoratis testimoniis, cetera quae commemorare non sinimur propter anxieties temporis, per vos ipsos iam observare in Scripturis et invenire possitis. CAPUT II.—2. Primus modus quo Christus praedicatur ut Deus.

Verbi similarity.—Ad primum ergo modum insinuandi Domini nostri Iesu Christi Salvatoris, unici Filii Dei, per quem facta sunt omnia, pertinet illud quod nobilissimum et praeclarissimum est in Gospel secundum Ioannem: In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum; hoc erat in principle apud Deum: omnia per ipsum facta sunt, et sine ipso factum est nihil. Quod iactum est.

and life was the light of men, and the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not accept it. These words cause admiration and amazement and that must be embraced before even understanding them. If any food is presented to your mouth, one receives a part of it and another another: the same food reaches all, but not all the whole food. In the same way my words are now presented to your ears as food and drink, but this food and drink reaches everyone in its entirety. Or is it that, when I speak, one stays with one syllable and another with another? Or one with one word and another with another? If that were the case, I would have to say as many words as there are men I am seeing, so that each one gets at least one. It is certainly very probable that I say more words than I see men; but they all reach everyone. The word, then, of man is not divided into syllables so that everyone can hear it; And is the Word of God going to have to be divided into pieces so that it is everywhere? Ea enim quae dixi, dicta sunt [1495] ante assumptam carnem. Nunc autem audi illud quod moda praedicat Scriptura: Verbum, inquit, caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (lo 1,14). Ut enim illud videam, hic mecum agitur; ut purget ad illud contemplandum, infirmitati meae ipse subvenit. Suscipando de natura humano ipsam naturam humanora, factus est homo. human, became man. With the donkey of his flesh he approached the one who lay wounded on the road to shape and nourish our little faith with the sacrament of his incarnation, to purify the understanding so that it sees what it never lost through what it assumed. Indeed, he began to be a man, he did not stop being God. This, then, is what is proclaimed of our Lord Jesus Christ as mediator, as head of the Church: that God is man and man is God, since John says: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. 4. Listen to one thing and another in that very well-known text of the apostle Paul: Who, existing in the form of God, says, did not consider it a plunder to be equal to God. This is equivalent to: In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. How did the Apostle say: Did he not consider it a plunder to be equal to God, if he is not equal to God? If, on the other hand, it is God the Father, but not him, how is it the same? So, where John says: The Word was God, Paul says: He did not consider it a plunder to be equal with God. And where that one: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, this one: But he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant. Pay attention: inasmuch as he became man, inasmuch as the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, in that very sense he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant. How did he become overwhelmed? Not in a way that would lose divinity,

but by putting on humanity, showing men what he was not before he was a man. Thus, he annihilated himself by making himself visible, that is, hiding the dignity of his majesty and showing the flesh, the clothing of his humanity. So he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, without losing the form of God. In fact, when speaking of the form of God, he did not say "took", but: Existing in the form of God, he did not consider it a plunder to be equal to God; but when he came to the form of a servant, he said, Taking the form of a servant. Therefore, inasmuch as he emptied himself, he is mediator and head of the Church, through whom we are reconciled to God through the sacrament of his humility 2, passion, resurrection, ascension and future judgment, so that those two future things may be heard, although God has spoken only once. When will both things be heard? When he repays each one according to his own works. 5. Maintaining this, then, do not be surprised by human issues, which, according to the Apostle's words, spread like cancer; but guard your ears and the virginity of your mind, as betrothed by the bridegroom's friend to one man to show you Christ as a chaste virgin. Your virginity, then, is in the mind. Corporal virginity is possessed by few in the Church; virginity of mind must be found in all the faithful. The serpent wants to profane this virginity, of which the Apostle himself says:

Christus utroque moda commendatus ab Apostólo.—Audite iam utrumque in illo notissimo capitulo apostoli Pauli: Qui cum in forma Dei esset, inquit, non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo (Phil 2,6). Si autem Pater Deus, ille non Deus, quomodo aequalis? Ubi ergo ille ait: Deus erat Verbum; ibi iste: Non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo. ut indueret humanitatem, apparens hominibus quod non erat, antequam homo esset. Sic apparendo se exinanivit, id est, reservans dignitatem maestatis, et offerens carnem indumentum humanitatis. The Arian problem troubled the weak brothers of the Church; but, with the mercy of the Lord, the Catholic faith triumphed. With a certain promise of science, it seeks to expel Christians from the paradise of the Church so as not to allow them to return to the paradise from which the first man was expelled. 6. Be attentive, brothers. What happened in that paradise, the same thing happens in the Church. Let no one keep us from this paradise. impunity, as he also promised there when saying: Are you going to die? In order for Christians to live badly, he suggests things like this: "Is God, he says, going to lose everyone?" Are you going to condemn them all by chance? God says: “I will condemn them, I will forgive those who change; If they change their actions, I change my threats. The serpent is therefore the one who murmurs and mutters, saying: “See where it is written: The Father is greater than I; And you say that he is equal to the Father? The Evening Sacrifice and the Incarnate Word
Theme: The evening sacrifice and, then, the incarnate Word (Ps 140,2; Jn 1,1-18). Location: Unknown. Date: Unknown.

1. My sermon is going to be about the evening sacrifice. Indeed, singing we have prayed and praying we have sung: Let my prayer rise as incense in your presence; The lifting up of my hands is my evening sacrifice. In prayer we see meaning in the man, and in the outstretched hands, the cross. It is, then, the sign that we carry on our foreheads, the sign by which we have been saved. A sign that was the object of ridicule, to be later honored; object of contempt, to be later glorified. God allows himself to be seen so that man can supplicate him and hides so that man can die. Well, if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord. This sacrifice, in which the priest is at the same time a victim, redeemed us with the shed blood of the Creator. Not only did he create us with blood, but he redeemed us with blood. He created us the Word that existed in the beginning, the Word that was with God, and the Word was God. By it we were created. There are kinds of worlds, as there are kinds of houses; The building is called a house and its inhabitants are called a house. The house is the building, as when we say: «He built a great house; "he built a very beautiful house." The house is the inhabitants, as when we say: «Good house: bless the Lord; "bad house: may God forgive it." Thus the world was made by her: both the habitation and the inhabitants; and the world did not know her, that is, the inhabitants. 4. She came to her own house, and her people did not receive her. Why did he come, then? Didn't she know beforehand that her people were not going to receive her? Hear why she came: But to all who received her. His own did not receive it and his own received it; The world did not believe and everyone believed. In the same way we say: "The whole tree is full of leaves." Is it that, perhaps, there is no room left for the fruit? Both things can be stated

Potestas data ut efficiamur filii Dei.—Erige cor, genus humanum, breathe in aura vitae et securissimae libertatis. What are you listening to? quid tibi promittitur? Dedit eis potestatem. men and became children of God. He descended to what he was not, because he was something else; He elevated you to what you were not, since you were another. Raise, therefore, your hope. Topic: Susana and José, models of chastity. Place: Carthage. Date: May of the year 397. 1. The divine readings and the holy oracles of God that have just sounded in our ears must nest in our minds. Do not fly away and leave, nor stop and leave later, but rather generate something. For if the bird found a house and the turtledove a nest in which to place its chicks, how much more so the bird, which is the Word of God, and the turtledove, which is his mercy! We listen to the story about Susana. Let marital purity be built; Let it rest on such firm foundations and surround it with such a wall that, in addition to repelling those who stalk it, it leaves false witnesses convicted. That woman was still chaste, who would have died if the one who saw what was hidden from the judges had not been present. The words he spoke in paradise, that is, in his garden, were written; words that no man heard, except those two who stalked the modesty of another's woman and who plotted false testimony against anyone who offered resistance to them. Only they heard what was said there: Anxiety surrounds me everywhere; Well, if I do such a thing, death comes to me; If, on the contrary, I don't do it, I won't escape your SERMO
[RB 66(1956)28] (PL 39,1505) TRACTATUS DE SUSANA ET IOSEPH

1. Diuinae lectiones et sancta oracula dei, quae insonuerunt auribus nostris, nidum faciant in mentibus nostris. Non uolent et transeant, aut sedeant et discedant, sed aliquid pariant. Nam si passer inuenit sibi domum, et turtur nidum ubi reponat pullos suos (Ps 83,4), quanto magis passer uerbum dei, et turtur misericordia dei! Audiuimus de Susanna lectionem. Aedificetur pudicitia coniugalis, et also firm foundation innitatur walloque ualletur, ut et insidiantes repellat, et false testes conuincat. Remanserat casta mulier moritura, nisi adesset qui uidebat quod iudicantes latebat. Conscripta sunt uerba eius, quae habuit in paradiso (Dan 13:7), hoc est in uiridario suo, quae uerba nullus hominum audiuit, nisi soli duo, qui pozori uxoris alienae insidiabantur, et reluctanti falsum testimonium meditabantur. lili soli audierunt quod dictum est: Angustiae mihi undique. Si enim hoc fecero, mors mihi est; si autem non fecero, non effugiam manus uestras. Melius est autem mihi manus

hands. But it is better for me not to escape from your hands than to sin in the presence of the Lord. He despised what he heard because he feared those who he did not see, but in whose divine eyes he was very present. For it does not follow from the fact that she did not see God that she was not seen by him. God saw what he was building, contemplated his work, inhabited his temple; there he was; He was the one who responded to those who snared him. In fact, if the giver of chastity had abandoned it, chastity would have foundered. He says, then: Anxiety surrounds me everywhere. But she was waiting for the one who was going to save her from the timidity and the storm of false witnesses like destructive winds. Chastity was not shipwrecked in the midst of those winds and waves because the Lord took the helm. There were screams, people came, came closer and took the case to court. Susana's house had believed what the elders, full of falsehood, said against their lady. And, although their previous life, immaculate and flawless, could provide valid testimony in favor of their chastity, it seemed against religion to them not to give credit to the elderly. Such a thing had never been said about Susana. They were false witnesses, but only God knew. One thing was what he believed to be his house and another was what the Lord saw. But what the Lord saw was unknown to men. It seemed that the elders had to be believed. Consequently, he had to die. But if the flesh died, chastity would receive its crown. The Lord came to the aid of those who begged him. He listened to the one he knew well; He did not let the one he had helped die so that she would not commit adultery.

The Lord raised up the holy spirit of Daniel, still young in his age, but robust in his piety. As the prophetic spirit dwelt in him, he immediately realized the deception of those wicked elders. But we had to see how he expressed to others what he knew. He said: They are false witnesses. Go back to court. He knew that they were false, to whom the prophetic spirit had revealed them. Those who ignored it had to be taught. Therefore, if the judges are to be instructed, without a doubt the witnesses must be convicted of falsehood. To do this, considering the falsity of their testimony, of which he was already aware, he ordered that they be separated from each other. He asked each one separately. The two may have been possessed by the same passion, but they could not think of a single answer. One was asked under which tree he had surprised the adulterers. He answered: Under a mastic tree. The same question was asked to the other, who answered: Under an oak tree. The disagreement between the witnesses revealed the truth and freed chastity. 2. As I already said, brothers, chastity would have been liberated and crowned even if the flesh, which would someday have to die, had died by that judgment. In fact, we all have to die, and whoever wants to escape death does not strive to eliminate it, but to postpone it. No one is free from this debt that we have brought from Adam; We all have to pay it. We do not want to die, but the creditor of this debt does not guarantee that this will not be the case; What we ask for is a delay.

ours are not euadere, quam in conspectu dei peccare (ib., 22). Contemnebat quod audiebat, quia timebat quem non uidebat, cuius tamen diuinis oculis erat ipsa conspicua. Ñeque enim quomodo illa deum non uidebat, sic non uidebatur a deo. Videbat deus quod aedificabat, inspiciebat opus suum, habitab templum suum: ibi erat, ipse insidiantibus responderbat. Nam si castitatis dator deseruisset, castitas interisset. Ait ergo: Angustiae mihi undique. Be expectabat eum, qui eam saluam faceret a pusillanimitate, et tempestate falserum testium, tamquam uentorum malotum (cf. Ps 55,9). In illis tamen uentis et fluctibus naufragium castitas non fecit, quia dominus gubernauit. Clamatum est, uentum est, processum est, peruenit causa ad iudicium. Domus Susannae crediderat contra dominam senioribus falsis. Et quamuis ante acta illaesa et immaculata [29] uita idoneum uideretur pudicitiae testimoníum perhibere, illis autem irreligiosum uidebatur senioribus non credere. Nullus talis sermo umquam sonuerat de Susanna. lili ergo falsi testes, sed noti deo. Aliud credebat domus, aliud uidebat dominus. Sed quod uidebat dominus, nomines nesciebant. Senioribus credi uidebatur. Ergo moriendum erat. Be yes expensive moreretur, castitas coronaretur. Adfuit dominus precanti. Exaudiuit quam nouerat. Non deseruit ne moreretur, cui subuenit ne

adulteraretur. Excitauit dominus spiritum (1506) sanctum (Dan 13:45) Danihelis adhuc nouelli aetate, sed robusti pietate. Quia ergo erat in eo propheticus spiritus, continuo nequissimorum seniorum uidit fallaciam. Sed quod Ule intuebatur, prouidendum erat quomodo ceteris monstraretur. Falsi, inquit, testes sunt. Redite in iudicium (ib., 49). Sed quod falsi essent, Ule nouerat, cui propheticus spiritus reuelauerat. Docendi werent qui nesciebant. Ergo si iudices docendi, testes procul dubio conuincendi. Conuincens ergo eos, intendens falsitatem testimonii, quam ipse iam nouerat, iussit eos ab inuicem separi. Single interrogation. Unam enim concupiscentiam habere ambo potuerunt, sed unum consilium meditari non potuerunt. Interrogatus est unus, sub qua arbore comprehendisset adulterers. Respondit: Sub mastic. Interrogatus est alius. Respondit: Sub I did (ib., 54.58). Dissonantia testimonyrum patefecit ueritatem, liberauit castitatem. 2. Et castitas quidem, fratres, sicut iam dixi, liberaretur et coronaretur, etiam si caro, quandoque moritura, illo iudicio moreretur. Morituri enim sumus omnes, nec agit quisquam qui cupit euadere, ut mortem auferat, sed ut differat. Debitum hoc omnes tenet. Hoc omnes reddituri sumus, quod of Adam traximus. Et quod mori nolumus, ab exactore huius debiti non securitas datur, sed dilatio postulatur. Susanna ergo

So Susanna, a pious woman and chaste wife, also had to die sometime. And if that "sometime" had been then, what would have harmed chastity? The body would be locked in the tomb, while chastity would return to God to be crowned by him. Do you think, brothers, that there is great gain in the fact that false witnesses do not prevail over the innocent? The gain is not great if false testimony does not prevail against the innocent. It would be if he had not prevailed against the Lord. Jesus Christ our Lord himself was crucified by the tongue of false witnesses. But even the same false witnesses prevailed momentarily. How did they harm the one who was going to resurrect? Thus, then, the Lord our God, by his example in his flesh, in his weakness and in the form of a servant that he took to free the servant, to search for the fugitive, to redeem the captive, to release the chained, to make a servant a brother..., coming for this purpose in the form of a servant, offered the servant an example so that he should not fear false witnesses even when they are given credit. They can certainly create a bad reputation, but they cannot kill conscience. Three men were released from the burning fiery furnace. Their God helped them, they walked unharmed among the flames that burned around them and did not burn them, and as they walked they sang the praises of God, and they came out as unharmed as they had entered. Therefore, their God assisted them. Did the God of the Maccabees abandon them?

Those were free from the fire, these burned instantly. Both were put to the test; These saw their flesh consumed, those emerged unharmed: but both were crowned. When the three men emerged unharmed from the flames, Nebuchadnezzar was granted faith in their God. He who was able to deliver them manifestly was also able to crown them secretly. But, if he had crowned them secretly, he would not have freed the king who had tormented them. Health in the bodies of the former became health for the soul of the latter. Those, praising God, escaped from the flames, but those present; He, believing in God, escaped the flames, but the eternal ones. Therefore, more was granted to him than to them. Antiochus, on the other hand, the torturer of the Maccabees, was not worthy of being granted such gifts. That is why he exulted with joy seeing them consumed by fire and torments; but whoever humbles himself will be exalted. 3. The same one who freed Susanna, a chaste woman and faithful wife, from the false testimony of the elders, also freed the virgin Mary from the false suspicion of her husband. That virgin to whom no man had approached was found in state. Her womb had enlarged with the child, but the virginal integrity remained. He had conceived, through faith, the sower of the same faith. He had welcomed the Lord into his body; he had not allowed his body to be violated. But the husband, a man after all, became suspicious. He believed that what he knew did not come from himself came from somewhere else, and that "from somewhere else" he suspected was adultery. an angel

religious mulier et púdica coniux erat utique quandoque [30] mount. Et ipsum 'quandoque' si tune esset, pudicitiae quid obesset? Caro conderetur sepulchro, castitas redderetur deo, coronaretur a deo. Putatis enim, fratres, tamquam ad magnum meritum pertinere, si falsi testes non praeualeant super innocentem? Non est magnum meritum, si non praeualeat falsum testimonium aduersus innocentem. Magnum meritum esset, si aduersus dominum non praeualuisset. Ipse dominus noster Iesus Christus per linguam falserum testium est crucifixus. Sed etiam ipsi quidem falsi testes ad horam praeualuerunt, resurrecturo quid nocuerunt? Example itaque suo dominus deus noster in carne sua, in infirmitate sua, et in forma serui, quam suscepit ad liberandum seruum, ad quaerendum fugitiuum, ad redknendum captiuum, soluendum uinctum, faciendum de seruo fratrem: ad hoc ueniens in forma serui demonstrauit seruo exemplum, ne false tests perhorrescat, et cum creduntur, non timeat. Possunt enim faceré malam famem, non possunt interficere conscientiam. Liberati sunt tres uiri de camino ignis ardentis (cf. Dan 3:24). Adfuit deus eorum, deambulauerunt inter ignes innoxios, circum ardentes et non urentes, et in ipsa deambulatione laudes dixerunt deo, et illaesi sicut missi fuerant euaserunt (cf. ibid., 51). Adfuit ergo deus eorum. Numquid defuit deus Macchabaeorum? (cf. 2 Mach 7). lili euaserunt,

illi mox arserunt: utrique tentati. Hii carne consumpti, My carne illaesi: utrique coronati. Ut euaderent flammas tres uiri, Nebuchodonosor praestitum est ut crederet in deum eorum. Nam qui eos potuit in manifesto liberare, potuit et in hidden coronare. Sed (1507) si illos in hidden coronasset, regem qui saeuierat non liberasset. Salus corporis illorum, salus animae facta est illius. lili deum laudando euaserunt, sed praesentes ignes. Ule credendo in deum euasit, sed aeternas gehennas. Plus ergo illi quam illis praestitum est. Antiochus autem non erat dignus cui talia praestarentur a quo Macchabaei torque[31]bantur. Ideo illis igne tormentisque consumptis exsultauit, sed qui se exaltat humiliabitur (Luke 18:14). 3. Qui ergo liberauit Susannam mulierem castam, coniugem fidam, a false testimony seniorum, ipse liberauit et uirginem Mariam a false suspicione mariti sui. Inuenta est ergo uirgo illa praegnans, ad quam uir non accesserat (cf. Mt 1:19). Uterus quidem fetu intumuerat, sed uirginalis integritas manserat. Seminatorem fidei fide conceperat. Dominum in suum corpus assumpserat, non eius corpus uiolari permiserat. Marito tamen tamquam homini uenit in suspicionem.
