of his mind against himself if he fears that: It is fitting that we appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that there each one may receive according to the works done through the body, good or bad. Appear before yourself so that what was said does not happen to you later. God, in effect, threatens the sinner, saying: I will accuse you and bring you before your own eyes. Thus, the heart being constituted as a tribunal, the thought presents itself as an accuser; conscience, as witness, and fear, as executioner. Run from there, through tears, like the blood of the soul that confesses. Finally, let the mind itself pronounce such a sentence that man considers himself unworthy to participate in the body and blood of the Lord. Thus, whoever fears that the final sentence of the supreme judge will separate him from the kingdom of heaven, will be separated for some time from the sacrament of heavenly peace through ecclesiastical discipline. Represent before your eyes the image of the future judgment; In this way, when others approach the altar of God to which he does not approach, think how much there is to fear such a penalty, by which, while some receive eternal life, others are precipitated to eternal death. Even many criminals can access this altar that now appears placed in the church on earth, exposed to earthly eyes, to celebrate the divine mysteries, since God exercises his patience at this time, to apply his severity in the future. The ignorant also agree, since the patience of God leads them to penitence. Those, on the other hand, to the extent of the hardness of their hearts and their impenitence, store up anger for the day of wrath and revelationsi timet illud quod oportet they exhibit us before the tribunal Cbristi, ut illic' recipiat unusquisque quod per Corpus gessit, sive bonum, sive malum (2 Cor 5,10). Constituat se ante faciem suam, ne hoc ei postea fiat. Nam minatur hoc Deus peccatori, they say: Arguam te, et statuam te ante faciem tuam (Ps 49,21). Atque ita constituto in corde iudicio, adsit accusatrix cogitatio, testis conscientia, camifex timor. Inde quidam sanguis animi confitentis per lacrimas profluat. Postremo ab ipsa mente talis sententia proferatur, ut se indignum homo iudicet participatione corporis et sanguinis Domini: ut qui separan a regno caelorum timet per ultimam sententiam summi iu[1543]dicis, per ecclesiasticam disciplinam a Sacramento caelestis pañis interim separetur.

Versetur ante oculos imago futuri iudicii: ut cum alii accessunt ad altare Dei, quo ipse non accessit, cogitet quam sit contremiscenda illa poena, qua percipientibus alus vitam aetemam, alii in mortem praecipitantur aeternam. Ad hoc enim altare, quod nunc in Ecclesia est in terra positum, terrenis oculis expositum, ad mysteriorum divinotum signacula celebranda, multi etiam scelerati possunt accesoré: quoniam Deus commendat in hoc tempore patientiam suam, ut in future exserat severitatem suam. Accedunt enim ignorantes quoniam patientia Dei ad paenitentiam eos adducit. lili autem secundum duritiam cordis sui et cor impaenitens, thesaurizant sibi iram in die irae

tion of righteous judgment from God, who will repay each one according to his works. But to that altar to which Jesus ascended for us as a precursor, to which he preceded us as head of the Church and to which his members are to follow, none of those of whom, as I already remembered, the Apostle said: For those who do such works will not possess the kingdom of God. Only the priest will attend there; but the priest in his fullness, that is, with the body, of which the head, he, has already ascended to heaven. He is the one about whom the apostle Peter said: Holy people, royal priesthood. How will he dare or be able to enter inside the veil or into that invisible saint of saints who despised the medicine of celestial discipline and did not want to separate himself little by little from visible things? Whoever did not want to humble himself in order to be exalted, when he wants to be exalted he will be humiliated, and everyone who during this time has not secured a place in the body of the priest by the merit of obedience and the satisfaction of penance will be forever separated from the eternal saints. With what shameless face will he then want God's gaze to be turned away from his sins who does not say with all his heart: Because I recognize my crime and my sin is always before you? On what basis, I ask, will God deign to forgive what man disdains to acknowledge in himself?

8. Or what is it with which those who are deceived in their vanity flatter themselves? Persevering in his evils and lusts, et revelationis iusti iudicii Dei, qui reddet unicuique secundum opera sua (cf. Rom 2:4-6). Ad illud autem altare, quo praecursor pro nobis introiit Iesus, quo caput Ecclesiae praecessit, membris ceteris secuturis, nullus eorum accesoré poterit, de quibus, ut iam commemoravi, dixit Apostolus: Quoniam qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt (Gal 5:21). Solus enim sacerdos, sed plañe ibi totus assistet, adiuncto scilicet corpore qui caput est, quod iam ascendit in caelum. Ipse est cui dixit apostolus Petrus: Plebs sancta, regale sacerdotium (1 Petr 2,9). Quomodo ergo in interiora veli, et in illa invisibilia Sancta sanctorum intrare audebit aut poterit, qui medicinalm caelestis disciplinae contemnens, noluit paulisper a visibilibus separan? Qui enim noluit humiliari, ut exaltaretur; cum exaltan voluerit, deicietur; et in aeternum seiungetur ab aeternis sanctis, quisquís hoc tempore per merita oboedientiae et per satisfactionem paenitentiae non sibi providit locum in corpore sacerdotis. Qua enim fronte impudentiae tune volet averti faciem Dei a peccatis suis, qui nunc toto corde non dicit: Quoniam facinus meum ego agnosco, et peccatum meum ante me est semper? (Ps 50.5). Quo pact, quaeso, Deus dignatur ignoscere, quod in se ipse homo dedignatur agnoscere? 8. In eos qui sibi salutem praeter regnum caelorum pollicentur. Sententia ultima mittens aut in regnum, aut in ignem.—Aut illud quale est, in quo sibi blandiuntur, qui sua se vanitate seducunt? Persevering

despite hearing what the Apostle says: Because those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of heaven, they dare to promise themselves the desired salvation outside the kingdom of God and, at the same time they refuse to do penance for their sins and improve their perverse customs, they say among themselves: «I do not want to reign; "It is enough for me to save myself." They are deceived from the start, because there will be no salvation for those who persevere in iniquity. Truly the Lord said: As iniquity abounded, the love of many will grow cold; but whoever perseveres to the end, he will be saved; He promised, yes, salvation to those who persevere in love, not in iniquity. But where love exists, those evil works that separate from the kingdom of God cannot be found. For the entire law is contained in a single phrase; in which it is written: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself." Therefore, granted that there is some difference between those who reign and those who do not reign, it is nevertheless advisable that they all be in the same kingdom so as not to be counted in the number of enemies or strangers. All Romans own the Roman kingdom, although not all reign in it, but rather obey those who reign. The Apostle did not say: "Those who do such works" will not reign with God, but rather: they will not possess the kingdom of God. He said the same thing about the body and blood: flesh and blood will not possess the kingdom of God, since this corruptible will put on incorruption, and this mortal will put on immortality; so that it will no longer be body and blood, but

that from the animal body will derive the form and nature of the spiritual body. Fill them with terror, at least, that final sentence of our judge, which he wanted to discover now so that the faithful can avoid it, giving those who fear him a signal to flee from the presence of the arch. Except those who will be judges with him, as he promised when he said: You will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel... This number of judges includes all those who abandoned all their possessions for the sake of the Gospel and followed the Lord. The number 12, indeed, means a certain universality. The fact that Paul was not among the Twelve does not indicate that he will not be there. Except for them, then, whom he meant by the name of angels when he said: When the Son of Man comes to judge with his angels... The angels are, certainly, messengers; We rightly consider as messengers those who announce heavenly health to men. Hence we can also call evangelists good messengers; Even of John the Baptist it has been said: Behold, I send my angel before you. Except for them, as he had begun to say, the rest of the human multitude, as is evident from the Lord's own words, will be divided into two groups. He will put the sheep on the right, and the goats on the left. To the sheep, that is, to the righteous, he will say: Come, you blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you since the beginning of the world. Referring to this kingdom, the Apostle said

enim in malitiis atque luxuriis suis, cum audiunt Apostolum dicentem: Quoniam qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt (Gal 5,21): audent sibi praeter Dei regnum salutem, quam desiderant, polliceri; Atque ita inter se loquuntur, dum recusant agere paenitentiam pro peccatis suis, et perditos mores aliquando in melius commutare: Regnare nolo, sufficit mihi salvum me esse. In quo primum eos fallit,_ quia eorum nec salus ulla est; quorum iniquitas perseverat. Quod enim ait Dominus: Quoniam abundavit iniquitas, refrígescet caritas múltorum; qui autem perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit (Mt 24,12.13); salutem utique promisit perseverantibus in caritate, non in iniquitate. Ubi autem caritas est, opera illa mala a regno Dei separantia esse [1544] non possunt. Omnis enim lex in uno sermone impleta est, in eo quod scriptum est: Diliges proximum tuum tanquam te ipsum (Gal 5,14). Deinde si est aliqua differentia inter regnantes et non regnantes; oportet tamen ut in uno regno sint omnes, ne in hostium aut alienorum number deputentur. Omnes enim Romani Romanum regnum possident; quamvis non omnes in eo regnent, sed ceteris regnantibus pareant. Non autem ait Apostolus: Qui talia agunt, non regnabunt cum Deo; sed regnum Dei non possidebunt (ib., 21). Quod etiam de carne et sanguine dictum est: Caro et sanguis regnum Dei non possidebunt; quia corruptibile hoc induet incorruptionem, et mortale hoc induet immortalitatem (1 Cor 15,50.53); ut iam non caro et sanguis, sed ex animali corpore spiritualis

corporis habitum naturamque mereatur. Vel illa eos terreat ultima sententia iudicis nostri, quam propterea nunc aperiri voluit, ut ab eius fidelibus praecaveatur; dans metuentibus se significationem, ut fugiant a facie arcus (Ps 59,6). Exceptis enim eis qui cum illo etiam iudicabunt, quibus et promisit, they say: Sedebitis super duodecim thronos, iudicantes duodecim tribes Israel (Mt 19,28). In quo numero iudicantium omnes intelleguntur, qui propter Evangelium omnia sua dimiserunt, et secuti sunt Dominum. Duodenarius quippe numerus ad quamdam universitatem refertur. Non enim Paulus apostolus ibi non erit, quia inter illos duodecim non Fuit. Exceptis ergo illis, quos etiam nomine Angelorum significavit, quando ait: Cum venerit Filius hominis iudicare cum Angelis suis (ib., 25,31). Angelí enim utique nuntíi sunt. Nuntíos autem rectissime accipimus omnes qui salutem caelestem hominibus nuntiant. Unde etiam Evangelistae boni nuntii possunt interpret: et de Ioanne Baptista dictum est: Ecce mitto angelum meum ante faciem tuam (Mal 3,1). His ergo, ut dicere coeperam, exceptis, cetera omnium hominum multitudo, sicut in ipsius verbis Domini manifestum est, in duas parts dividetur. Positurus est enim oves ad dexteram, haedos ad sinistram: et dicetur ovibus, id est iustis: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est a constitutione mundi (Mt 25,3). De hoc utique regno dixit Apostolus, cum enumeraret opera mala:

recounting evil works: For those who do such works will not possess the kingdom of God. Listen to what those on the left will hear: Go to the eternal fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels. Therefore, who will dare to boast of the Christian name and at the same time not listen with all obedience and fear to the Apostle, who says: Be clear about this, knowing that no fornicator, nor impure, nor covetous person, who is a servant of idols, will have any share in the inheritance of the kingdom of Christ and of God? Let no one deceive you with vain words; Because of all this, the wrath of God comes on the distrustful children. So have no part with them. More extensively he says the same thing to the Corinthians: Do not be deceived; Neither the fornicators, nor the idolaters, nor the adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor the sodomites, nor the thieves, nor the covetous, nor the drunkards, nor the revilers, nor the robbers will possess the kingdom of God. But see how he took away the fear and hopelessness of salvation from those who committed such things in their former lives: You also were all these, but you have been washed and sanctified in the name of Jesus Christ our Lord and in the Spirit of our God. 9. So, then, will everyone who after baptism finds himself bound by some of his past evils be an enemy of himself to such an extent that he still hesitates to change his life while there is still time, even though, sinner as he is, he continues to live? By persevering in his sin, he stores up wrath for

the day of wrath and the revelation of God's righteous judgment. While still living, God's patience leads him to penitence. Bound with the chains of such deadly sins, do you refuse, or defer, or hesitate to flee to the keys of the Church, to be loosed on earth to be loosed in heaven? Can he who trusts only in his name as a Christian dare to promise himself any salvation after this life and not fear that truthful thunder that comes from the mouth of the Lord: Not everyone who says, "Lord, Lord," will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven; Will this one enter the kingdom of heaven? That? Does not the Apostle conclude the same thing when mentioning such things in his letter to the Galatians? The works of the flesh are manifest, he said, such as fornications, impurity, lust, idolatry, witchcraft, enmities, strife, jealousy, wrath, dissensions, heresies, envies, drunkenness, carousing, and the like, about which I tell you, as I have already told you, that those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God. Therefore, let man judge spontaneously regarding these things while he is still able and improve his habits, lest, when he is no longer able to do so, he will be judged by the Lord, even if he does not want to. And, although he himself pronounces against himself the sentence of a very harsh medicine, but always medicine, he presents himself to the bishops, the ministers of those keys in the Church 4. And as someone who is already beginning to be a good son, keeping the

Quoniam qui taita agunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt. Audi quid audiant qui a sinistris erunt: Ite, inquit, in ignem aeternum, qui praeparatus est diabolo et angelis eius (ib., 31). Quapropter, praesumere quis audeat de nomine christiano, et non cum omni oboedientia et timore audiat Apostolum dicentem: Hoc enim scitote, cognoscentes quoniam omnis fornicator, aut immundus, aut avarus, quod est idolorum servitus, non habet hereditatem in regno Christi et Dei? Nemo vos seducat inanibus verbis: propter haec enim venit ira Dei in filios diffidentiae. Nolite itaque effici participates eorum (Eph 5,5-7). Latius autem ad Corinthios haec dicit: Nolite errare; ñeque fornicatores, ñeque idolis servientes, ñeque adulteri, ñeque mólles, ñeque masculo[í545~\rum concubitors, ñeque jures, ñeque avari, ñeque ebriosi, ñeque maledici, ñeque rapaces, regnum Dei possidebunt (1 Cor 6,9-10). Sed videte quemadmodum timorem et desperationem salutis abstulerit eis, qui haec in vita veteri commiserunt. Et haec quidem, inquit, fuestis, sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis in nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi, et in Spiritu Dei nostri (ib., 11). 9. Paenitentia relapsis post Baptismum amplectenda.—Quisquís ergo post Baptismum aliquorum pristinorum malorum opere obligatus tenetur, usque adeone sibi inimicus est, ut adhuc dubitet vitam mutare, cum tempus est, cum ita peccat et vivit? Nam utique quod ita perseveranter

peccat, thesaurizat sibi iram in die irae et revelationis iusti iudicii Dei. Quod autem adhuc vivit, patientia Dei ad paenitentiam eum adducit. Implicatus igitur tam mortiferorum vinculis peccatorum detrectat, aut differt, aut dubitat confugere ad ipsas keys Ecclesiae, quibus solvatur in terra, ut sit solutus in cáelo; et audet sibi post hanc vitam, quia tantum christianus dicitur, salutem aliquam polliceri; nec verídico illo dominicae vocis tonitruo contremiscit: Non omnis qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum caélorum; sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei qui in caelis est, ipse intrabit in regnum caélorum? (Mt 7,21). Quid, ad Galatas idem apostolus, nonne talia enumerans eodem fine concludit? He manifested sunt, inquit, opera carnis, quae sunt jornicationes, immunditiae, luxuriae, idolorum servitus, veneficia, inimicitiae, contentiones, aemulationes, animositates, dissensiones, haereses, invidiae, ebrietates, comessationes, et his similia; quae praedico vobis, sicut praedixi quoniam qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt (Gal 5,19-21). Iudicet ergo se ipsum homo in istis voluntate, dum potest, et mores convertedat in melius: ne cum iam non poterit, etiam praeter voluntatem a Domino iudicetur. Et cum ipse in se protulerít severíssimae medícínae, sed tamen medicinale sententiam, veniat ad antistites, per quos illi in Ecclesia keys ministrantur: et tanquam bonus iam incipiens esse filius, See additional note [2]: ha mediation of the Church in the granting of forgiveness p.542.

order of the maternal members, receives the measure of satisfaction from the ministers of the sacraments. Thus, offering with devotion and supplication the sacrifice of a troubled heart, he accomplishes what will not only serve him personally to receive health, but also as an example for others. If his sin not only causes serious harm to him, but also serves as a scandal for others, and it seems to the bishop that it will have repercussions for the good of the Church, do not refuse to do penance before the knowledge of many or even the entire people; Do not oppose or shamefully add another tumor to your lethal and mortal wound. Always remember that God resists the proud and gives his grace to the humble. Is there anything more unfortunate, more perverse, than not feeling ashamed of a wound that cannot be hidden, and instead feeling ashamed of the bandage? 10. Let no one think, brothers, that they should despise the healthy advice of this penance because perhaps they warn and know that many whose serious sins they know approach the sacrament of the altar. Many, indeed, are corrected, like Peter; others are tolerated, like Judas; Many go unnoticed until the Lord arrives, who will illuminate the hidden darkness and reveal the thoughts of the heart. There are many who do not want to accuse others because they want to find an excuse in them. But many good Christians remain silent and tolerate the sins of others that they know about because

They often lack documentary evidence and cannot demonstrate what they know before ecclesiastical courts. Even if some things are true, the judge should not give them easy credit if they do not prove it reliably. I cannot separate anyone from communion (even if it is not a mortal withdrawal, but a medicinal one) unless there is a spontaneous confession or they have been summoned and declared convicted in an ecclesiastical court. Who will dare to carry one thing or another on their shoulders, that is, to be someone's accuser and judge? It is known that the apostle Paul briefly hinted at this way of proceeding in the same letter to the Corinthians: when, having mentioned some of those sins, starting from certain cases, he left the standard of ecclesiastical judgment for all fellow human beings. He said: I wrote to you in a letter not to mix with fornicators - of course they are not the fornicators of this world - or with the covetous, or those who live by plunder, or idolaters; Otherwise you would have to leave this world. For men who live in this world cannot not live with such; nor could they win them to Christ if they avoided talking and eating with them. Therefore said the Lord, who ate with publicans and sinners: The healthy have no need of a doctor, but the sick; For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners. And for this very reason the Apostle continues and adds: But now I have written to you not to mix. If a brother is denounced as a fornicator, or an idolater, or a covetous man, or a curser, or a drunkard, or a thief, do not even eat with those like him.

maternorum membrorum ordine custodito, a praepositis Sacramentorum accipiat satisfactionis suae modum; ut in offerendo sacrifice cordis contriban devotus et supplex, id tamen agat quod non solum ipsi prosit ad recipiendam salutem, sed etiam ceteris ad exemplum. Ut si peccatum eius, non solum in gravi eius malo, sed etiam in Tanto scandalo aliorum est, atque hoc expediré utilitati Ecclesiae videtur antistiti, in notitia multorum, vel etiam totius plebis agere paenitentiam non recuset, non resistat, non lethali et mortiferae plaguee per puderem addat tumorem. Meminerit semper, quod superbis Deus resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam (Iac 4,6). Quid enim est infelicius, quid perversius, quam de ipso vulnere, quod latere non potest, non erubescere, et de ligatura eius erubescere? 10. In eos qui paenitentiae neglegendae exemplum ex alus sumunt. A communione non prohibentur nisi sponte confessi, vel legitime convicti. Nemo arbitretur, fratres, propterea se consilium salutiferae huius paenitentiae [1546] debenré contemnere, quia multos forte advertit et novit ad Sacramenta altaris accessé, quorum talia crimina nonignot. Multi enim corriguntur, ut Petrus: multi tolerantur, ut ludas: multi nesciuntur doñee veniat Dominus, qui illuminet abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestet cogitationes cordis (cf. 1 Cor 4,5). Nam plerique propterea nolunt alios aecusare, dum se per illos cupiunt excusare. Plerique autem boni christiani propterea tacent, et sufferunt aliorum peccata quae noverunt

quia documentis saepe deseruntur, et ea quae ipsi sciunt, iudicibus ecclesiasticis provere non possunt. Quamvis enim vera sint quaedam; non tamen iudici facile credenda sunt, nisi certis indiciis demonstrentur. Nos vero a communione prohibere quemquam non possumus (quamvis haec prohibitio nondum sit mortalis, sed medicinalis), nisi aut sponte confessum, aut in aliquo sive saeculari, sive ecclesiastico iudicio nominatum atque convictum. Quis enim sibi utrumque audeat assumere, ut cuiquam ipse sit et aecusator et iudex? Cuiusmodi regulam etiam Paulus apostolus in eadem ad Corinthios Epistola breviter insinuasse intellegitur, cum quibusdam talibus commemoratis criminibus, ecclesiastici iudicii formam ad omnia similia ex quibusdam daret. Ait enim: Scripsi vobis in epistola non commisceri fornicaras: non utique fornicariis huius mundi, aut avaris, aut raptoribus, aut idolis servientibus; alioquin debueratis de hoc mundo exire (ib., 5,9-10). Non enim possunt nomines in hoemundo vivos, nisi cum talibus vivere: nec eos possunt lucrifacere Christo, si eorum colloquium convictumque vitaverint. Unde et Dominus cum publicanis et peccatoribus comedens: Non est opus, inquit, sanis medicus, sed male habentibus. Non enim veni vocare iustos, sed peccatores (Mt 9,12.13). Et ideo sequitur Apostolus, et adiungit: Nunc autem scripsi vobis non commisceri. Si quis frater nominatur aut fornicator, aut idolis serviens, aut avarus, aut maledicus, aut ebriosus, aut rapax;

Who am I to judge outsiders? Of those within, do you not judge? Of those who are outside, God will be the judge. Drive evil away from yourselves. With those words he made it clear that evildoers should not be separated from the communion of the Church lightly and in any way; If they cannot be separated by a trial, they must rather be tolerated, lest, by undiscerningly avoiding the bad, someone will himself leave the Church and drag those from whom he seems to flee to hell. In this regard, the Holy Scriptures have left us examples, such as that of the harvest, where the straw must be tolerated until the last clean; or that of the nets, where the good fish are mixed with the bad until the moment of separation, which will take place on the shore, that is, at the end of the world, and must be tolerated with a calm spirit. And this does not contradict what the Apostle says elsewhere: Who are you to judge another's servant? He stands or falls for his own lord. He did not want a man to judge another man based on an arbitrary suspicion or even usurping a judicial power that was not his, but rather that it be done according to the order established in the Church, either confessing spontaneously, or after having been accused and declared convicted. Otherwise, why did he say: If a brother is denounced as a fornicator or idolater, etc., if not because he wanted to imply that this denunciation made against someone is carried out by means of a sentence in accordance with the regulations cum huiusmodi nec quidem cibum sumere. Quo enim mihi de bis qui foris sunt iudicare? Nonne de bis qui intus sunt vos judicatis? De bis autem qui foris sunt, Deus judicabit. Aujerte malum a vobis ipsis (1 Cor 5:11-13). Quibus verbis satis otendit non fearé aut quomodolibet sed per iudicium auferendos esse malo ab Ecclesiae communione: ut si per iudicium auferri non possunt, tolerantur potius, ne perverse malo quisque avoiding, ab Ecclesia ipse discedens, eos quos fugere videtur, vinciat ad gehennam. Quia et ad hoc nobis sunt in Scripturis sanctis exempla proposita, velut in messe, ut palea sufferatur usque ad ultimum ventilabrum (cf. Mt 3:12); velut intra illa retía, ubi pisces boni cum malis usque ad segregationem, quaefutura est in littore, id est, in fine saeculi, aequo animo tolerentur (ib., 13,47-50). Non enim contrarium est huic loco id quod alio loco dicit Apostolus: Tu quis es qui judicas alienum servum?

Suo domino [1547] stat, aut cadit (Rom 14:4). Noluit enim hominem ab nomine iudicari ex arbitrio suspicionis, vel etiam extraordinary usurpato iudicio sed potius ex lege Dei secundum ordinem Ecclesiae, sive ultro confessum, sive accusatum atque convictum. Alioquin illud cur dixit: Si quis frater nominatur aut fornicator, aut idolis serviens (1 Cor 5:11), et cetera; nisi quia eam nominationem intellegi voluit quae fit in quemquam, cum sententia ordine iudiciario

and integrity of the law? Well, if the denunciation is enough, many innocent people will be convicted, since it is common for them to be falsely accused of any crime. 11. Those whom we exhort to do penance should not look for companions in torment nor rejoice in finding many, since they will not burn less because they burn in the company of many. That would not be sound advice for health, but rather the vain consolation of an ill-wisher. Or do you notice that many of the dignitaries and ministers who are in positions of honor in the Church do not live in accordance with the words and sacraments that they themselves administer to the people? Oh unfortunate men, who forget Christ to look at such! To Christ, who said so far in advance that one must obey the law of God rather than imitate those who say and do not do, and who, tolerating his betrayer until the end, even sent him to evangelize with others. These men are so absurd, so out of order and miserable, that they prefer to imitate the bad customs of their superiors than to comply with the precepts of the Lord preached by them. They are like a traveler who thinks he has to stop along the way because the milestone stones that, full of inscriptions, tell him so, are not working. If you want to get there, why not look and follow those companions who not only show you the right path, but also walk along it with perseverance and joy? And if these are missing or, better yet, not seen—well, can't pueatque integratate profertur? Nam si nominatio sufficit, multi damnandi sunt innocentes, quia saepe false in quoquam crimine nominantur. 11. Adversus eos qui pravis exemplis acquiescentes contemnunt paenitentiam. Praepositi mali non imitandi. Elegans similareo.—Non ergo ílli, quos monemus agere paenitentiam, quaerant sibi committees ad supplicium; nec gaudeant quia plures inveniunt. Non enim propterea minus ardebunt, quia cum multis ardebunt. Non est enim hoc sanitatis certum consilium, sed malevolentiae vanum solatium. An forte attendunt multos etiam in ipsis honoribus ecclesiasticis praepositorum et ministerum non congruenter vívete sermonibus et Sacramentis, quae per eos populis ministrantur? O miseros nomines, qui hos intuendo Christum obliviscuntur! qui et Tanto ante praedixit, ut legi Dei potius obtemperetur, quam imitandi videantur illi, qui ea quae dicunt non faciunt (cf. Mt 23:3); et traditorem suum tolerans usque in finem, etiam ad evangelizandum cum ceteris misit.

Tam sunt autem isti absurdi et praeposteri et miseri, qui praepositorum suorum malas mores imitari eligunt, quam per eos praedicata Domini praecepta servare; quam si quisquam viator remanendum sibi esse existimet in itinere, cum viderit milliaria_ lapídea litterís plena viam docere, et non ambulare. Cur enim non potius, si pervenire desíderat, such committees intuetur et consequítur, qui et viam bene demonstrant, et in ea perseveranter atque alacriter ambulant? Quod si istí desint, vel potius minus appareant, nam deesse

may be lacking—why do these men not seek with eager love what they preach in order to carry it out, in the same way that they seek with maliciousness full of suspicions what to murmur in order to deceive, partly because they cannot find good ones, while they themselves are bad, and partly fearing to find them, always wanting to be bad? But let us grant that no men worthy of imitation will now be found. Whoever you are who thinks this, look with your mind to the Lord, who became man to teach man how to live. If Christ dwells in the inner man through the faith present in your heart and you remember what the apostle John said: Whoever says that he abides in Christ must walk as Christ walked, you will not lack someone to follow, and if someone else sees you, he will stop lamenting the lack of good Christians. If, then, you do not know what it means to live holyly, learn the divine commandments. Perhaps there are many who live this way, but it seems to you that no one lives that way, because you do not know what living rightly consists of. But, if you know it, put it into practice, to have what you are looking for and show others what to imitate. Look with your mind at Christ, at the apostles, the last of whom is the one who says: Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ. Contemplate with your mind so many thousands of martyrs. Why do you delight in celebrating their births with clumsy banquets 5 and do you not like to follow their life with honest customs? Among them you will see not only vanon possunt: ​​non enim sic quaerunt nomines caritate studiosa quod praedicent ad imitationem quomodo quaerunt iniquitate suspiciosa quod murmurent ad deceptionem, partim non inveniendo bonds, dum ipsi mali sunt; partim timendo invenire, dum mali esse semper volunt. Sed tamen concedamus non apparere nunc nomines worthy imitatione. Quisquís hoc whores, mind Dominum intuere, qui homo factus est, ut hominem vivere doceret. Si habitat Christus in interiore homine per fidem in corde tuo, rememberisque illud quod Ioannes ait: Qui dicit se in Christo manere, debent quemadmodum Ule ambulavit, et ipse ambulare (1 lo 2,6); ita nec tibi deerit quem sequaris, et cum te alius viderit, de bonorum inopia conqueri desinet. Si enim non nosti quid sit recte vivere, divina praecepta cognosce. Fortassis enim multi recte vivunt; sed propterea tibi nullus recte vivere videtur, quoniam quid sit recte vivere [1548] you ignore. Si autem nosti, age quod nosti; ut et tu quod quaeris habeas, et alus quod imitatentur ostendas.

Christum animo attende, attende Apostólos, quorum novissimus est ille qui dicit: Imitatores mei estofe, sicut et ego Christi (1 Cor 4,16). Take heart tot martyrum millia. Cur enim te atalitia eorum conviviis turpibus celebrare delectat, et eorum vitam sequi honestis moribus non delectat? men, but also women, and even boys and girls, whom neither imprudence deceives, nor iniquity perverts, nor the fear of danger bankrupt, nor the love of the world corrupts. Thus, without you finding an excuse, you will be surrounded not only by the inevitable rectitude of the precepts, but also by an innumerable multitude of examples 6. 12. But let us try how useful and healthy penitence is, to fulfill once and for all what we proposed. If, having lost hope in salvation, you accumulate sins upon sins, as it is written: The sinner, when he reaches the depths of evil, despises it, do not despise it, do not lose hope; Cry out to the Lord even from the depths and say: From the depths I have cried out to you, Lord; Lord, listen to my voice. Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If you look at crimes, Lord, Lord, who will stand? Because forgiveness is in you. From that depth the Ninevites shouted, and found that forgiveness, and the prophet's threat was annulled more easily than the humiliation of penitence. Here you may say: «I am already baptized into Christ, at which time all my past sins were forgiven; I have become despicable by repeating my ways and in the eyes of God I have become like a horrible dog that returns to its vomit. Where will I flee from his spirit? Where will I flee from his presence? Where, brother, but, through repentance, to the misericorsed etiam feminas, desserto, pueros et puellas, nec imprudentia decipi, nec iniquitate pervertí, nec periculi timore frangí, nec saeculi amore corrumpi. Ita te non invenientem quid excuses, non solum praeceptorum inevitabilis rectitudo, sed etiam exemplorum innumerabilis multitudo circumdabit. CAPUT V.—12. Peccator nullus desperet, sed ad paenitentiam confugiat. Mutatio vitae et satisfiiio pro commissis.—Sed de utilitate ac salubritate paenitentiae, ut quod instituimus aliquando peragamus: si iam de sanitate desperans addis peccata peccatis, sicut scriptum est: Peccator, cum venerit in profundum malorum, contemnit (Prov 18,3): noli contemnere, noli desperare; clama etiam de profundis ad Dominum, et dic ei: De profundis clamavi ad te, Domine; Domine, exaudi vocem meam. De tali profound Ninivitae clamaverunt, ct hanc propitiationem invenerunt: faciliusque est evacuata, comminatio Prophetae, quam humiliatio paenitentiae (cf. Ion 3). Hic fortasse dicis: Sed ego iam baptizatus sum in Christo, a quo omnia mihi peccata praeterita dimissa sunt; vilis factus sum nimis iterans vias meas, et canis horribilis oculis Dei, conversus ad vomitum suum. What abibo a spiritu eius? et a facie eius quo fugiam? Quo, frater, nisi ad eius misericordiam Augustine, like a good Roman, unites the praeceptum and the exemplum. day of him whose power you had despised by sinning? No one can effectively flee from him except by fleeing towards him, fleeing from his severity to his goodness. Indeed, what place will receive you in your escape where His presence does not find you? If you go up to heaven, he is there; If you descend to hell, it is there. Therefore take your wings and set yourself in a straight direction and dwell in hope at the extremities of this world: there his hand will take you and his right hand will guide you. Whatever you have done, whatever you have sinned, you are still in this life, from which the Lord would certainly have taken you if he had not wanted to cure you. Why then do you overlook that the patience of God leads you towards penitence? He who by crying could not persuade you not to go away, forgiving you, calls you to return. Look at King David. He had also already received the sacraments of his time, he was already circumcised, something that our parents considered to be baptism; Well, referring to that, the Apostle says that Abraham had received the sign of the righteousness of faith. He was also already anointed with a venerable anointing, in which the royal priesthood of the Church was figured. He was suddenly convicted of adultery and murder. Not in vain, then, repentant, he cried to the Lord from such a terrible and abrupt abyss of crime, saying: Turn your face from my sins and erase all my ways. In merit of what but what he says next: I recognize my evil and my sin is always in your presence? What did you offer the Lord to have it for him?

peak? If you had wanted a sacrifice, he said, I would have offered it to you; but burnt offerings do not delight you. Sacrifice for God is a troubled heart; a contrite and humiliated heart, God does not despise it. Thus, not only did he devoutly offer him this sacrifice, but he also showed with those words what should be offered to him. In fact, it is not enough to improve one's morals and turn away from bad actions if one does not satisfy God for everything one has done through the pain of penitence, the groaning of humility, the sacrifice of a contrite heart and the collaboration of alms. Blessed are the merciful, for God will have mercy on them. It has not only been said that we abstain from sins: Pray to God, he said, also for past sins, so that they may be forgiven you. Peter was also already faithful and had even baptized others into Christ. Look, then, at Peter boasting and accused, fearful and hurt, weeping and healed. Even after the coming of the Holy Spirit from heaven, a certain Simon wanted to buy the Holy Spirit himself, thinking of an extremely criminal and impious treatment already after being baptized; However, he too, corrected by Peter himself, accepted the advice of penitence. The apostle Paul, who certainly sent his letters to those who were already faithful, also says: It is strange that, when I come to you, God does not humble me again and I have to mourn many of those who previously sinned and did not do penance for the impurity, lust and fornications that they

paenitendo, cuius potestatem sinning contempseras? Nemo enim tecte fugit ab ilio, nisi ad illum, ab eius severitate ad eius bonitotem. Quis enim locus te excipiet fugientem, ubi eius praesentia te non inveniat? If you ascend in caelum, ibi est: if you descend ad infernum, adest. We are surrounded, therefore, not only by the precepts to act rightly, but also by the examples of both those who did good and those who repented to recover the salvation they had lost by sinning. But suppose it is not assured that God will forgive. What does he lose by pleading with God who did not hesitate to lose salvation by offending God? Who is certain that the emperor will forgive? And yet, you spend money, you cross the seas and you subject yourself to the uncertainty of storms, and, to avoid death, you almost receive death itself. A man is supplicated through other men; They do it without hesitation, despite the end to which they are to arrive being doubtful. And yet, the keys of the Church offer more guarantee than the hearts of kings, and everything that those keys unleash on earth will also be unleashed in heaven, as promised. And humility is also much more honest, by which one humbles oneself in the Church of God, and requires less effort, and without any danger of temporal death eternal death is avoided. Circumstant ergo nos et praecepta tecte faciendi, et exempla non tantum recte facientium, sed etiam paenitentium ad recipiendam _ salutem, quae fuet amissa peccando. Sed fac incertum esse utrum ignoscat Deus. Quid perdit, cum supplicat Deo, qui salutem perdit non dubitavit, cum offenderet Deum? Quis enim certus est quod etiam imperator ignoscat? Et tamen pecunia funditur, maria transmeantur, procellarum incerta subeuntur; et penis ut mors Evitatur, Mors ipsa suscipitur. Supplicatur deinde per homines homini: sine dubitatione fiunt ista, cum sit dubium quo fine proveniant. Et tamen certiores sunt claves Ecclesiae, quam corda regum: quibus clavibus quodcumque in terra solvitur, etiam in cáelo solutum promittitur (cf. Mt 16,19). Et multo est honestior humilitas, qua se quisque humiliat Ecclesiae Dei: et labor minor imponitur, et nullo temporalis mortis periculo mors aeterna vitatur.

1. It is easy to recognize the voice of the repentant in the words with which we have responded to the psalmist. Turn your face from my sins and erase all my evils. Not having prepared any sermon to address to your charity, I have seen that I have to speak to you about it by command of the Lord. Today I wanted to give you time to ruminate, knowing the sumptuous banquet in which you participated yesterday. But since you take what is served to you with benefit for your health, there is not a day that you do not enjoy a good appetite. May the Lord our God himself grant me abundant strength and you to listen usefully. I am not unaware that I have to serve your good and profitable will. Help me with your desire and attention: desire for God and attention to the word, so that I can tell you what He who feeds you through me deems useful. We recognize, therefore, the cry of the repentant in these words: Turn your face from my sins and erase all my evils. So, then, the divine order comes to me to speak to you something about penance. Let us say something, then, about the usefulness of penance, especially taking into account that the holy day of the anniversary is approaching, in view of whose proximity it is advisable to put more effort into humiliating souls and taming bodies. 2. In Holy Scripture there is a three-fold way of doing penance. In fact, no one properly approaches the baptism of Christ, in which all our sins are forgiven without having done penance for their previous life. No one chooses a new life without having repented of the old one. I must prove with the authority of the divine books whether those who are to be baptized must do penance. When the previously promised Holy Spirit was sent, the Lord faithfully fulfilling his promise, once the disciples received him, they began, as you know, to speak in all languages, so that each one present recognized his own. Terrified by this miracle, they asked the apostles for advice on what they should do. Then Peter told them that they had to worship the one they crucified and drink with faith the blood that they had shed in fury. After our Lord Jesus Christ had been announced to them, recognizing their guilt, they were sorry, praying that what was predicted by the prophet would be fulfilled in them: I turned to my misfortune when the thorn was stuck in me. They turned to their misfortune of pain, while the thorn of the memory of their sin stabbed them. They were with-

defeated that they had not done anything wrong: the thorn had not yet been stuck in them. So that you may recognize that the thorn was stuck in them when Peter spoke, the Scripture said: When Peter spoke, they were pricked in their hearts.' Therefore, after saying in the psalm: I turned to my misfortune when the thorn pierced me, he continues: I recognized my sin and did not hide my crime. I said, "I will proclaim my crime against myself to the Lord, and you have forgiven the wickedness of my heart." After feeling pricked by the thorn of memory, they said to the apostles: What must we do? Peter answered them: Do penance and let each one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and your sins will be forgiven. If by chance some of those who are preparing to be baptized are present here—I think they will attend to hear the word with greater eagerness the closer they come to the moment of forgiveness—I speak to them now first so that they may open their minds to hope. Love becoming what you are not, hate what you were. Conceive with desire the new man that is to be born; Do not doubt that you can be forgiven for anything that bothers you about your past life, anything that torments your conscience, absolutely everything, whether big or small, worthy of being said or not, lest human doubt hold against you what the mercy of God wants to forgive.

3. Each one remembers exactly the example we found in that first town. Referring to that, the Apostle said: All these things were figures of ours. What had he said? I do not want you to ignore, brothers, that our fathers were under the cloud and that they were all baptized in Moses, in the cloud and in the sea; that they all ate the same spiritual food and drank the same spiritual drink. They drank, in effect, from the spiritual rock that followed them. The rock was Christ. The one whom no faithful has ever contradicted, said that all of these were our figures. And, despite having listed many, he only gave the solution to one by saying: The rock was Christ. By solving only one, he invited us to investigate the rest; But so that the investigator does not go astray away from Christ, so that he investigates firmly, founded on the rock, he said: The rock was Christ. He said that all those things were our figures, but they were all dark. Who can remove the bark? Who will reveal them? Who will dare to argue about them? In this, like dense jungle and thick shadow, a light turned on: The rock, he said, was Christ. Now in the presence of the light, let us investigate what the others mean: what is the meaning of the sea, the clouds, the manna. He did not explain this to us, but he showed us what the rock was. The transit through the sea is baptism. But like baptism, that is, saving water, it is not saving if it has not been consecrated with the name

of Christ, who shed his blood for us, is signed to the water with his cross. To signify this in that baptism, the Red Sea was crossed. What the manna from heaven symbolizes was clearly explained by the Lord himself: Your fathers, he said, ate the manna in the desert and died. How could they not live, if the figure, although it could foreshadow life, could not be life? They ate, he said, the manna and died, that is, the manna they ate could not save them from death; which does not mean that the manna caused their death, but simply that it did not free them from it. The one who, on the other hand, was going to deliver them was the one who was figured in the manna. The manna came, indeed, from heaven. See what it represented: I am, he said, the living bread that came down from heaven. As diligent and attentive people, pay attention to the words of the Lord to progress and know how to read and listen. They ate, he said, the same spiritual food. What does the same mean if not that they ate the same as us? I see that it is somewhat difficult to present and explain what I have tried to say, but your benevolence will help me; she will get from the Lord whoever is capable. They ate, he said, the same spiritual food. It would have been enough to say: "They ate spiritual food." But he said the same. I can't find any other way to understand this but by referring to what we also eat. So, someone will say, is that manna the same as the one I receive now? If so, nothing came now, if it was there before. In this way the scandal of the cross is left without content. Why then is it the same but because

added spiritual? In fact, those who then received the manna thinking that it only satisfied their bodily needs and that it fed their belly, not their mind, ate nothing great; They simply satisfied his need. God fed some and meant something to others. The first ate a bodily food, but not a spiritual food. Which of our fathers does he say ate the same spiritual food? Who should we think about, brothers, but those who were truly our parents? Better yet, not only were they our parents, but they are, since they all still live. The Lord said to some unbelievers: Your fathers ate the manna in the desert and died. What do your parents mean here if not those whom you imitate with your infidelity, whose ways you follow by not believing and offering resistance to God? According to this way of understanding it, it says: You have the devil for your father. The devil, it is true, neither created by his power nor begot any man, and yet he is called the father of the wicked, not because he begat them, but because they imitate him. In the same way, but on the contrary, it is said: Therefore, you are Abraham's offspring, although he is speaking to the Gentiles, who did not bring their carnal offspring from Abraham. They were his children not because they were born to him, but because they imitated him. The Lord abrogates and rejects Abraham's fatherhood over unbelievers when he says to them: If you were Abraham's sons, you would do his works. And to eradicate those evil trees that gloried in Abraham's fatherhood, his children are promised.

As in this place it says: Your fathers ate the manna in the desert and died, because they did not understand what they ate, and, not understanding it, they took only a corporal food, so also the Apostle says that our fathers - not the fathers of the unbelievers, of the impious, who ate and died, but our fathers, the fathers of the faithful - ate a spiritual food, and, consequently, the same. Our fathers, he said, ate the same spiritual food and drank the same spiritual drink. So there were those there who understood what they were eating; There were those who tasted Christ more in their hearts than manna in their mouths. Why talk about others? Among them was, first of all, the servant of God Moses, faithful in all his house, who knew what he dispensed, and which must then remain hidden and be revealed in the future. To put it simply: all those who saw meaning in Christ in the manna ate the same spiritual food as we do; All those who sought nothing more than bodily satiety in the manna are the fathers of the unbelievers, who ate it and died. In the same way, they drank the same drink: For the rock was Christ. So they drank the same drink as us; but a spiritual drink, that is, that which was taken by faith, not that which was drunk with the body. You heard that it was the same drink: The rock was Christ, since there is not one Christ from then and another from now. Certainly, that rock was one thing and the stone that Jacob placed next to it was another.

Sic etiam eumdem potum: Petra enim Christus (1 Cor 10:4). Eumdem ergo potum quem nos, sed spiritualem; Id est, qui fide capiebatur, non qui corpore hauriebatur. Audistis eumdem potum: Petra erat Christus (ib.); non enim alter Christus tune, alter nunc. Altera quidem illa petra (cf. Ex 17:6), alter lapis quem sibi

to his head; one the lamb sacrificed to be eaten and the other the ram tangled in the bushes to be sacrificed when Abraham forgave his son because he was commanded, as he had also offered him to obey a command. The animals were different, the stones different, but they were the same Christ and, therefore, the same food and the same drink. Finally, the rock itself was hit with the wood so that water came out, since it was hit with a rod. Why with wood and not with iron but because the cross was brought close to Christ to give us grace to drink? So, the same food and the same drink, but for those who understand and believe. For those who do not understand, there was nothing there but manna and water, food for the hungry and drink for the thirsty; neither one nor the other for the believer; for the believer it is the same as now. So, Christ still had to come; Now, Christ has already come. It must come and it came: different words, but the same Christ. 4. Since the occasion arises, I want to say something about the doubt of God's servant Moses. She was also a figure of ancient saints. Moses hesitated before the water; He hesitated when he hit the rock with the stick so that water came out. Whoever reads this doubt may pass it by without understanding it, since he or she will not even dare to investigate it. The Lord did not like that doubt, and he made it known not only by rebuking it, but also by punishing it. Through it it is said to Moses: You shall not introduce posuit ad caput Iacob (cf. Gen 28:11); alter agnus occisus ut manducaretur Pascha (cf. Ex 12), alter aries haerens in vepribus immolandus, quando filio suo pepercit Abraham iussus, quem iussus obtulerat (cf. Gen 22:13); alter ovis et altera ovis, alter lapis et alter lapis, Idem tamen Christus; ideo eumdem cibum, ideo eumdem potum. Denique percussa est ipsa petra ligno, ut aqua deflueret: vírga ením percussa est (cf. Ex 17, 5-6). Quare ligno, non ferro, nisi quia crux ad Christum accessit, ut nobis gratiam propinaret? Eumdem ergo cibum, eumdem potum, sed intellegentibus et credentibus. Non intellegentibus autem, illud solum manna, illa sola aqua; ille cibus esurienti, potus iste sitienti; nec ille, nec iste credenti: credenti autem idem qui nunc. to your people in the land of promise. Go up the mountain and die. God here certainly appears angry. What shall we say of Moses, my brothers? He doubted when the tree was applied to the rock: the disciples doubted when they saw the Lord crucified. Moses was a figure of them. He was a figure of that Peter who denied him three times. Why did Peter hesitate? Because the wood was applied to the rock. When the Lord announced the manner of his death, that is, the cross, Peter was afraid: Far be it from you, Lord; that won't happen! You doubt because you see that the rod is getting closer to the rock. Then the disciples lost the hope they had in the Lord; in a way it was interrupted when they saw him crucified, when they mourned him dead. After his resurrection, the Lord found them talking among themselves, wrapped in sadness, about it; and controlling his eyes so that they would not recognize him, not in order to withdraw from the believers, but to defer making himself known to those who doubted, he joined them as a third party in conversation and asked them what they were talking about. They were surprised that he was the only one to ignore what had taken place in the same person who asked. Are you the only one, they said to him, who are a foreigner in Jerusalem? And they tell him what happened to Jesus. And they immediately open the marrows of his despair and, without knowing it, show his wound to the doctor: We hoped, they tell him, that the redemption of Israel would take place in him. Mare Rubrum Baptismus erat, populus transiens baptizabatur: transitus ipse Baptismus erat, thirst in cloud. Adhuc enim nubilabatur quod praenuntiabatur: adhuc occultabatur quod promittebatur. Iammo recessit clouds, manifestae veritatis serenitas facta est: quia recessit et velum, per quod loquebatur Moyses. Hoc velum et in temple pendebat, ne secreto templi viderentur: sed in junction Domini velum conscissum est, ut paterent. Come ergo ad Baptismum: ingredere intrepidus viam per mare Rubrum; noli esse de peccato praeterito tanquam de Aegyptio sequente sollicitus. Premebant te peccata tua duro onere servitutis, sed in Aegypto, in amore huius saeculi, in peregrinatione longinqua; cogebant te sectari opera terrena, tanquam lateres faceré, opera lútea operabaris. Premunt te peccata, veni securus ad Baptismum: usque ad aquam hostis sequi poterit, ibi morietur. Time aliquid de vita praeterita, crede aliquid remansurum tuorum peccatorum, si aliquis remansit Aegyptiorum. He prayed, then stretched out his arms; and when he lowered them, Amalee triumphed; When he raised them he was defeated. Have your hands extended too; May Amalee be defeated, tempter and impediment in our path. Be sober and vigilant in prayer, in doing good; but not outside of Christ, since extending his arms symbolized the cross of Christ. The Apostle expands on it when he says: The world is crucified for me, and I for the world. Be defeated, then, Amalee; be defeated and do not prevent the passage of God's people. If you let your hands fall from doing good, from the cross of Christ, Amalee will prevail. In any case, do not think that you must always be courageous, nor do you faint in total despair. That alternation of weakness and strength in the hands of the servant of God Moses was, perhaps, a symbol of the same alternation in you. Sometimes, in fact, you faint in the midst of temptations, but you do not succumb. He lowered his hands for a little while, he didn't completely collapse. If I said, "My foot has moved," behold, your mercy helped me. Do not be afraid, because you have as a helper on the way the one who did not lack you as a liberator in Egypt.
