Immo vero unda quaedam caritatis ibat in corde tuo, et tanquam de vena interiore manabat: tenes odium contra fratrem, obturasti fontem. Non solum ergo nihil perdis, cum ignoscis; sed abundantius irrigaris. Caritas non angustatur. Ponis ibi lapidem offensionis, et tu tibi facis anguishes. Vindicabo me, ulciscar me, ego illi ostendam, ego faciam: aestuas, laboras, cui licet ignoscendo esse securum, securum vivere,
Sermon 352 Penance

be, live and pray calmly. Well what are you going to do? You are going to pray. Why ask when? Today you are going to pray. Or are you not going to pray? Full of anger and hatred, threats of revenge: you do not forgive from the heart. Hete praying; Hehe, the time has come to pray; you begin to hear or recite those words yourself. Having recited or listened to the previous requests, you have to reach this other one. Or if you are not to arrive, where are you to go? Will you stray from Christ to not forgive the enemy? In fact, if you go astray in prayer so as not to have to say: Forgive us our debts, since you cannot continue: Just as we forgive our debtors, lest the answer be given to you instantly: "I forgive you in the same way that you forgive"; Therefore, since you cannot speak such words and do not want to forgive, you will deviate from this little verse, ignore it and say what follows: Do not lead us into temptation. Here your creditor will arrest you, whose face you tried to avoid. It happens like when in a village one meets another to whom one owes something: if a narrow street is easy, one abandons the path one was taking and takes another direction so as not to meet the creditor. This is what you thought you had done with this little verse. You avoided saying: "Forgive me, as I forgive", so that I would not forgive you like you, that is, deny you forgiveness, since you do not want to forgive; You didn't mean it, avoiding his presence. Who are you avoiding? Who are you that you shun it? Where will you go, where can you be that he is not? You will have to say: Where will I go that takes me away from your spirit? where

Will I flee from your presence? If I go up to heaven, there you are; If I descend into hell, there you are. Can you, debtor, go, fleeing from Christ, to a place farther than hell? Your creditor is also there. What do you have to do but what's next? I will take my wings and fly straight to the end of the sea, that is, I will meditate from my hope on the end of the world, I will live in your precepts and I will rise with the two wings of charity. Therefore, it fulfills the two wings of charity. Love your neighbor as yourself and do not maintain hatred that makes you flee from the creditor. 8. There still remains the third way of penance, about which I am going to speak briefly to fulfill, with the help of the Lord, what I had proposed and promised myself. It is the most severe and painful penance that properly gives its name in the Church to penitents, who are removed from participation in the sacrament of the altar, lest, receiving it unworthily, they eat and drink their own damnation. Such penance is pitiful. The wound is serious: perhaps adultery has been committed, perhaps murder, perhaps some sacrilege; serious incident, serious and fatal injury; but the doctor is all-powerful. After having suffered the suggestion of the fact, having delighted in it, having given consent and carried it out, he already smells as if he were four days dead. But even the Lord did not abandon him, but cried out: Lazarus, come out. The mass of the grave gave way before the voice of the

securum orare. Nam ecce quid acturus is? Oraturus is. What do you say when? Hodie oraturus is. Is it not yet oraturus? Ira et odio impletus, vindictam minaris: non dimittis ex corde. Ecce oras, ecce venit orandi hora, incipis verba illa vel audire vel dicere. Dictis et auditis superioribus, venturus es ad hunc versum. Aut si non venturas, quo iturus? Ne ignoscas immico, are you deviating Christo? Plan si in oratione deviabis, ut nolis dicere: Dimitte nobis debita nostra (Mt 6,12); quia non potes dicere: sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris (ib.); ne tibi cita responda[1558]tur. Sic dimitto quomodo et tu dimittis: ergo quia hoc non potes dicere, et non vis dimittere, deviabis ab hoc versu, et praetermittes, et dices quod sequitur: Ne nos patiaris induci in temptationem (ib., 13); Ibi te capiet creditor tuus, cuius quasi faciem devitabas. Quomodo quisque in vico cum occurrerit ei cui aliquid debent, si ad manum est diverticulum, dimittit quo ibat; et it per aliam partem, ne faciem videat creditoris. Hoc tu in isto versu te fecisse arbitratus is: devitasti dicere: Dimitte, sicut ego dimitto; ne sic dimitteret, id est non dimitteret, quia non dimittis; et noluisti dicere, devitans faciem creditoris. What do you devita? who do you devita? Quo ibis, ubi tu esse possis et Ule non esse? Dicturus is: Quo abibo a spiritu tuo? et a facie tua quo fugiam?

If I ascend in caélum, your illic is; If I descend in infernum, ades (Ps 138,7-8). Quantum potest a Christo debitor fugere, quam ut eat in infernum? Adest iste creditor et ibi. Quid invoices is, nisi quod sequitur? Si assumpsero pennas meas in directum, et volavero in extreme maris (ib., 9); Id est, spe mea finem saeculi meditabor, in praeceptis tuis vivam, duabus alis caritatis attollar. Imple ergo duas alas caritatis. Dilige proximum sicut te ipsum; et non teneas odium, unde fugias creditorem. CAPUT III.—8. Tertium genus paenitentiae luctuosae, pro mortiferis peccatis. Desperatione veniae anima suffocatur.—Restat paenitentiae tertium genus, unde aliquid breviter dicam, ut adiuvante Domino proposita et promissa persolvam. Est paenitentia gravior atque luctuosior, in qua proprie vocantur in Ecclesia paenitentes, remoti etiam a Sacramento altaris participadi, ne accipiiendo indigne, iudicium sibi manducent et bibant. Illa ergo paenitentia luctuosa est. Grave vulnus est: adulterium forte commissum est, forte homicidium, forte aliquod sacrilegium, gravis res, grave vulnus, lethale, mortiferum: sed omnipotens medicus. Iam post suggestionem facti et delectationem et consensionem et perpetrationem, quasi quatriduanus mortuus putet: sed nec ipsum Dominus deseruit, sed clamavit: Lazare, prodi foras (lo 11,43). Cessit voci mise-

mercy: death gave way to life; hell, before the exalted one. Lazarus got up and left the tomb; He was bound, as penitent men are when they confess their sin. They have already come out of death, because they would not confess it if they had not come out. To confess it is to leave the dark and gloomy place. But what does the Lord say to his Church? What you bind on earth will be loosed in heaven. Therefore, when Lazarus came out, the Lord accomplished the good of his mercy by bringing the buried and already putrefied dead to confession; The rest is already done by the ministry of the Church: Untie it and let it go5. But, dearly beloved, no one should propose this type of penance, no one should prepare for it; However, if it happens that you have to suffer it, let no one lose hope. Judas the traitor was not killed so much by the crime committed as by the despair of achieving forgiveness. He was not worthy of mercy; That is why the light did not shine in his heart to run towards the forgiveness of the one he had betrayed, as those who crucified him did. Losing hope, he killed himself, hung himself from a rope and drowned. What he did in his body, the same thing happened in his soul. Wind and air are also called spirit. Just as those who hang themselves cause death by not allowing the spirit—the air—to enter, so those who have lost hope of God's forgiveness hang themselves.

They are overcome internally by the same desperation, so that the Holy Spirit cannot enter to visit them. 9. Pagans usually reproach Christians for the penance that the Church has instituted, which has maintained this Catholic truth against some heresies 6. There were those who taught that penance could not be granted for certain sins; such were excluded from the Church and became heretics. Mother Church does not lose her pious core in the face of any kind of sin. Regarding this, the pagans tend to insult us, without knowing what they are saying, since they have not reached the Word, which makes the tongues of infants loquacious. «You, they say, promote men's sin by promising them forgiveness if they later do penance. This is debauchery, not an exhortation not to sin. Each one exaggerates this statement with as many words as he can and does not remain silent with his tongue, whether loud or stuttering. When we talk to them, even if we defeat them, they do not agree. However, let your charity hear how they must be defeated, because divine mercy has arranged everything in a wonderful way in his Church. They affirm that we give license to sin because we promise the port of penitence. If the entrance to penance were closed, would that sinner not add sins upon sins, all the more so the greater his desperation to achieve forgiveness? In

ricordiae moles sepultutae: cessit mors vitae, cessit infernus superno. Elevatus est Lazarus, processit de tumulo: et ligatus etat, sicut sunt homines in cofessione peccati agents paenítentiam. Iam processerunt a morte: nam non confiterentur, nisi proceedent. Ipsum confiten, ab occulto et a tenebroso I will proceed est. Sed quid Dominus Ecclesiae suae? Quae solveritis, inquit, in tena, soluta erunt et in cáelo (Mt 18,18). Proinde Lazarus coming, quia implevit Dominus misericordiae suae bonum, perducere ad confessionem mortuum latentem, putentem; iam cetera implet Ecclesiae ministerium: Solvite illum, et sinite abire (lo 11,44). Sed, carissimi, hoc genus paenitentiae nemo sibi proponat, ad hoc genus nemo se praeparet: tamen si forte contigerit, nemo desperet. Iudam traditorem non tam scelus quod commisit, quam indulgentiae desesperatio fecit penitus interire. Non erat dignus mi [1559] sericordia, ideo ei non fulsit lumen in corde, ut ad eius indulgentiam concurreret quem tradiderat, sicut illi qui eum crucifixerant; sed desperando se occidit, et laqueo suspendit se, suffocavit se. Quod fecit in corpore suo, hoc factum est in anima ipsius. Spiritus enim dicitur etiam iste ventus aeris huius. Quomodo ergo qui sibi collum ligant, inde se occidunt, quia non ad eos intrat spiritus aeris huius: sic illi qui desperant de indulgen5 See additional note [2]: The mediation of the Church in the granting of forgiveness p.542.

Aunt Dei, ipsa desperatione intus se suffocant, ut eos Spiritus sanctus visitare non possit. 9. Contra Paganos paenitentiae permissione peccandi licentiam ¿tari suggillantes.—Solent inde Christianis Pagani insultare de paenitentia quae instituía est in Ecclesia: et contra nonnullas haereses tenuit Ecclesia catholica istam veritatem de paenitentia agenda. Fuerunt enim qui dicerent, quibusdam peccatis non esse dandam paenítentiam; et exclusi sunt de Ecclesia, et haeretici facti sunt. In quibuscumque peccatis non perdit viscera pia mater Ecclesia. Ergo solent inde etiam Pagani quasi insultare nobis, nescientes quid loquantur; quia ad verbum Dei, quod linguas infantium facit disertas, nondum pervenerunt. Vos, inquiunt, facitis ut peccent homines, cum illis promittitis veniam, si egerint paenítentiam. Dissolutio est ista, non admonitio. In hanc sententiam exaggerant verba, quanta quisque potest; Lingua vel sonanti, vel titubanti, non tacent: tamen et quando eis loquimur, etsi vincantur, non consentiunt. Tamen quomodo vincantur, breviter accipiat Caritas vestra, quia Domini misericordia totum optimal constituit in Ecclesia sua. Dicunt I will give us peccatis licentiam, quia portum paenitentiae pollicemur. Si clauderetur aditus paenitentiae, nonne ille peccator tanta magis adderet peccata peccatis, quanto magis sibi desperaret ignosci? Diceret enim sibi: See the complementary note [5]: Heresies contrary to penance p.543.

In effect, he would say to himself: "Behold, I have sinned, I have committed a crime; there is no longer room for forgiveness; penance is fruitless; I will be condemned; Why not live at ease now? Since I no longer find love there, at least I will satisfy my passion here. Why abstain? There the entrance has been closed to me; What I do not do here, that I will lose, since the future life will not be granted to me. "Why, then, not put myself at the service of my passions, to give them satisfaction and satisfy them, and do what pleases me, even if it is not lawful?" Perhaps one could say to him: "But, wretch, you will be arrested, accused, tortured, punished." Bad men know well that this is how men usually speak and that this is how it is between them, but they notice that many who live badly and criminally live unpunished among their sins; they can hide them, but not redeem what they can hide; redeem until old age a lascivious, blasphemous, sacrilegious, lost life. They do the math for themselves. What do they say? Did not he who committed so many sins live to old age? Don't you notice that that sinner and wicked man died as an old man precisely so that God would show his patience in him, waiting for him to do penance? Therefore the Apostle says: Do you not know that the patience of God leads you to penitence? But he, according to the hardness and impenitence of his heart, stores up wrath for himself against the day of wrath and the revelation of the just judgment of God, who will repay each one according to his works. It is necessary, therefore, that this fear takes hold of the minds; It is necessary that he who wants not to sin

Think to yourself that you have God present not only when you are in public, but also at home; and not only at home, but also in his room, at night, in his bed, in his heart. Therefore, if you eliminate the port of penance, sins will increase with despair. See that those who think that sins increase because the Christian faith offers the port of penance respond nothing. What to say then? Shouldn't God have provided so that, because of the hope of forgiveness, sins would not increase? Just as He has provided so that despair does not increase them, He must have provided so that hope does not increase them either. In truth, just as despair can increase them, so can hope for forgiveness. One can say to oneself: “I will do what I want. God is good, and he will forgive me when I convert." Say to yourself, then: "He will forgive me when I convert"; This is assuming that you have insurance for tomorrow. Does not the exhortation of Scripture go in this direction, which says: Do not delay in turning to the Lord nor defer it from day to day; Suddenly his anger will come and in the time of revenge he will lose you? See, therefore, that the providence of God protected us from one thing and another. So that we would not increase our sins due to lack of hope, he proposed the port of penance, and so that we would not increase them due to excess of hope, he left the day of our death in uncertainty.

Ecce peccaví, ecce scelus admisi, iam mihi veniae nullus est locus; paenitentia infructuosa est, damnandus sum: quare iam non vivo ut flew? Quia ibi non invenio caritatem, hic saltem pascafn cupiditatem. Quare enim me abstineam? Ibi mihi locus omnis clausus est, hic quidouid non fecero, perdo; Quia vita quae post hancfutura est, non mihi dabitur. Ouare ergo non servio libidinibus meis, ut eas irupleam et saturem, et faciam quidquid non licet, sed libet? Diceretur ei fortassis: Sed miser capieris, accusaberis, torqueberis, punieris. Sciunt ista nomines mali ab hominibus dici, et inter homines servari; attendunt multos male et scelerate vivos impunita habere peccata: occultare possunt, redeem quae occultare non possunt; redeem usque in senectutem vitam lascivam, blasphemam, sacrilegam, perditam. Enumerant sibi: Quid? Ile qui tanta fecit, non senex mortuus est? Numquid attendis ideo illum peccatorem et sceleratum senem mortuum, ut ostenderet in illo Deus patientiam, exspectans paenitentiam? Unde Apostolus says: Ignoras quia patien[\560~\tia Dei ad paenitentiam te adducit? Ule autem secundum duritiam cordis sui et cor impaenitens, thesaurizavh sibi iram in die irae et revelationis iusti iudicii Dei, qui reddet unicuique secundum opera sua (Rom 2,4-6). Opus est ergo ut hic timor minds possideat,

opus est ut ille qui peccare non vult, praesentem Deum sibi cogitet, non in publico solum, sed etiam in domo; non in domo solum, thirst et in cubicle, in night, in lecto suo, in corde suo. Ergo si tuleris portum paenitentiae, desperatione augebunt peccata. Ecce nihil dicunt illi, qui putant ideo augeri peccata, quia portus paenitentiae in christiana fide proponitur. Quid ergo? Deus, ne per illam spem indulgentiae rursus augerentur peccata, non dehinc providere debuit? Quomodo enim providit ne desperando augeantur, sic providere debuit ne waiting for augeantur. Quomodo enim revera auget peccata qui desperaverit, sic potest augere peccata et qui veniam speraverit: ut dicat sibi, Faciam quod voló, Deus bonus est, quando me convertero, ignoscet mihi. Ita plan dic tibi, When I convert, ignoscet mihi; Si crastinus dies certus est lubi. Nonne ad hoc te admonet Scriptura, they say: Ne afternoons converted ad Dominum, ñeque differas de die in diem; sudden enim veniet ira eius, et in tempore vindictae disperdet te? (Eccli 5,8-9). Ecce ad utrumque vigilavit pro nobis providentia Dei. Ne desperando augeamus peccata, propositus est paenitentiae portus: rursus ne sperando augeamus, datus est dies mortis incertus.
Topic: Exhortation to neophytes. Location: Hippo, Leontian Basilica. Date: Eighth Sunday of Easter. Beginning of the ministry.

1. May my word as a caring shepherd stimulate the ears and minds of all those whom my pastoral care embraces! However, now it is addressed particularly to you, whose recent spiritual infancy is marked by the cradle of the sacraments of regeneration. Above all, the divine word caresses you through the apostle Peter: Therefore, he said, lay aside all evil, all deceit, flattery, envy, detraction: like newborn children, desire rational and innocent milk, so that you may grow in it to salvation, if you have tasted how sweet the Lord is. I am a witness that you have enjoyed it, since I myself have served you that softness by acting as a nurse. Having heard this admonition, act in imitation of holy childhood; Put away evil, fraud, flattery, envy and detraction. You must maintain this innocence, without losing it as you grow up. What is evil but the desire to harm? What does deception consist of if not doing one thing and simulating another? What is flattery but seduction through false praise? What is envy but hate SERMO IN
DIE OCTAVARUM INFANTIUM: QUOS EXHORTATUR VERBIS PETRI APOSTOLI, "DEPOSITA ERGO OMNI MALITIA", ETC.

CAPUT I. — 1. Baptize them exhortatur. Innocentia morum retinenda. Humilitas sectanda.—Omnium quidem aures et mentes, quos cura nostra complectitur, solliciti pastoris sermo compellat: verumtamen ad vos proprie nunc dirigitur, quorum recens infantia spiritualis generationis Sacramentorum ibabulis insignitur. Vobis enim máxime per apostolum Petrum sic divinum blanditur eloquium: Deposita ergo, inquit, omni malitia et omni dolo et adulatione et invidia et detractione, tanquam moda nati infantes rationabile et innocens lac concupiscite; ut in illo crescatis in salutem, si gustastis quoniam dulcís est Dominus (1 Petr 2,1-3). Proinde quia gustastis, nos testes sumus: nos vobis hanc suavitatem nutricis officio ministravimus. Agite itaque admoníti sanctae instar infantiae, deponite malitiam, dolum, adulationem et invidiam et detractionem. Hanc innocentiam sic tenere debentis, ut eam crescendo non amittatis. Quid est malitia, [1561] nisi nocendi amor? Quid est dolus, nisi aliud agere et alíud simulare? Quid est adulatio, nisi fallad laude seductio? Quid est invidia, nisi odium felicitatis alienae? Quid is

to other people's happiness? What is detraction if not rebuke that is more scathing than truthful? Evil delights in the evil of others; Envy is also tormented by the good of others; Idol makes the heart double; flattery of the language; Detraction violates fame. But the innocence of this your holiness, since it is the daughter of love, does not rejoice in evil, but in the truth. It is simple as the dove and clever as the serpent; It is not moved by the desire to harm, but to protect oneself from those who harm. I exhort you to it, for to such belongs the kingdom of heaven, that is, to the humble, to the infants in spirit. Do not despise it, do not hate it. This simplicity is typical of the greats; Pride, on the other hand, is the false greatness of the weak, which, when it takes over the mind, lifting it up brings it down; By inflating it, it empties it, and by extending it so much, it breaks it. The humble cannot harm; The proud cannot not harm. I speak of that humility that does not want to stand out among perishable things, but rather thinks of something truly eternal, where it must reach not with its own strength, but with help. She cannot wish evil on anyone, because it does not increase her good either. On the other hand, pride immediately breeds envy. What envious person is there who does not want evil for the one whose good torments him? Consequently, envy logically engenders evil, from which comes deception, flattery and detraction and all evil deeds that you do not want to suffer at the hands of anyone. So, if you maintain this pious humility which Holy Scripture shows to be detractio, nisi mordacior, quam veracior reprenso? Malitia malo delectatur alieno: invidentia et bono cruciatur alieno: dolus duplicat cor: adulatio duplicat linguam: detractio vulnerat famem. Huius autem vestrae innocentia sanctitatis, quoniam filia est caritatis, non gaudet super iniquitate, con gaudet autem veritati (1 Cor 13:6). Simplex ut columba, et sic astuta ut serpens (cf. Mt 10:16), non studio nocendi, sed nocentem cavendi. CAPUT II.—Ad hanc vos hortoror. Talium est enim regnum caelorum (Mt 19:14), humilium scilicet, hoc est, spiritualiter parvulorum. Non contemnatis, non abhorreatis. Magnorum is this pusillitas. Superbia vero fallax infirmorum est magnitudeo; quae ubi mentem possederit, erigendo deicit, inflando evacuat, distendendo dissipat. Humilis esse non potest nocens, superbus esse non potest innocens.

Humilitatem illam loquor, quae non vult perituris rebus excellere, sed aeternum aliquid veraciter cogitat, quo non suis viribus, sed adiuta perveniat. Haec malum cuiusquam velle non potest, quo nequáquam bonum eius augetur. Porro autem superbia continuo parit invidiam. Quis vero sit invidus, qui non ei malum velit, cuius bono cruciatur? Ergo et invidia parit consequenter malitiam: unde proceedit et dolus et adulatio et detractio, et omne opus malum, quod pati nolis ab alio. Pia itaque humilitate servata, quae in
Exhortation to neophytes

a holy childhood, you will be sure of achieving the immortality of the blessed: Of such is the kingdom of heaven. 2. Now, he who is not arrogant before men, much less should he be contumacious before God, since, if what we do not want others to do to us is not to be done to anyone and there is no man who wants to suffer the disobedience of a subordinate of his, how much more must we guard against being before God what we do not want others to be before us! Those who believe that it is enough not to do to others what they do not want done to them deceive their souls, and they corrupt themselves with such a lustful life that they try to do to God what they do not want any man to do to them. Nor do those same people who with miserable blindness desecrate the house of God within themselves want anyone to tear down their house, deaf to the words of the Apostle, who cries: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone desecrates the temple of God, God will destroy him, for the temple of God, which is you, is holy. Let no one be fooled. How is it that they think they maintain their innocence before men, when they harm themselves so much that they lack God as an inhabitant of them and will punish them as an avenger? Here it also happens that, fallen and scattered by harmful pleasures, they not only cease to be temples of God, but become ruins in which

Evil demons live there, to whom they begin to make supplications and worship, and, as it is said, for them the after will be worse than the before. As he previously warned you, regenerated from immortal semen, from the perverse desires to harm, by which men are done with what they do not want, so he then freed you from the clumsy and illicit carnal pleasures and nefarious sacrileges, by which men do not seem to harm other men by not doing to them what they do not want; But, by not obeying God, to whom everything is submitted, they do to the Lord of lords what they do not want their servants to do to them. The apostle Peter himself addresses you when he says: Having suffered Christ in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same thought. "Since he who has died to the flesh ceases to sin, so that the rest of his life in the flesh is guided not by human desires, but by the will of God. It is enough that in the past you have satisfied the desires of the Gentiles by living in lasciviousness, pleasures, feasting, drunkenness and in shameful idolatry. It is enough, then, that in the past you have served the muddy works of sin, such as the domination of the Egyptians. The sea Red, that is, the baptism of Christ consecrated with his blood, has already overthrown the true Pharaoh and caused the Egyptians to perish; fear nothing regarding past sins, as if they were enemies that pursue you from behind. For the rest, think about crossing the desert of this life and reaching the land of promise, the heavenly Jerusalem, the land of the living;

Scripturis sanctis sancta probatur infantia, securi eritis de immortalitate beatorum: Talium est enim regnum caelorum (Mt 19:14). 2. Erga Deum multo maxime servanda innocentia. In Israelitis data baptizatis figura vitae chrístianae.—Porro qui superbus in homines non est, multo máxime adversus Deum contumax esse non debent: quoniam si non est alicui faciendum quod quisque ab alio pati non vult, et nullus hominum vult inoboedientem pati eum qui suo iuri subditus fuerit; quanto magis cavendum est, ne in Deum quisquam talis existat, qualem in se existenre hominem non vult? CAPUT III.—Fallunt proinde animas suas qui sufficere existimant, si quod sibi fieri nolunt, nulli hominum faciant, seseque vita luxuriosa ita corrumpunt, ut Deo faceré conentur quod sibi ab nomine fieri nolunt. Neque enim volunt a quoquam pervertí domum suam, qui in se ipsis domum Dei miserabili caecitate pervertunt, surdi adversus Apostolum clamantem: Nescitis quia templum Dei estis, et Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis? Si quis autem templum Dei corrumpit, corrumpet illum Deus. Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos (1 Hear 3,16-17). Nemo fails. Quid ergo se putant servare circa alios homines innocentiam suam, cum sibi ita noceant, ut Deo careant habitatore, et puniantur ultore? Hinc [1562] etiam fit ut per noxias voluptates lapsi et effusi, non solum templa Dei esse desinant, verum etiam ruinae fiant, in quibus

inhabitant mala daemonia, quibus supplicare, et quae colere incipiunt: fiuntque lilis, ut dictum est, posteriora deteriorates prioribus (Luke 11,26). Topic: Exhortation to religious people. Location: Unknown. Date: Before the year 410.

1. In the gospel read, the Lord indicated to us that whoever believes in him, believes in the one who sent him. True faith assures that the Savior of the world has been sent to us, since Christ is preached by Christ himself, that is, the body of Christ spread throughout the world. He, it is true, was in heaven, but he said to the persecutor who tormented him on earth: Why are you persecuting me? In this way the Lord expressed that he was also in us. Thus all of him grows, because as he is in us here, so we are in him there. This union is the fruit of charity. The same one who is our head is the savior of his body. Thus, Christ preaches Christ, the body preaches his head, and the head protects (1 Petr 4:3). Audite et apostolum Paulum: Humanum dico propter injirmitatem carnis vestrae. Sicut enim exhihuistis memhra vestra I will serve immunditiae et iniquitati ai iniustitiam: sic nunc exhíbete memhra vestra I will serve iustitiae in sanctificationem (Rom 6,19).

So he has no money that he can or dares to call his own. You see the hospital whose construction was planned to be completed. I imposed it on him, I ordered it on him. He obeyed me very willingly, and, as you see, it is now a reality. In the same way, by my order he built the Basilica of the Eight Martyrs with the means that God gives him through you. He started it with the money that had been given to the Church for the hospital; After having begun to build it, the pious people who wanted their names to be inscribed in heaven helped him to the best of their ability, and so it was built. He will not continue to be a clergyman either. It is true that I had said, and I am aware of it, that if they did not want to accept living in common with me, I would not take away their clergy, that they could support themselves and live apart and serve God as they wanted. But I put before their eyes the great evil of falling from purpose. I preferred to have lame people than cry dead people. Indeed, whoever is hypocritical is dead. Therefore, in the same way that I affirmed that I would not remove the clergy from anyone who wanted to remain apart and live on his own, so now I affirm that, since, with the help of God, this common life pleased them, whoever I find living in hypocrisy, whoever I find possessing something of his own, I will not allow him to make a will, but I will delete him from the list of clerics. Appeal against me to a hundred councils; sail against me wherever; certainly be where you can; The Lord will help me so that he does not become a clergyman where I am a bishop. You have heard it, you have heard it. But I hope in our God and in his mercy that as they have joyfully accepted this disposition of mine, they will maintain it holy and faithfully. 15. I have said that none of the presbyters who live with me have anything of their own; among them is also Barnabas. I have also heard that there have been no shortage of rumors regarding him; First of all, he bought a farm from my dear and honorable son Eleusino. That is false; He did not sell it, but rather donated it to the monastery. I am a witness of this. What else do you want to know, I don't know. I am a witness that he did not sell it, but that he

donated. But at the same time that it is not believed that he could donate it, it is believed that he sold it. Blessed is the man who performed an action so good that he deserves no credit. At least now, believe him and stop giving an easy ear to the detractors. I have already said it: I am a witness. It was also said about him that in the year in which he was in charge of the administration of the Church's assets, he contracted debts on purpose so that, when I wanted him to pay them, I would give him the Victory estate; as if he had said to me: "In order to pay my debts, give me the land of Victory for ten years." This is also false. But the rumor was born for a reason. He contracted debts that he had to pay. I have paid them in part, as I could. He still had something left that he owed to the monastery that God built through him. Since that debt still remained, we began to look for ways to pay it. No one offered to rent the property, paying more than forty solids beforehand. But we saw that the farm could give more to pay off the debt sooner, and I entrusted it to him, so that the brothers would not claim the profits from the rent, but rather whatever she produced with its fruits would be used to pay off the debt. It's a matter of trust. The priest is willing to put it in the hands of others to return what has been obtained from the fruits to the brothers. Someone from you or someone from those who made such accusations come forward to entrust him with this mission. There are pious people among you who felt pain based on a false rumor.

Theme: Praise of peace. Place: Carthage. Date: May of the year 411. 1. It is time to exhort your charity, according to the strength that the Lord gives me, to love peace and to beg it from the Lord. Be peace our beloved and friend; Let our hearts be the chaste bed to lie with her; May your company be a confident rest and a union without bitterness; May your embrace be sweet and friendship inseparable. It is more difficult to praise peace than to possess it. In fact, if we want to praise her, we desire the strength to do so, we search for thoughts and weigh the words; On the contrary, if we want to possess it, we will have it and possess it without any work. Those who love peace deserve praise; However, those who hate it must be pacified, taught and kept silent, rather than provoked by reproach. The true lover of peace also loves its enemies. In the same way that, if you love this light, you do not get angry at the blind, but rather you pity them, because you become aware of the good that you enjoy and, when you contemplate the great good of which they are deprived, you consider them worthy of mercy, and, if you had goods, science, medicines, you would rather rush to heal them than to condem

Apud Carthaginem habitus, instant collatione cum Donatistis, anno 411, circiter 15 diem maii 1. Pacis laus.—Tempus est exhortan Caritatem vestram, pro viribus quas Dominus donat, ad pacem amandam, et pro pace Dominum deprecandum. Sit ergo pax dilecta nostra et árnica, cum qua sit castum cubile cor nostrum; cum qua sit fida requies et non amarum consortium, cum qua sit dulcís complexus et inseparabilis amicitia. Pacem laudare difficilius est, quam habere. Si enim eam laudare volumus, vires optmus, sensus quaerimus, verba libramus: si autem habere volumus, sine aliquo labore habemus et possidemus. Laudandi sunt qui amant pacem: qui autem oderunt, melius interimdocendo ac tacendo pacandi, quam vituperando provocandi. Verus pacis amator inimicorum eius amator est. Quemadmodum enim, si luzm istam amares, caecis non irascereris, sed eos doleres; quale enim bonum tu caperes, nosses, et ideo quanto bono illi fraudarentur conspiciens, mercy tibi digni viderentur; et si opes assets, si artem, si medicamentum, potius ad eos healing cur-

nar them. In the same way, if you are a lover of peace, whoever you are, pity those who do not love what you love nor have what you have. What you love is such that you are not envious that another possesses it with you. Have peace with you and do not reduce your possession. If you love anything earthly, it is difficult not to envy the person who owns it. If perhaps the idea comes to you of dividing your lands so that they praise your goodness, so that love is proclaimed even in what refers to these temporary things; If, then, you want to share with your friend an earthly possession of yours, such as a property, a house, or something of the like, you share it with someone, admit him into your company, and rejoice with him. Maybe you even think about a third or a fourth, and you start to look at how many there is room for or how many it is for, that is, how many can live in the house or feed themselves from the fields; and you say to yourself: «The fifth no longer fits; the sixth cannot dwell with us; How can such a small field feed a seventh person? Thus, the rest are excluded, not because of you, but because of the narrowness. Love peace, have peace, possess peace, conquer as many as you can so that they possess peace; It will be all the more spacious the more there are possessors. An earthly house does not admit many inhabitants: the possession of peace grows with their multiplication. 2. What a great good it is to love peace! That is, possessing it. Who doesn't want what they love to increase? If you want to be at peace with a few, small will be your peace. If you want it

grow this possession, add possessors to it. Indeed, brothers: what is the value of what I said: "To love peace is a good and to love it is to already have it"? What voice can praise or what heart can think: "To love is to possess"? Consider all the other things for whose love men are consumed. Think of someone who loves land, silver, gold, many children, beautiful and decorated houses, lush and extremely beautiful meadows. —Do you love these things? —He loves them. But does he have them because he loves them? Someone who loves them all may be completely devoid of them. When he does not possess them, he loves them and burns with love to possess them; but, when he begins to own them, he is tormented by the fear of losing them. Love honor, love power. How many private men long to acquire dignities, and often their last day comes before they achieve what they love! What, then, is the value of what you can have just by loving it? What you love cannot be acquired with money, nor do you have to look for someone to support you to achieve it. Love peace in the same place you are, and you will have what you love. It is something that belongs to the heart, and you don't communicate it to your friends like you give them bread. In fact, if you want to distribute bread to them, the more there are those to whom it is given, the more what is distributed decreases. But peace is similar to that bread that multiplied in the hands of the Lord's disciples when they broke and distributed it. 3. Have peace, brothers. If you want to attract others

reres, quam damnandos: ita si pacis amator es, quisquís es, miserere eum qui non amat quod amas, qui non habet quod habes. Talis quippe est res quam diligis, ut non invideas compossessori tuo. Theme: Peace and love. Place: Carthage. Date: May of the year 411.

1. The supplications of your holiness support the concern that I take for you, for my enemies and for yours, for the salvation of all, for rest, for common peace, for the unity that the Lord commanded and that the Lord loves, so that it may be the theme of my address to you and a reason for joy with you. In fact, if we must always speak of peace and love, since we always love, much more must we do so at these moments, when peace is so loved that, put in a position to love it and stay with it, those to whom we do not return evil for evil, with whom - as it is written - we are peaceful, although they hate peace, want to tear us down for no reason because we address them; Those who are like this oscillate between the love of peace and the confusion caused by modesty, and, not wanting to be defeated, they cannot remain undefeated. If they do not want to be defeated by truth, they are defeated by error. Oh, if only love and not animosity controlled them! His defeat would be his victory. We love the Catholic Church, we remain in it and defend it; to SERMO

1. Curam nostram pro uobis, et pro inimicis nostris et uestris, pro salute omnium, pro quiete, pro pace communi, pro unitate quam dominus iussit, dominus diligit, adiuuent preces sanctitatis uestrae, ut de illa identidem et ad uos loquamur, et uobiscum gaudeamus. Etenim de pace et caritate loqui, si semper amamus, semper debenmus, multo magis ergo isto tempore, quando pax sic amatur, ut in periculo eius amandae et tenendae constituti illi, quibus malum pro malo non reddimus (cf. Rom 12:17), et cum quibus, sicut scriptum est, odio habentibus pacem sumus pacifici (cf. Ps. 119,7), et quia loquimur eis, debellare nos uolunt gratis: illi ergo qui tales sunt, periclitantur inter amorem pacis et confusionem pozoris, nec id agunt, cum uinci nolunt, ut inuicti sint. Who enim uinci a ueritate nolunt, ab errore uincuntur. Or if those caritas potius quam animositas surpasses! Inde uctores ieront, unde uicti essent. We invite her enemies to make peace and reconcile with her not on the basis of human opinions, but with divine testimonies. What should I do with someone who shouts in favor of a part and fights against the whole? Is it not good for him to be defeated, since, if he is defeated, he will have the whole, while, if he wins, he will remain in part? Better, if he believes that he wins, because only the truth wins. The victory of truth is love. 2. What need do I have, brothers, to praise with many words, and my own words, the Catholic Church, which bears fruit and grows throughout the entire world? We have the words of the Lord in favor of her and of us. The Lord - it is written - said to me: «You are my son, today I have begotten you. Ask me, and I will give you the towns as an inheritance, and your possession will reach to the ends of the earth. So, brothers, why do we litigate for possession instead of reading the holy tables? 2 Suppose we have appeared before the judge. The lawsuit is about possession; a dispute that is not generated by the desire to litigate, but by love. Furthermore, he who fights for an earthly possession does so to exclude his adversary from it; us to include it. He who fights for an earthly possession, when he hears his adversary say: "I want to possess it," responds: "I won't allow it." I, on the other hand, say to my brother: "I want you to possess it with me"; he, litigating, eius, non humanis opinionibus, sed díuinis testimoniis, amamus, tenemus, defendimus. Quid cum illo agam, qui pro parte clamat, et contra totum litigat? Nonne bonum illi est uinci, quia si uictus fuerit, totum tenebit; if uícerit, in part remanebit? immo si uincere sibi uidebitur, nam non uincit nisi ueritas: uictoria ueritatis est caritas. 2. Quid ergo uobis, fratres, ecclesiam catholicam toto orbe [145] terrarum fructificantem atque crescentem commendem multis uerbis, et meis. Habemus uerba domini pro illa, et pro nobis. Dominus, inquit, dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te. Postula a me, et dabo Ubi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam fines terrae (Ps 2,78). Quare ergo, fratres, de possessione litigamus, et non potius sanctas tabulas recitamus? Venisse nos opinentur * ad iudicem. De possessione contentio est: et haec contentio non litis, sed dilectionis est. Denique litigator terrenae possessionis ad hoc litigat, ut excludat aduersarium: nos ut intromittamus.

Litigator terrenae possessionis, cum audierit aduersarium dicentem: Possidere uolo; respond: Not allowed. Ego autem fratridico: Possideas mecum uolo; ille litigando dicit: Nolo. That is, in favor of Donato's party, limited to Africa alone, against the Church, spread throughout the empire and even outside it. He is referring to Scripture, considered God's testament. See complementary note [8]: Scripture as God's testament p.548, b] opinemur PL.

He answers: "I don't want to." I am not afraid, then, that the Lord will despise or reproach me like those brothers or that brother who addressed him in public to say: Lord, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me. You see that I read the tables of this possession; but not to keep her alone, but to convince my brother that he does not want to have her with me. Here are the tables, brother: Ask of me, he said, and I will give you the towns as an inheritance, and your possession will reach to the ends of the earth. This was said to Christ; therefore it has been said to us, who are members of Christ. Why do you run in one part? Why do you stay in one part? Keep everything that appears in the tables. You seek to know between which and which your possession is, in the same way that possessors search in documents with whom they border on one side or another. Whoever gave you everything left nothing that could border on what is yours. 3. Listen to another testimony of the holy tables. Of Christ the Lord, in the person of Solomon, it is said: Dominará de Non itaque timeo ne contemnat me dominus et corripiat, (1587) sicut illos fratres, uel illum fratrem, qui eum interpellauit in populo, et ait: Domine, dic fratri meo, ut diuidat mecum hereditatem (Luke 12:13). Quaeris Inter quem et quem possideas, quomodo solent instrumentis quaeri possessores, Inter quos sint affines. Qui tibi dedit omnes fines, nullos dimisit affines. 3. sea ​​to sea and from it river to the ends of the globe of the earth. Before him the Ethiopians will prostrate themselves and their enemies will lick the ground. A thousand names, as many tears. Going after a man, they will deprive you of such a great inheritance, of which you have heard little: From sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the globe of the earth. Why don't you stay with her? Because you love a man. What is a man but a rational animal taken from the earth? That is why you are an enemy of inheritance: because you lick the earth. Refuse that; Stop licking the earth, to put your hope in the one who made heaven and earth. This is our hope, these our testimonies: The God of gods has spoken, and called to the earth from sunrise to sunset. Don't stay on earth; but go to where the land has been called. 4. Noli lingere terram, ut spem ponas in eum qui fecit caelum et terram. Haec spes nostra, haec testimonia: Deus deorum dominus locutus est, et uocauit terram, a solis ortu usque ad occasum (Ps 49,1). Noli remanere in terra, sed quo ocata est terra. 4. Et quis potest omnia de tabulis sanctis possessionis huius testimonia recitare? Vidit haec ecclesia, quod dixit in psalmo. Modo audistis, recentia uerba sunt in auribus et cordibus uestris: The first two names, Gaius and Lucius, already appeared in sermon 42,3; Perhaps they do not refer to any specific character, but to anyone. end of total consummation. What does it mean: I saw the end of the total consummation? Consummation: consummation as perfection and not as consumption. End: the end as perfection, not as abolition. I saw the end of the total consummation: your commandment is very spacious. I saw the end of the total consummation_ What end is it? Your commandment is very spacious. Of course, say with me: The end of the precept is... You have all said what you have always heard, not without fruit. The end of the precept is the love that arises from a pure heart. End that you, says perfection, not consumption. This end is spacious, since it is identified with the commandment of God, to which it is said: Your commandment is very spacious. I give you a new commandment: that you love one another. Consider the breadth of this commandment. Where is its width? Perhaps in the flesh? More like in the heart. In fact, if it were also spacious in the flesh, you, attentive listeners, would not suffer hardships. Its width is in the heart. See where it is spacious, if you have anything to do with it, and from there listen to the Apostle, who informs you how spacious the commandment of love is: The love of God has spread in your hearts. He did not say that it had been included, but rather disseminated. The word "include" sounds narrow, while "disseminate" makes us think of breadth. Therefore, your commandment is very broad. Lord our God, give your approval to the invitation that we have addressed to our brothers in response to that Omnis consummationis uidi finem (ib., 96). Quid est: Omnis consummationis uidi finem? Consummationis, perfectionis non consumptionis; et finem, perfectionis non abolitionis. Omnisd consummationis uidi finem: latum mandatum tuum ualde &. Omnis consummationis uidi finem. Who is this? Latum mandatum tuum ualde. Finis enim praecepti est, iam uos dicite mecum e. Omnes dixistis, quod non infructuose semper audistis. Finis praecepti est caritas de corde pure (1 Tim 1,5). Finis quo perfícimur, non quo consumimur. Iste finis latus est, quia mandatum dei est et cui f dictum est: Latum mandatum tuum ualde. Mandatum nouum do uobis, ut uos inuicem diligatis (lo 13,34). Vide latitudinem mandati huius. Vbi latum est? Numquid in flesh? In corde potius. Nam si et in carne latum esset, auditores studiosi, anxieties non pateremini. In corde latum est.

Vbi latum est uide, si situ unde uideas, et hinc audi apostolum, quam latum est mandatum caritatis: Caritas autem dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris (Rom 5,5). Non dixit, even, sed diffusa. Verbum enim quod est, even, quasi anxieties sonat: quod est diffusa, latitudinem insinuat. Latum ergo mandatum tuum ualde. amplitude. Do you want to be bishops? Be it with us. Don't the people want two bishops? Be brothers with us in the inheritance. Let us not put impediments to the peace of Christ with our honors. I know, therefore, that what the Apostle said will not happen to them: For whoever resists authority, resists what is established by God. Princes do not cause fear to those who do good, but to those who do evil. Let us avoid all tumult and every occasion of uproar. Perhaps you say: "We have well engraved in our minds what we have to do." What else can I add to you? The fruitful fruits of piety. We argue in your place; you pray for us. As I have already indicated to you again, also help your prayers with fasting and almsgiving. Lend them those wings with which they can fly towards God. Applied to that activity, perhaps you will be more useful to us than we are to you. None of us boasts about ourselves in this discussion; all our hope is in God. It comes down to this: what is mercy? Nothing else but a certain misery contracted in the heart. Mercy gets its name from the pain for a miserable person: the word includes two others: misery and heart, misery and heart. We speak of mercy when the misery of others touches and shakes your heart. Who is there who does not find joy in the harmony between brothers? And, something worthy of regret, that great thing is very rare among men; It is something that everyone praises and very few guard. Blessed are those who embrace against themselves what they are forced to praise even in others. There is no brother who does not praise the fact that brothers agree. Why is it that harmony between them is so difficult? Because they litigate over earthly matters, because they want to be earth. Sinful man heard from the beginning: You are earth, and to the earth you will return. So let us discuss and examine the words that, on the contrary, the righteous should hear. If it has been rightly said to the sinner: You are earth, and to earth you will return, it is rightly said to the just; "Heaven you are, and to heaven you will go." Are not just heavens? Of the evangelists it has been said very clearly: The heavens proclaim the glory of God. That what has been said refers to them is sufficiently indicated by what follows: And the firmament, he says, announces the works of his hands. Those whom he called heaven he also called firmament. The day communicates the word to the day and the night proclaims science to the night. There are no languages ​​or words in which their voices cannot be heard. Whose voices? You ask, and you find none other than those of the heavens. They refer to the apostles, the announcers of the truth. Therefore it continues like this: Throughout the land his

sound, and his words reached the ends of the earth. When the Holy Spirit descended on them and God began to inhabit the heaven that he made of the earth, filled with the Holy Spirit, they spoke the languages ​​of all peoples. That is why it was said: There are no languages ​​or words in which their voices are not heard. And how from then on they were sent to preach the Gospel to all peoples: Their sound was heard throughout the land, and their words reached to the ends of the earth. Whose words? Those of the heavens, to whom it is rightly said: "You are heaven, and to heaven you will go," just as it is said to the sinner: You are earth, and to earth you will return. 2. Litigare quis censendus.—Ecce quale consilium Dominus fratribus dedit dissidentibus, quo concordes essent, ut carerent cupiditate, et continuo implerentur veritate. Inveniamus ergo talem hereditatem. Quamdiu loquimur de concordia tierrarum fratrum, quae rare est, quae suspecta est, quae difficilis est? Loquamur de illa fratrum concordia, quae vera esse debent, et potest. Fratres sint Christiani orones, fratres sint fideles omnes, fratres sint

the Mother Church by the Holy Spirit; be brothers, they also possess the inheritance that is to be given and not divided. His inheritance is God himself. He whose inheritance they are is, at the same time, their inheritance. How come they are your inheritance? Ask me, and I will give you the towns as your inheritance. How is he their inheritance? The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup. In this inheritance, harmony is safeguarded, it is never litigated over. Any other inheritance is acquired through litigation, it is lost by those means. Men who don't want to lose her avoid litigation. They don't litigate even when they give that impression. Sometimes they seem to get into litigation or it is thought that they are litigating when they want to look out for their brothers. See how concordant their litigation is, how peaceful, how benign, how just, how faithful. In fact, we give the impression of litigating with the Donatists, but we do not litigate, since he who wants evil for his adversary litigates; He litigates who wants his adversary to suffer decrease in order to increase himself; that the other lacks, to add to one's own. We are not one of these. You who have been reconquered from the heart of the division also know it; You know that this strife is not a strife, because it is not malicious, because it does not seek the adversary's detriment, but rather his gain. We wanted, in effect, those with whom we were in dispute, or rather gave the impression of being in dispute, to win with us; not that they suffered losses to enrich us. Our cry is different from that of that brother nati ex Deo et ex visceribus matris Ecclesiae per Spiritum sanctum: fratres sint, habeant et ipsi hereditatem dandam, et non dividendam. Hereditas eorum Deus ipse est. Cuius sunt ipsi hereditas, ipse est vicissim eorum hereditas. Quomodo sunt ipsi eius hereditas? Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam (Ps 2,8). How is Ule ipsorum hereditas? Dominus pars hereditatis meae, et calicis mei (Ps 15,5). In hac hereditate concordia custoditur: pro hac hereditate non litigationtur. Alia hereditas litigating acquiritur: ista litigating amittitur. Nolentes homines hanc hereditatem will lose, vitant litigare. Et quando forte videntur litigare, non litigant. Be forte videntur litigare, aut putantur litigare, cum volunt fratribus consulere. Videte quam consors sit eorum litigatio, quam paci[1594]fica, quam benigna, quam iusta, quam fidelis. Nam nos litigare videmur cum Donatistis: sed non litigamus.

Ule enim litigat, qui adversa suo male vult; litigat ille qui adversarium suum vult detrimentum pati, se augmentum; illi aliquid decedere, yes I will agree. Non sic sumus nos. Scitis et vos, scitis qui extra unitatem litigatis; scitis et vos, qui ex divisione acquisiti estis: scitis quia ista lis non est talis lis, quia non est malévola, quia non tendit in detrimentum adversarii, sed magis in lucrum. Volebamus enim eos, cum quibus litigare videbamur, vel adhuc videmur, acquirere nobiscum; I will not lose, ut nos acquiramur. Denique alia vox nostra est, quam Fuit fratris illius,

That this is what we desire is also attested by the public records'; That this is what we wanted is shown not only by the speeches given, but also by the letters we delivered to them. Do you love being bishops? Be it with us. We hate, detest, abhor and anathematize nothing else in you more than human error. We detest, I have said, human error, not divine truth; We recognize what you have from God and we correct the evil you have. I recognize in the deserter the sign of my God, the sign of my general, the distinctive sign of my king. I search, I find, I get moving, I approach, I take the hand, I lead and I correct the deserter, but I do not destroy the sign. For those who notice it, for those who see it, this is not litigation, but love. We said that, within the one Church, the brothers could live in harmony for the sake of peace; Fraternal concord is, in fact, a beautiful thing. 2. “There cannot be two bishops at the same time.” We said that both should sit in the same basilica; one in the chair, another as a guest; that one would sit in the Christian chair; the other, next to it, in that of the heretic, qui interpellavit Christum in terra ambulantem. Nam et nos interpellamus eum in hac causa in cáelo sedentem: et non dicimus: Domine, dic fratri meo, ut dividedat mecum hereditatem (Luke 12,13); sed: Dec fratri meo, ut teneat mecum hereditatem. 5. Catholicorum propositum et voluntas pro Ecclesiae pace.—Quoniam hoc volumus et publica Gesta testantur: quoniam hoc voluerimus, Indices sunt non tantum sermones, sed litterae nostrae datae ad illos. Episcopatum amatis? Nobiscum habete. In vobis nihil odimus, nihil detestamur, nihil exsecramur, nihil anathemamus, nisi humanum errorem. Signum Domini mei, signum Imperatoris mei, characterem Regis mei in desertore agnosco; quaero, invenio, admoveo, accesso, apprehendo, duco, corrigo desertorem, non violo characterem. If you want to warn, if you want to attend, hoc non est litigare, sed amare. Diximus posse in an Ecclesia, pacis causa, esse fratres concordes: speciosa enim res est concordia fratrum.

Caecilianus inventus innocens.—Salva ergo causa Ecclesiae, confirmata, et incommutabiliter fixa ac stabilita, tanquam supra fundamentum petrae, quam portae inferorum non vincant: hac ergo salva, venimus et ad causam Caeciliani, iam securi quidquid ille inveniretur admisisse. Forte enim, si ut homo inveniretur in aliqua culpa, nos litigaturi eramus, ut propter culpam unius hominis damnandi aut rebaptizandi iudicaremur?

Having preserved the cause of the Church, which is in no way affected by Caecilian's sin, since neither Caecilian's justice crowns the Church nor his guilt condemns it, let us also examine his personal situation. We undertook its examination as one would examine the case of a brother, not as that of a father or mother. Our father is God; our mother, the Church; Ceciliano was or is a brother; yes well, a good brother; yes bad, a bad brother, but always a brother. If we found that he was innocent, in what situation are you who have succumbed to human slander? If, on the contrary, it turns out to have been guilty, even in this way we are not defeated, because we achieve the unity of the Church, which is undefeated. Let us admit that he is found guilty: I condemn the man, but I do not abandon the Church. That's what we did and what we said; From now on, we will no longer read his name in celebrations alongside those of the bishops we consider faithful and innocent. We have done nothing else 3. Should the entire world be renamed because of Caecilian? With this firm assurance their cause began to be examined. He was found innocent, he was found a desired target of slander. He was convicted twice in his absence and three times acquitted in his presence; condemned by a group, acquitted by ecclesiastical truth 4. All this was read and proven. They were asked if they had anything to argue against. All subways exhausted

fugitives of their slander, when they could no longer provide anything against such obvious documents or against the innocence of Cecilian himself, a sentence was passed against them. And yet they claim to have won. Victory, but yourselves, so that Christ may possess you; defeat them who redeemed them. 7. However, there are many who have given us cause for joy. Many of them were successfully defeated, because in reality they were not defeated. Human error was defeated and man was saved. In effect, the doctor does not confront the patient; and, if the sick person collaborates with the doctor, the fever is defeated and the sick person heals. The doctor seeks nothing else but to conquer, and the same thing the fever. The patient remains as if in the middle of both. If the doctor wins, the sick person heals; If the fever overcomes, the patient dies. In our struggle, the doctor fought for our health, and the patient for the fever. Those who heeded the doctor's advice conquered and defeated the fever. Now we see them healthy and happy in church. Before they blasphemed against us because they did not recognize us as brothers; the fever had disturbed his mind. But, even though they hated us and were cruel to us, we loved them and put ourselves at the service of such cruel patients. We resisted, we fought and we gave the impression of litigating, but we loved them. Those who serve such patients find them annoying; It is a nuisance that brings health.

8. But sometimes we find lazy men who tell us: -It is true, Lord, it is true; There is nothing to say against it. "Then what?" Come on, come. —My father died among them and my mother was buried there. —You have named two people, one dead and one buried. But you still live, you still have someone to talk to. Your parents were Christians in Donato's party; Their parents may also have been Christians, but their grandparents or great-great-grandparents were certainly pagans. Were the first to become Christians cold towards the truth, despite their parents having been pagans? Did they follow the authority of their parents and not rather put the living Christ before their dead parents? Therefore, if here is true unity, outside of which you will necessarily die forever, why do you want to follow your dead parents, dead to you and to God? What are you saying? Reply. —You tell the truth; there is nothing to oppose. What do you want me to do? I don't know what custom has such men imprisoned. They are lethargic, they suffer from the opposite disease, they have to die in their sleep. Others are frantic, angry. In fact, the lethargic person, although he must die, at least does not bother those who care for him. The frantic, who have lost their minds, are truly annoying; Demented and furious, they wander armed here and there looking for whom to kill and whose eyes to remove. We have received news that a certain Catholic priest has had his tongue torn out 5. Those are the frantic ones.

You have to exercise love, you have to love them too. Many, once corrected, cried; many, corrected; I know them, for they have come to me from the number of those furious. They cry daily for their past actions and cannot get enough of shedding tears when they look at the fury of those who are still angry at not having digested the drunkenness of vanity. What do we do then? Love forces us to also put ourselves at its service. Although we cause inconvenience to both kinds of sick people, waking the lethargic and tying up the frantic, we love them all. 9. Concord between brothers is a good thing; but see where: the concord in Christ, the concord of Christians. And love of neighbor. What to do if you are not yet a brother in Christ? As a man, he is our neighbor; love him too to win him. Therefore, if you live in harmony with your Christian brother, you must love your neighbor, even the one with whom you do not now live in harmony, since he is not yet a brother in Christ, because he has not yet been reborn in Christ nor does he know the sacraments of Christ. He is a pagan, he is a Jew; but, nevertheless, he is your neighbor, because he is a man. If you also love him, you have entered into another love, the fruit of another gift, and thus there are two in you: Concord between brothers and love of neighbor. All those who live in harmony with their brothers and love their neighbors are those who make up the Church, dedicated to

These must be the place where God enters. You honored your bishop by wanting to designate this basilica with the name of Florence, but you are his Florence. Indeed, thus says the Apostle: You are my joy and my crown in the Lord. Everything in the world disappears, passes away. This same life, what is it but what the psalm said: In the morning it will pass away like grass; In the morning it will bloom and pass away; In the afternoon it will decay, harden and dry? That's how all meat is. That is why we have been promised to Christ, a new life, an eternal hope and the consolation of immortality; promise already made reality in the flesh of Christ. He received from us that flesh that is now immortal and showed us what was fulfilled in him. For us he took the meat. Well, in itself: In the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Seek the flesh and blood; where can you find it in the Word? Since he truly wanted to suffer with us and redeem us, he took on the form of a servant and descended who was already here to manifest himself, he who had never been absent; He wanted to become a man who made the man, to be made of the mother who created the mother. He climbed to the cross, died, and showed us what we already knew: being born and dying. He fulfilled in himself, in a humble act, what had been familiar and known to us since ancient times. We knew being born and dying, but not being resurrected and living forever. He assumed, humbled, this double and ancient reality of ours; The other two great and new realities he fulfilled as exalted. He resurrected his flesh, the vestra intrent: sed mentes vestrae debent esse, quo Deus intret. Honorastis episcopum vestrum, ut hanc basilicam Florentiam vocare velletis; sed Florentia eius vos estis. Nam sic dicit Apostolus: Gaudium et corona mea vos estis in Domino (Phil 4,1). Quidquid est in saeculo, vanescit, transit. Vita ista quid est, nisi quod Psalmus dixit: Mane sicut herba transiet, mane floriet et praeteriet: vespere decidet, durescit et arescit? (Ps 89.6). Hoc est omnis expensive. Ideo Christus, ideo nova vita, ideo spes aeterna, ideo consolatio immortalitatis promissa, et in Domini carne iam reddita. A nobis enim assumpta est illa caro, quae iam immortalis est, et nobis quod in se implevit, ostendit. Propter nos enim carnem habuit. Nam propter se: In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deus, et Deus erat Verbum (lo 1,1). Quaere carnem et sanguinem: ubi in [1598] Verb?

Ascendit usque in cruzen, mortuus est, et ostendit nobis quod noveramus, nasci et morí. Implevit in se humilis haec vetera nostra usitata et note. Well, as levavit in caelum carnem says, sedet ad dexteram Patris. I want to speak to your charity about this patience as much as the Lord grants me. The Lord Jesus Christ also says in a certain place in the Gospel: With your patience you will possess your souls. And in another place it is also said: Woe to those who have lost patience! Whether we talk about patience, endurance or tolerance, there is only one reality, meaning with several terms. We must fix in our hearts that one reality, not the diversity of the words that express it, and possess within ourselves what we designate outside. Who knows that he is a pilgrim in this world, regardless of where he is physically; He who knows that he has an eternal home in heaven, he who is certain that there is the region of a happy life, which here it is lawful to desire, but it is not possible to have and burns with desire so good, so holy and so chaste, he lives here patiently. Patience does not seem necessary for prosperous situations, but for adverse ones. No one patiently endures what pleases him. On the contrary, whenever we tolerate, that we endure something with patience, it is something hard and bitter; That is why it is not happiness, but unhappiness, that requires patience. patience, since it is annoying for him to tolerate the pilgrimage itself until he reaches the desired and loved homeland. One is the self-love of desire and the other is that of vision. Thus, then, there are three things that the Apostle mainly urges us to build in the inner man: faith, hope and love; and, after having praised the three virtues, he says in conclusion: The greatest of all is love. Pursue love. What then is faith? What the hope? What love? And why is love greater? As defined by a certain text of Scripture, faith is the content of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen. He who hopes for something does not yet possess what he hopes for, but through faith he becomes like the one who possesses it. Faith is, he says, the content of what is hoped for; It is not yet the very reality that we will possess, but faith is in its place. It cannot be said that he who has faith has nothing or that he who is full of faith is empty. That is why the reward of faith is great: because, although he does not see, he believes. If he saw, what reward would he deserve? For this reason, when the Lord rose from the dead and appeared to his disciples, not only until he was seen, but until

being touched with the hands, and convinced the human senses that he, the one who had recently hung on the tree, was the one who had risen, after living with them for some days, which seemed sufficient to him to strengthen the Gospel and ensure faith in the resurrection, he ascended to heaven so that no one would see him, but rather they would possess him by faith. If it always remained here, visible to these eyes, faith would not deserve any praise. Now, however, a man is told: "Believe." But he wants to see. It is replied: «Believe now, so that you may see sometime. Faith originates desert; vision is the prize. If you want to see before you believe, you ask for the reward before doing the work. What you want to possess has a price. You want to see God. The price of such great good is faith. Do you want to get there and don't want to walk? Vision is possession; faith, the path. "He who refuses the fatigue of the journey, how can he claim the joy of possession?" 4. Faith does not fail, because it is sustained by hope. Eliminate hope, and faith will fail. Love ignites hope, and hope shines through love. But what faith will there be to praise when we come into possession of those things that we have hoped for, believing in them without having seen them? Because faith is the proof of what is not seen. 11. Mammona is the Hebrew name for riches; That's why in Punic they are called mamon. What are we to do, then? What the Lord commanded? Make friends with the "mammon" of iniquity, so that they too may receive you in the eternal tabernacles when you begin to faint. It is easy to understand from these words that we must give alms, that we must give to the needy, since in them it is Christ who receives. He himself said: When you did it to one of these little ones of mine, you did it to me. In another place he also said: Whoever gives one of my disciples a glass of cold water just for being a disciple, truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward. We understand that we must give alms, and we must not waste much time in choosing to whom we should give them, since we cannot examine hearts. When you give them to all, then you will give them to the few who are worthy of them. You are hospitable; you offer your house to pilgrims; It also admits those who do not deserve it, so as not to exclude those who deserve it. You cannot judge or examine hearts. Although even if you could say: "It's bad, it's not good," I add: it's still your enemy. If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If you have to do good even to your enemy, how much more so to the stranger, who, although bad, is nevertheless not your enemy! In those words we see this indicated, because those who act in this way acquire friends who will receive them in the eternal tabernacles once they are expelled from this administration. Many take from others and give something from it, thinking that in this way their sins are forgiven, bribing, in a certain way, the judge. Listen better to those who moan and complain about you than to those who give thanks for you. Let no one, therefore, believe that because the Lord has named the "mammon" of iniquity in the context of giving alms, one must dedicate oneself to fraud, rapine, plunder and any other unpleasant thing. What does it mean, then: Make friends with the "mammon" of iniquity? I think, brothers, that mammona is nothing other than gold, that is, riches. Let's use our term so you understand it. There are authentic riches and there are false riches. Iniquity calls false riches riches, since true riches

Topic: The resurrection of the dead. Location: Unknown. Date: Winter of the year 410 to 411. 1. When the Apostle's letter was read, I was able to notice a commendable movement of your faith and love, which showed how much horror is caused to you by those who think that there is no other life than this one that we have in common with the beasts and that after death there is no trace of man nor is there any hope of another better life. Twisting the itch of bad ears, they say: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die. Let my discussion begin from here and let it be the crux of my in Libris quos legebat, nec ego sponsam. Qui revelavit illi de Christi clarificatione quod scriptum est: Exaltare super caelos, Deus; ipse revelavit mihi from Ecclesiae effusione quod sequitur: Super omnem terram gloria tua (Ps 107,6). DE RESURRECTIONE MORTUORUM, I

CAPUT I.—1. Anirnadvertimus, cum Apostoli Epístola legeretur, laudabilem motum fidei caritatisque vestrae, quemadmodum exhorrueritis homines, qui putantes hanc solam esse vitam, quam cum pecoribus habemus communem, post mortem autem finiri totum quod est hominis, nec esse spem ullam vitae alterius melioris, pruritum malarum aurium corrumpentes, dicunt: Manducemus et bibamus; you were enim morimur (1 Cor 15:32; Wis 2:6). Hinc ergo sumatur nostrae disputationis exordium, et

sermon, point of reference for everything that the Lord deigns to suggest to me. 2. Our hope is none other than the resurrection of the dead, and also our faith. The resurrection of the dead is equally our love, which is inflamed by the preaching of things not yet seen and kindled by its desire, the greatness of which makes our hearts capable of the happiness that we are promised to come, while we believe in what is not yet seen. Therefore, our love should not concern itself with these temporal and visible things, hoping that we will have in the resurrection something like that which, if we despise it now, we live better and are better, that is, carnal pleasures and delights. Once faith in the resurrection of the dead is eliminated, the entire Christian doctrine collapses. On the other hand, once faith is well founded in it, security does not occur automatically for the Christian soul if the future life is not distinguished from this one, which is passing. Consequently, we must pose the problem in the following way: if the dead are not resurrected, we have no hope of a future life; If, however, they are resurrected, there will certainly be a future life. But the second question concerns what that life will be like. Thus, the first discussion centers on whether there will be a resurrection of the dead; the second, about what the life of the saints will be after the resurrection. 3.

In altera infidelis errat, in altera christianus carnalis. Christianus auctoritatis pondere ducendus.—Qui ergo dicunt
The resurrection of the dead

Christians; Those who, on the contrary, think that after the resurrection the dead must live carnally, are carnal Christians. Therefore, all discussion against the opinion of those who deny the resurrection of the dead is directed against those who are outside, none of whom I think are present here. Therefore my discussion might seem superfluous if I stopped at trying to demonstrate that the dead are resurrected. The weight of authority must move the Christian who already believed in Christ, and who knows that the Apostle can never lie. It is enough, then, for the Christian to hear: If the dead are not raised, our preaching is vain and your faith is vain. If the dead are not resurrected, he said, neither was Christ resurrected. But, if Christ was resurrected, in whom the salvation of Christians is found, it is no longer impossible for the dead to be resurrected, because he who resurrected his Son and resurrected his flesh left an example in his head for the rest of the body, which is the Church. It could well be superfluous, therefore, to talk about the resurrection of the dead in order to go on to discuss what Christians are accustomed to, namely: what we will be like after the resurrection, how we will live, what our occupations will be, whether we will have any or, rather, none; If we do not have any, we will live in leisure, doing nothing; If we do something, what we will do; also, if we are to eat and drink, if the union of man and woman will subsist or if there will be some type of simple and uncorrupted common life; and in this case what will that life itself be like, what the movements and what the

shape of the bodies. This is what Christians discuss once faith in the resurrection is assured. 4. I would go on to discuss this, as far as a man can explain it to another man, which is you and I, if a certain concern for some of our brothers who are too carnal and almost pagan would not force me to dwell a little on the question that asks if the dead really rise from the dead. I think that there are no pagans here, but that they are all Christians. But the pagans and those who mock the resurrection do not cease to murmur every day in the ears of the Christians: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die. And as the Apostle already said, showing his concern and adding this phrase: They corrupt good customs with bad words. Fearing these evils and full of concern for the weak, with love not only paternal, but also maternal, I must say something about it, as much as is sufficient for Christian people, since a greater devotion to the Holy Scriptures is what has moved all those who have gathered today, since the festivity of an ordinary day has not summoned to the Church even the masses who frequent the theaters. Many tend to attend not because they are moved by pity, but by the festivity. This consideration causes me to first speak of the resurrection of the dead, and then, if the Lord grants me the easy word, I will speak of what the life of the righteous must be like afterwards.
