They cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor will corruption inherit incorruption, showing that under the terms of "flesh" and "blood" he meant the corruption of the mortal and animal body. He then resolves himself the question that the attentive listeners might ask of him; He himself worries that his children understand more than his children worry about their parents' words. Add these words: See that I announce to you a mystery. Cease your thinking, O man, whoever you are. Taking support from the words of the Apostle, you had begun to think that human flesh is not resurrected, having heard: the flesh and the healing will not possess the kingdom of God; but apply your ear to the words that follow and correct the presumption of your heart. See, he said, that I announce to you a mystery: we will all be resurrected, but not all of us will be transformed. What does this mean? The transformation can be for better or worse. If there has been talk of a transformation, without yet seeing what it will be like, whether for something better or for something worse, let us continue reading, let him clarify it for us; why go into assumptions? Perhaps the authority of the Apostle will prevent you from following your conjectures and slipping into error through human suspicion; perhaps indicate clearly what transformation you want to be understood. Having said: We will all be resurrected, but not all of us will be transformed, I warn that we must all be resurrected, good and bad; But let's see who will be transformed, and, from here, we will understand what the transformation must be like, whether for the better or non possunt; ñeque corruptio incorruptlonem hereditate possidebit (1 Cor 15:50); ut ostenderet nomine carnis et sanguinis corruptionem mortalis animalisque corporis se intellegere voluisse. Deinde solvit iam ipse quaestionem, quam possent ab eo solliciti auditores exquirere: quia sollicitior ipse de intellectu filiorum, quam filii sunt de verbis parentum. Subiungit ergo, et dicit: Ecce mysterium vobis dico (ib., 51). Quiescat cogitatio tua, or homo, quisquís is. Coeperas enim cogitare de verbis Apostoli, quod caro humano non resurgat, cum audires: Caro et sanguis regnum Dei non possidebit (ib., 50): sed praebe aurem consequentibus verbis, et corrige praesumptionem cogitationis. Ecce, inquit, mysterium dico vobis: omnes quidem resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur (ib., 51). Quid est hoc? Mutatio quippe aut in peius est, aut in melius.

Si ergo posita est mutatio, ut nondum videamus qualis erit, utrum in aliquid melius, an in aliquid deterius: ergo sequatur, et ipse exponat; quid nobis est suspicari? Et fortasse humano suspicione labi in errorem te non permittit in coniecturas tuas apostolica auctoritas, et hoc liquide exponit, cuiusmodi mutationem velit intellegi. Quid ergo? Cum dixisset: Omnes resurgemus, non tamen omnes immutabimur (ib.): video omnes resurrecturos et bonds et malo; sed qui immutabuntur, videoamus; et hinc intellegamus mutationem, utrum in melius an in deterius sit future. Yes enim

for worse. If this transformation occurs in the bad, it will be for the worse; If in the good, for the better. In an instant, he says, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. The trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise uncorrupted and we will be transformed. Therefore, this transformation will be for the better, since it says: And we will be transformed. But it has not yet adequately expressed to what extent our body will be transformed for the better. He has not yet said what that improvement consists of. Well, even when the transformation from childhood to adolescence occurs, we can speak of a mutation for the better, despite the fact that, although the weakness is minor, it continues to exist alongside mortality. 20. Therefore, let us consider point by point again. In an instant, he says. It seems difficult to men for the dead to rise again; but it is admirable how the Apostle removed all doubts and difficulties from the hearts of the faithful. You say: "The dead are not resurrected"; I not only say that they are resurrected, but that it will happen with such speed that you did not even have time to be conceived and born. How much time a man spends in the womb until he is formed, perfected, born and strengthened with the passage of time! Should he be resurrected in the same way? No, but in an instant, he said. Many ignore what an instant (atomus) is. The term atomus is derived from TO\IT¡, which means section, division;

Greek, means that which cannot be sectioned or divided. The term is used both for bodies and for time. malorum est is mutatio, in peius; si autem bonorum, in melius erit. In atom, inquit, in ictu oculi, in new tuba. Canet enim tuba, et mortui resurgent incorrupti, et nos immutabimur (ib., 52). Iam ergo in melius erit ista mutatio, cum dicit: Et nos immutabimur; sed nondum expressum est quantum exprimi opportitu, quousque corpus nostrum commutatur in melius. Quid est ipsum melius, nondum dictum est. Nam et ab infantia in adolescentiam cum mutatur, potest dici in melius commutari, ubi etsi minus infirmum, adhuc tamen infirmum et mortale est. CAPUT XVII.—20. Celeritas resurrectionis. Atomus, crux. Atom in corpore. Atom in tempore. Ictus oculi.—Ergo singula diligentius retractemus. In atom, inquit. Difficile videtur hominibus resurgere mortuos: sed mirum est quemadmodum abstulerit Apostolus omnes ancipites difficultates de cordibus fidelium. You say: Non resurgunt mortui: ego non solum resurgere mortuum dico, sed tanta celeritate, quanta non conceptas et natus es. Quanta enim mora est ut formetur homo in uterus, ut perficiatur, ut nascatur, ut aetatum successione roboretur? Numquid forte sic resurrecturus est? Non: thirst in atom, inquit. Multi nesciunt quid sit atomus. Atomus dictus est a TOMIÍ, quod est sectio: hopo? graece quod secari non potest. Sed dicitur atomus in corpore, dicitur in tempore. In corpore dicitur, si quid inveniri potest quod quidem

Referring to bodies, it is applied in the event that something can be found that appears impossible to be divided; something so tiny that it does not admit the possibility of being sectioned. Referring to time, it is a brief moment that cannot be divided either. So that slower hearts can understand what I'm saying, I'm going to give an example. Take a stone; divide it into several parts; Divide these parts into grains, and the grains into grains, such as sand; Still divide the grains of sand into very fine dust until you reach, if you can, such a fineness that it no longer admits of being divided. This is an "atom" referred to bodies. Applied to time, it is understood in this way: a year, for example, is divided into months; the months, in days; days can still be divided into hours; the hours, even in other spacious parts that admit divisions until you reach a point of time and a drop of a moment that can no longer be extended in the slightest and that, therefore, cannot be divided. This is the temporal "atom." You said, then, that the dead are not resurrected; Not only are they resurrected, but they are resurrected so quickly that everyone's resurrection will take place in an atom or instant of time. And, explaining the speed of the instant, after having said: in an instant, he then added what action or movement can be carried out in that space of time: In the blink of an eye, he said. He knew, in fact, that it was not clear in an instant, and he wanted to say something more clearly that would be more intelligible. What does it mean in a blink of an eye? No

The resurrection of the dead

You will see its same external appearance, you will preserve it; but, if you look for corruption and mortality, you will not find it. Has corruption retreated somewhere? No, rather there it perished and there it was absorbed. Therefore, after having said: It is fitting that this corruptible put on incorruption and that this mortal put on immortality, he added: Then what is written will be fulfilled: "Death has been absorbed into victory." Where is your strife, oh death? Where is your sting, O death? It does not say: "Death departed until victory," but rather: Death was absorbed in victory. How then did they stray from the truth? Because they affirmed one resurrection as true, but denied the other. 23. There is, in fact, a resurrection in faith, according to which everyone who believes is resurrected in the spirit. And he who has been resurrected before in the spirit will be resurrected for good in the body, since those who have not been resurrected before in the spirit by faith will not be resurrected in the body for that transformation in which all corruption will be assumed and absorbed, but they will be resurrected whole for punishment. The bodies of the wicked will also be resurrected whole, without the slightest diminution appearing; but bodily integrity and, so to speak, a certain corporeal and corruptible solidity is destined for punishment. Where there may be pain, it cannot be said that there is no corruption, although that weakness does not perish in the midst of the pain nor does the pain itself die. It is not wrong to see

prophetically signified that corruption under the name “worm,” and pain under the term “fire.” But the solidity will be so great that neither the pains will push it to death nor will it be transformed into that incorruption in which there is no pain; That is why it is written: Their worm will not die and their fire will not be extinguished. The transformation that will not know corruption is typical of the saints. Those who now have the resurrection of the spirit through faith will possess it; resurrection of which the Apostle says: If you have risen with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ sits at the right hand of the Father; Taste things above, not things on earth. For you are dead and your life is hidden with Christ in God. As death according to the spirit corresponds to resurrection according to the spirit, so death according to the flesh corresponds to resurrection according to the flesh. Death according to the spirit consists in not believing the vanities that were believed and in not doing the evil that was done, and the resurrection according to the spirit, in believing the healthy things that were not believed and in doing the good that was not done. Whoever had idols and other figures as gods and knew the only God and believed in him, died in idolatry and was resurrected in the Christian faith. He who was a drunk and has become sober, has died to drunkenness and has been resurrected to sobriety. In the same way, when the removal of any bad work is carried out, a certain death occurs in the soul and it is resurrected in its good works. no exit open to slanderers and those who seek to separate Christians from the faith by using it precisely, injecting their poison to cause the death of weak souls. My role will not be as a commentator, but as a reader, so that this my sermon is based on the authority of the Scriptures and is not built on the sand of human assumptions in the event that my memory fails me. Listen, then, to the gospel according to John: The Lord speaks: Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life and will not be judged, since he has already passed from death to life. Truly, truly I tell you, the hour has come, and it is this, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live. As the Father has life in himself, so he gave the Son to have life also in himself, and gave him the power to judge, since he is the son of man. Do not be amazed by this, because the hour has come when all those who are in the tombs will hear his voice, and those who did good will come out to the resurrection of life, and those who, on the other hand, did evil, to the resurrection of damnation. I think that many have noticed in this text that the Lord speaks clearly and distinctly of the two resurrections, the one that takes place in the spirit through faith and the one that will take place in the flesh at the moment that well-known trumpet sounds. However, let us consider these words more carefully so that they may be clear to all who heard them. In

Truly, truly I tell you that whoever hears my word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life and will not be judged, because he has already passed from death to life. These words refer to the resurrection in the spirit, which now takes place by faith. But so as not to give the impression that he proposes it as for a still distant future, despite not having said: "He will pass from death to life", but rather: He has passed from death to life; so that it would not seem that he uses the past tense in a symbolic way, just as when he says: They pierced my hands and my feet, announcing what was still future, he explains it more clearly below: Truly, truly I tell you that the hour has come, and it is this, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live. Where before he said: He has passed from death to life, now they will live. But so that the words the hour will come do not refer to the end of the world, when the resurrection of the bodies will also take place, he added: And this is it. He did not just say: The hour will come, but: The hour will come, and this is it. Those who hear that voice will live, that is, they will live with the life that he indicated before when he said: He has passed from death to life. In these words he has mentioned those who will be free from the torment of judgment, because they have anticipated it with their faith, and pass from death to life.

Sed ne ita proposita videretur, quasi adhuc longe future sit; quanquam non dixerit: Transiturus est a morte in vitam; sed: transitum fecit a morte in vitam: tamen ne verbo praeteriti temporis imagine usus videretur, sicut est: Foderunt manus meas et pedes (Ps 21,17), quod adhuc futurum praenuntiabatur; sequitur, et hoc ipsum planius explicat: Amen, amen dico vobis, inquit, quia venit hora et nunc est, quando mortui audient vocem Filii Dei; et qui audierint vivos (lo 5,24). Quo supra dixit: Transiit a morte in vitam; hoc never dicit: vivost. Sed ne illud quod ait, Venit hora, in finem saeculi speraretur, quando etiam corporum resurrectio future est; addidit: et nunc est. Non enim ait tantum: Come hour; thirst: Venit hora, et nunc est. Qui autem audierint hac vocem, vivirt; scilicet vita quam superius significavit, they say: Transiit a morte ad vitam (ib., 24). Hic ergo eos significavit qui ad poenam iudicii non pertinent; quia praeveniunt iudicium fide sua, et transitum faciunt a morte ad vitam. CAPUT XXIII.—26. Resurrectio secundum carnemfutura.—Restat ergo ut iudicium futurum ostendat inter bonds et malo: quia hic bonds
26. He only has to show the future judgment, dividing the good and the bad, since in the text he has indicated that the

present resurrection, which takes place in the spirit, only occurs in the good. He continues saying: And he gave him the power to judge, since he is the son of man. He has hinted in what condition he has received the power to judge: since he is, he said, the son of man. Indeed, as the Son of God, he has everlasting power together with the Father. Then he explained what the judgment will be like: Do not be surprised by this, because the hour has come when all those who are in the tombs will hear his voice, and will come out; those who did good, for the resurrection of life; those who, on the other hand, did evil, for the resurrection from damnation. Before, after having said: The hour has come, he added: And this is a shame that it was not thought that the hour was announced in which, at the end of time, the bodily resurrection will take place. Here, on the contrary, since he wanted this one to be understood precisely, after having said: The hour has come, he did not add: And this is it. Furthermore, he spoke before that the dead would hear the voice of the Son of God, but without mentioning the tombs at all, so that we could distinguish between those who died due to a loss of mind, who are now resurrected by faith, from those other dead whose corpses will be resurrected at the end of the world. So that we might wait for that future resurrection of the bodies, he said here: All those who are in the tombs will hear his voice, and will come out. He also said before: They will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live. What need was there to add: Those who hear it, could have said: «Escutantum commemoravit ad praesentem resurrectionem, quae secundum spiritum est, pertinere. Sequitur itaque, et dicit: Et potestatem dedil ei et iudicium faceré, quia filius hominis est (ib., 27). Insinuavit secundum quid acceperit potestatem iudicii: quia filius, inquit, hominis est. Nana secundum id quod Filius Dei est, sempiternam cum Patre habet potestatem. Iam quomodo sit futurum iudicium, consequenter exonit: Nolite, inquit, mirai hoc, quia venit hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem eius; et proceedent qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitae; qui vero mala egerunt, in resurrectionem iudicii (ib., 2830). Superius cum dixisset: Venit hora; adiecit: et nunc est: ne illa hora praenuntiata putaretur, qua in fine saeculifutura est corporum resurrectio.

Hic ergo quia ipsam volebat intellegi, cum dixisset: Venit hora; non adiecit: et nunc est. item superius mortuos dixit audire vocem Filii Dei, monumentalum autem nullam commemorationem fecit; ut distinguishemus mortuos per mentís errorem qui resurgunt moda per fidem, ab eis mortuis [1630] quorum cadavera in monumentis sunt resurrectura in ultimo saeculi. Hic ergo ut illa in fine speraretur corporum resurrectio, Omnes, ait, qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem eius, et provenent. superius item: Audient, inquit, vocem Filii Dei; et qui audierint, vivirt (ib., 25). Quid opus erat addere: Qui audierint; cum posset ita says:
The resurrection of the dead

they will shout the voice of the Son of God and live", but because he said it about those who are dead because of the error of their mind, of whom many hear and do not listen, that is, do not obey or believe? Those who, on the other hand, listen as he wanted to be heard by saying: Those who have ears to hear, let them hear, they will live. Many will hear, but those who listen, that is, those who believe, will live, for those who hear without believing will not live. From which we deduce what death and what life he was talking about in that place; that is, of the death that only the bad possess, for the very fact of being bad, and of the life that only the good possess, for the very fact of becoming good. But here where he speaks of the future resurrection of the bodies he does not say: "They will hear his voice, and those who hear it will come out," because everyone will hear the last trumpet and everyone will come out, since the resurrection will be for everyone. But since not all of us will be transformed, he says next: Those who did good, for the resurrection of life; who, on the other hand, did evil, for the resurrection of damnation. Before, when he spoke of returning to the life of the spirit through faith, everyone faced the same fate; Such a life was not divided into a happy life and a miserable life, since everyone had the good part. Therefore, after having said: Those who listen to her will live, she did not add: "Those who did good, to eternal life, and those who did evil, to eternal punishment." By saying they will live he wanted it to be understood only in the good, in the same way that he had previously said: It has passed from death to life, without inAudient vocem Filii Dei, et vivost; nisi quia de his dicebat qui secundum mentís errorem mortui sunt, quorum multi audiunt et non audiunt, id est, non obtemperant, non credunt? Qui vero sic audiunt, quomodo volebat audiri, cum diceret: Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat (Luke 8,8); ipsivivent. Audient ergo multi, sed qui audierint, vivirt, id est, qui crediderint. Nam qui sic audient, ut non credant, non vivirt: unde apparet de qua morte, et de qua vita eo loco dixerit: de morte scilicet quae ad solos malo pertinet, eo ipso quo mali sunt; et de vita quae ad solos pertinet bonds, eo ipso quo boni fiunt. CAPOT XXIV.—Hic autem, ubi secundum corpora resurrecturos pronuntiat, non ait: Audient vocem eius, et qui audierint, provenent. Omnes enim novissimam tubam audient, et provenent, quia omnes resurgemus.

Sed quia non omnes immutabimur, sequitur et dicit: Qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitae; qui vero mala egerunt, in resurrectionem iudicii (lo 5,29). Superius itaque ubi per fidem secundum spiritum reviviscitur, ad eamdem sortem omnes reviviscunt; ut vita eorum non distribuatur in beatitudem et miseriam, sed ad bonam partem omnes pertineant. Et ideo cum dixisset: Qui audierint, vivirt (ib., 25); non adiecit: Qui bona egerunt, in vitam aeternam; qui vero mala egerunt, in poenam aeternam. Hoc enim ipsum quod dictum est, vivirt, in bono tantummodo accipi voluit: sicut etiam superius: Transitum, inquit, fecit a morte ad vitam;
The resurrection of the dead

tell what life, because reviving from death by faith cannot be a bad life. They will hear his voice and live; He wanted the word will live to be interpreted throughout this text in the sense of a life of good. But he said: They will hear, and they will come out, these words with which he indicates the bodily movement of the bodies when leaving their graves. But since coming out of the tombs will not become good for everyone, he continued: Those who did good, for the resurrection of life, wanting that here also life would be understood only in good; who, on the other hand, did evil, for the resurrection of condemnation, that is, of punishment. 27. Therefore, brothers, let no one ask with perverse subtlety what shape the bodies will have at the resurrection of the dead, what their height will be, how they will move and what their way of walking will be. It must be enough for you to know that your flesh will be resurrected in the same form in which the Lord manifested himself, that is, in human form. But you need not fear corruption, although the form is the same; Well, if you do not have to fear corruption, you will not fear that sentence either: Flesh and blood will not possess the kingdom of God; nor will you fall into the snare of the Sadducees, which you will not be able to avoid if you think that men will rise again to take wives, beget children, and repeat the works of mortal life. If you ask what that life will be like, what man can explain it to you? It will be the life of angels. Who can show you the life of the an-

gels, will be able to show you that of the saints, since they will be equal to the angels. If, on the other hand, the life of angels is hidden, let no one ask more, lest error prevent him from reaching what he is asking about and lead him to what he himself has imagined. Ask ahead of time and hastily. You advance along the road, because you will reach your homeland if you do not abandon it. Therefore, hold fast to Christ, brothers; Hold on to faith, stay on the path; the same path will lead you to that which you cannot see now. What the members have to expect was manifested in the head; In the foundation, what is built in faith was shown, to be completed later in the vision, lest, when you think you are seeing, the false image of something that appears to be what it is not is being shown to you, and, abandoning the path, you deviate into error and do not reach the homeland to which the path leads, that is, to the vision to which faith leads. 28. You will ask: "How do angels live?" It is enough for you to know that they do not live subject to any corruption. It is easier to tell you what that life is not than what it is. I too, my brothers, can briefly review the things that will not be there; and I can because they are things that we have experienced, and we know that they will not be found there. But what will be there, we have not yet experienced. Well we walk through the world, not yet in the vision. While we live in the body we are pilgrims far from the Lord. What is it,

nec dixit ad quam vitam; quia per fidem a morte revives, non potest esse mala vita. Hic autem primo non, Audient vocem eius et vivost; ipsum enim, vivost, per totam istam lectionem in bono intellegi voluit: sed dixit: audient, et provenent, quo verbo significavit corporalem motum corporum de locis sepulturarum suarum. Sed quia proceedé de monumentis non omnibus ad bonum erit: Qui bona, inquit, fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitae; etiam hic vitam in bono tantum intellegi voluit: qui vero mala egerunt, inquit, in resurrectionem iudicii (ib., 29), iudicium scilicet pro poena posit. CAPUT XXV.—27. Quale corpus, et qualis sanctorum vita post resurrectionem.—Iam ergo, fratres, nemo quaerat perversa subtilitate cuiusmodi figura erit corporum in resurrectione mortuorum, quanta statura, qualis motus, qualis incessus. Sufficit tibi quod resurgit caro tua in ea specie, in qua Dominus apparuit, in hominis utique specie. Sed noli propter speciem timere corruptionem: si enim non timueris eorruptionem, non timebis et illam sententiam: Caro et sanguis regnum Dei non possidebit (1 Cor 15,50); nec incides in laqueum Sadducaeorum, quem propterea non possis Evitare, quia putas ad hoc resurgere homines, ut ducant uxores, et generent filios, et agant opera vi[1631]tae mortalis. Si quaeris qualis erit vita, quis hominum hoc poterit explicare? Vita erit Angelorum. Quicumque tibi potuerit ostendere vitam Angelorum, osten-

det vitam eorum; quia aequales futuri erunt Angelis. Si autem Angelorum vita occulta est, nemo quaerat amplius; ne per errorem non perveniat ad id quod quaerit, sed ad quod sibi ipse confinxerit. Praepropere enim quaerit, et festinans quaerit. Your in via ambula; You come ad patríam, if you do not wish to travel. Tenete ergo Christum, fratres, tenete fidem, tenete viam: ipsa vos perducet ad id quod videre moda non potestis. In illo enim capite apparuit quod speretur in membris; in illo fundament demonstratum est quod in our aedificetur fide, ut postea perficiatur in specie: ne forte cum putatis vos cerneré, appareat vobis aliquid per imaginem falsem quasi esse quod non est, et dimissa via in errorem devietis, et ad patriam quo ducít via, id est, ad speciem quo ducit fides, non perveniatis. CAPUT XXVI.—28. Vita similis Angelorum erit, carens operibus corruptionis et indigentiae. Sabbatum perpetuum. Misericordiae opera cur ibi nulla erunt.—You say: Quomodo vivunt Angeli? Sufficit tibi scire hoc, quod non corruptibiliter vivunt. Facilius enim tibi potest dici quid ibi non erit, quam quid ibi erit. Possum enim et ego, fratres mei, breviter vobis percurrere quaedam quae ibi non erunt: et hoc propterea possum, quia ista experti sumus, et novimus ea quae ibi non erunt. Quid autem ibi erit nondum sumus experti. Per fidem enim ambulamus, nondum per speciem: quamdiu sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino
The resurrection of the dead

Well, what won't be there? I will not marry to beget children, since there is no death there; there will be no growth, nor will there be aging; there will be no refection, because there will be no deficiency either; there will be no occupations, because there will be no need; There will not even be the commendable works of innocent men that the poverty of this life makes necessary. I am not only saying that the works of robbers and usurers will not exist; Nor will those carried out by innocent men to alleviate poverty and human needs exist there. There will be a perpetual Sabbath, which the Jews celebrated temporarily, and which we understand lasts forever. There will be an ineffable rest, impossible to describe; but, as I said, in a certain way it is explained by saying what will not be there. We tend toward that rest, with a view to it we are spiritually reborn. As we are carnally born for fatigue, so we are spiritually reborn for rest. The Lord cries: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. Here it nourishes us, there it perfects us; here he promises, there he fulfills; here it is expressed symbolically, there it discovers reality. Once we have reached full perfection and salvation in body and spirit, in that happiness there will be no such occupations; The good works of the Christians we praise here will not even exist. What Christian is not praised when he gives bread to the hungry or drink to the thirsty, or when he dresses the naked or welcomes a pilgrim, or tames a quarrelsome person, or visits the sick, or burying the dead?

heal a dead person, or comfort someone who cries? Great works, full of mercy, full of praise and grace. These will not exist there either, since the works of mercy are generated by the necessity that causes misery. Who are you going to feed, where no one feels hungry? Who are you going to give a drink to if no one is thirsty? Are you going to clothe the naked, when all are clothed with the same immortality? You recently heard what the robes of the saints are. The Apostle says: It is fitting that this corruptible put on incorruption. Where clothing is talked about, clothing is mentioned. This garment Adam lost, and then received the skins. Or can you offer hospitality to a pilgrim where everyone lives in their homeland? Will you be able to visit the sick where everyone will be vigorous with the same solidity of incorruption? Can you bury a dead person where they live forever? Can you bring quarrelsome people to an agreement where peace reigns in everything? Can you console the sad where everyone will enjoy forever? Since all miseries will cease at the same time, these works of mercy will also cease. 29. What will we do there then? Didn't I already say that it is easier to say what there will not be than what there will be? What I know, brothers, is that we are not going to spend our leisure time sleeping, since even sleep has been given to the soul as a refuge against fainting. In fact, the fragile body would not support attention that had the senses in permanent action.

(2 Cor 5,6-7). Quid ergo ibi non erit? Ducere uxorem, ut filii propagentur; quia non est ibi mors: non ibi erit crescere, quia nec senescere: non erit refectio, quia nec defectio: non ibi erunt negotia, quia nec indigentia; nec ipsa laudabilia opera hominum innocentium, quae cogit operani egestas et necessitas huius vitae. Non enim dico tantummodo non ibi future opera latronum aut feneratorum, sed ipsa quae innocentes nomines operantur propter indigentiam sublevandarum humanorum necessitatum, non ibi erunt. CAPUT XXVII.—Sabbatum erit perpetuum, quod a Iudaeis celebratur temporaliter, a nobis autem in aeternum intellegitur. Quies erit ineffabilis, quae explican non potest; sed, ut dixi, utcumque explicatur, cum dicuntur quae ibi non erunt. Ad illam quietem tendimus, ad illam spiritualiter regeneramur. Sicut enim ad labores camaliter nascimur, ita ad quietem spiritualiter renascimur: clamante illo: Come ad me, omnes qui laborath et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos (Mt 11,28). Hic pascit, ibi perficit: hic promittit, ibi reddit: hic signifícat, ibi exprimit. Cum autem in illa beatitude et spiritu et corpore perfecti salvique fuerimus, ista negotia non erunt; nec illa ibi erunt, quae hic laudantur in bonis operibus Christianorum. Quis enim non laudatur christianus porrigendo panem esurienti potumque sitienti, dressing nudum, suscipiendo peregrinum, pacing litigationsum, visiting aegrotum, burying mortuum,

[1632] consoling lugentem? Magna opera, plena mercye, plena laudis et gratiae. Sed nec ipsa ibi erunt: quia opera misericordiae necessitas miseriae comparavit. Quem pascis, ubi nemo esurit? Cui potum das, ubi nemo sitit? An vestitus es nudum, ubi omnes ipsa immortalitate vestiti sunt? Audisti paulo ante robes sanctorum, loquente Apostólo: Oportet corruptibile hoc Die incorruptionem (1 Cor 15,50). Ubi induere sonat, indumentum indicat. Hoc indumentum Adam lost, ut pelles acciperet. An peregrinum suscepturus es, ubi omnes in patria sua vivunt? Aegrotos visitabis, ubi omnes eadem incorruptionis firmitate vigebunt? Mortuum sepulturus, ubi semper vivunt? Litigantes concordaturus, ubi omnia in pace sunt? Tristes consolaturus, ubi omnes in aeternum gaudebunt? Quia ergo cessabunt simul miseriae, cessabunt haec opera miseriae. CAPUT XXVIII.—29. Quae erit beatorum actio post resurrectionem. Amen et Alleluia erit tota actio nostra sine taedio.—Quid ergo ibi agetur? Nonne iam dixi, facilius me dicere quid ibi non erit, quam quid ibi erit? Illud scio, fratres, quod non sumus dormitaturi vacando, quia et ¡pse somnus subsidium defectionis datus est animae. Quippe intentionem perpetuam mortales sensus agitantem non ferret fragüe corpus, nisi sen-
The resurrection of the dead

mortal if the same fragility were not restored with the rest of the senses to put them back into action; Just as a renewal must come from death, so now it originates from sleep. There, therefore, it will not exist. Where there is no death, there will be no image of death either. Nor should anyone fear boredom when they hear that they will always be awake and doing nothing. I can affirm—although I cannot say how, since I cannot see it yet—; Without being reckless, I can say something, because I rely on the Scriptures, about what will constitute our activity there. All our activity will be reduced to "Amen" and "Hallelujah." What do you say, brothers? I am seeing that upon hearing it you have been filled with joy. But do not be sad again because of any carnal thought. If, by chance, any of you stood up to say "Amen" and "Hallelujah" daily, he would faint from boredom, fall asleep in the middle of his words, and would want to remain silent. But no one should consider that life despicable or worthy of being desired, thinking in this way: "If we always have to repeat 'Amen' and 'Hallelujah', who will endure?" I'm going to tell you something, if I can and however I can. “Amen” and “Hallelujah” we will not say with passing sounds, but with the affection of the soul. What does “Amen” mean? What does “Hallelujah” mean? “Amen” is equivalent to “It is true”; “Hallelujah”, to “Praise God”. Since God is the immutable truth, without decrease or increase, without defect or progress, without propensity 4 to any falsehood, perpetual

tua, stable, and always incorruptible, everything we do in the creature and in this life are like figures of the things signified through the bodies, and through them we walk in faith; but, when we see face to face what we now see as in a mirror, in an enigma, then we will say with another very different and ineffable affection: "It is true"; and, by saying that, we will be saying "Amen", but with an insatiable satiety. Since nothing will be lacking, there will be satiety; but since it will always delight what is not going to be lacking, if it can be spoken like this, there will be insatiable satiety. Therefore, the more insatiably satiated by the truth you are, the more you will say with insatiable truth "Amen." Who can say what it is like that which neither eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has entered into the heart of man? As we will see the truth without any fatigue and with perpetual delight, and we will also contemplate the most certain evidence, inflamed by the love of the truth and uniting ourselves with it through a sweet, chaste and at the same time incorporeal embrace, with such a voice we will praise him and we will also say "Hallelujah" to him. Burned with mutual love for God and exhorting each other to such praise, all the citizens of that city will say “Hallelujah,” because they will say “Amen.”

sibus consopitis ad eamdem agitationem ferendam repararetur ipsa fragilitas; et quemadmodum ex morte innovatio future est, sic nunc ex somno vigilatio ieront. Ibi ergo non erit. Ubi enim non est mors, nec imago mortis erit. Nec tamen cuiquam subrepat timor taediorum, cum ei dicitur quod semper vigilabit, et non aget aliquid. Possum dicere, et quomodo quidem fututum sit, non possum dicere, quia nec videre adhuc possum: tamen aliquid non impudenter dico, quia de Scripturis dico, quae ibi erit actio nostra. Tota actio nostra, Amen et Alleluia erit. What's up, brothers? Video quod auditis et gavisi estis. Sed nolite iterum carnali cogitatione contristan, quia si forte aliquis vestrum steterit et dixerit quotidie: Amen et Alleluia, taedio marcescet, et in ipsis vocibus dormitabit, et tacere iam volet: et propterea putet sibi esse aspernabilem vitam, et non desiderabilem, dicentes vobismetipsis: Amen et Alleluia semper dicturi sumus, quis durabit? Dicam ergo, si potero, quantum potero. Non sonis transeuntibus dicemus Amen et Alleluia, sed affectu animi. What is enim Amen? what alleluia? Amen, est verum: Alleluia, laúdate Deum. Quia ergo Deus veritas est incommutabilis, sine defectu, sine provectu, sine detrimento, sine augmento, sine alicuius falsitatis in4 Perhaps inquinaiione is more correct than propension, as the Maurinos suggest. In that case it would be necessary to translate: "without any stain of falsehood."

30. This life of the saints will so immortally fill and invigorate their bodies already transformed into the heavenly and angelic state, that no corruption caused by necessity separates or diverts them from that most happy clinatione perpetua, et stabilis, et semper incorruptibilis manens; haec autem quae agimus in creatura et in ista vita, velut figurae sunt rerum per significationes corporum, et quaedam in quibus ambulamus per fidem cum viderimus facie ad faciem quod nunc videmus per speculum in aenigmate (1 Cor 13:12), tune longe alio et ineffabiliter alio affectu dicemus, Ve[1653]rum est; et cum hoc dicemus, Amen utique dicemus, sed insatiabili satietate. Quia enim non deerit aliquid, ideo satietas: quia vero illud quod non deerit semper delectabit, ideo quaedam, si dici notest, insatiabilis satietas erit. Quam ergo insatiabiliter satiaberis verilate, tam insatiabili veritate you say, Amen. Iam quale est quis potest dicere, quod oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis nscendit? (1 Cor 2,9). Quia itaque sine aliquo fastidio et cum perpetua dclectatione videbimus verum, et certissima evidentia contuebimur, amore ipsius veritatis accensi et inhaerentes ei dulci et chaste amplexu eodemque incorporeo, tali etiam voce laudabimus eum, et dicemus, Alleluia. Insultants enim se ad parilem laudem flagrantissima caritate invicem ot in Deum, omnes cives illius civitatis dicet, Alleluia; quia digont, Amen. CAPUT XXIX.—30. Requies et recubitus beatorum in contemplationc ac laude veritatis.—Haec igitur vita sanctorum etiam corpora eorum commutata in caelestem et angelicum statum sic implebit, atque immorlaliter vegetabit, ut ab illa beatissima contemplatione et laude veritatis,
The resurrection of the dead

contemplation and praise of the truth. In this way, your food will be the same truth and rest will be like lying down. When the Lord said that they will attend the feast reclining, according to those words: Many will come from the east and the west, and will recline at the table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in my Father's kingdom, he indicated that they will feed on the food of truth in supreme rest. Such food restores, but does not diminish; full, but remains whole; you increase, but he is not consumed. Such is that food, different from the one here, which diminishes to restore your strength and which itself is exhausted so that the life of those who receive it is not exhausted. That lying down will be eternal rest; the viands, the immutable truth; the banquet, eternal life, that is, knowledge itself. This, he said, is eternal life, that they know you, the only God, and the one you sent, Jesus Christ. 31. That that life will consist of permanent contemplation, not only ineffable, but also delightful, of the truth, is attested to by a multitude of texts from Scripture, which I cannot quote in their entirety. That is what those words refer to: He who loves me keeps my commandments, and I will love him and show myself to him. As if someone had asked him what fruit and what reward he would obtain for having kept his commandments, he said: I will show myself to him, pinning perfect happiness on knowing him as he is. And also these others: Dearly beloved, we are children of God, but what has not yet been manifested

we will be We know that when he appears, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is. That is why the apostle Paul also said: Then we will see him face to face, who in another place had said: We are transformed into the same image, from glory to glory, as carried by the Spirit of the Lord. In the Psalms it is also said: Go and see that I am the Lord. We will see him fully when we are fully empty. When will that be but when the weary times have passed, the times full of needs that bind us now, while the earth produces thorns and thistles for sinful man so that he may eat his bread in the sweat of his face? Therefore, once the times of the earthly man have completely passed and the day of the heavenly man has fully fulfilled, we will see him fully, because we will fully vacate. Once corruption and poverty have disappeared in the resurrection of the faithful, there will no longer be anything to cause fatigue. As if it were said: "Lie down and eat," so it was said: Go and see. We will vacation, therefore, and see God as he is, and seeing him we will praise him. If our enemies have ended up at the bottom of the sea as if they were a stone, the devil only possesses and shows his hardness in those of whom it is written: The sinner, when he reaches the abyss of evils, despises them. They do not believe that they can be forgiven for what they did, and, driven by that desperation, they dive even deeper. But your right hand, Lord, has been glorified by its power; Your right hand, Lord, destroyed the enemy, and with the strength of your majesty, Lord, you broke the adversaries. You sent your anger, and it consumed them like chaff. We feared you when you were born 2, we believed in you, and all our crimes were consumed. Indeed, why were the waters divided by the breath of the Lord's wrath, the waters froze, forming like a wall; the waves froze in the middle of the sea, if in this division of the water, the waves freezing, a way was opened for the liberated people? Why were the waters not divided, rather, by the breath of the Lord's mercy but because the terror of his wrath, which despises that sinner who reaches the abyss of evils, is what drives us to baptism to be delivered through water, not by drowning, but by passing along the way?

whose temple was a passing figure, as appropriate, indicated that he was speaking of the eternal kingdom, which is the inheritance of God, the eternal Jerusalem. He then said: What your hand has prepared, O Lord! You who reign always, forever and even more. Is there anything that lasts longer than forever? Who can say? Why then did he add: and even more? Since it is customary to understand forever in the sense of a very long period of time, perhaps that is why he added: and even more so, so that authentic eternity, which has no end, could be understood. Does he speak thus, perhaps, because God always reigns in the heavenly kingdoms, which he established forever and ever, and established a precept that will not pass away; at the same time that he reigns forever in those to whom, after they were converted, he forgave the sins caused by the transgression of the precept and acquired them at a precise moment and gave them endless happiness, and he still reigns in those whom he placed, in the midst of most just tortures, at the feet of his people? For no one is excluded from the reign of him whose eternal law regulates all creatures within a most just order through the dialectic of giving and asking for accounts and the merit of reward and punishment. God resists the proud, while giving his grace to the humble. Pharaoh's cavalry entered the sea with the chariots and knights, and the Lord let the waters of the sea fall on them. This seems appropriate to think that it means the drum that Mary took to accompany the song. To make a drum, the meat is spread on a piece of wood; and from the cross they learn to confess the soft sound of grace. Made humble, therefore, through baptism, by the grace of piety and quenched in it our pride, by which the proud enemy ruled over us, so that whoever glories, glories in the Lord, we may sing to the Lord, for he has shown himself great and glorious; He threw horse and knight into the sea.

The rich epulon and the poor Lazarus (Luke 16,19-31)
Theme: The rich epulon and the poor Lazarus (Luke 16, 19-31). Location: Unknown. Roof: Unknown.

1. Your holiness, dearly beloved brothers, has noticed and, I believe, has considered with the utmost attention of the mind the opulence of the rich and the poverty of the beggar; the first, abounding in food, and the second, fainting from hunger. The two were certainly men, men of flesh and mortals, but they were not equal. The nature was the same, but the way of life was not. None of them is free from the mortal condition, and yet one feasts splendidly and the other appears all disgusting, wrapped in rags and squalor. He delighted in exquisite foods, the result of the inventiveness of his cooks; He was waiting for crumbs to fall from his table. Listen now, the rich who do not want to be merciful. Listen to the following: we are all born with the same condition, we live under the same light, we breathe the same air and we exhaust ourselves with the same death, which, if it did not get in the way, not even the poor would survive. This Lazarus, who lay covered with sores and naked, is carried in the hands of angels to Abraham's bosom.
DE VERBIS EVANGELII LUCAE 16,19-31; UBI DE DIVITE ET LÁZARO

CAPUT I.—1. Divitis cum Lázaro paupere comparatio. But behold, the well-fed and resplendent rich man is locked up in the prison of hell. Where is that one wearing purple? Where the life that overflowed and swam in all opulence? In the face of death, doesn't everything pass like a shadow? We have brought nothing into this world, says the Apostle, and we can take nothing from it. We carry nothing or take away with us. If we could take something, wouldn't we devour men alive? Where does such avidity in desire originate from, if even the beasts themselves maintain a certain measure? They only take prey when they feel hungry, but they ignore it when they have satisfied it. Only the greed of the rich is insatiable. He is always hoarding and is never satisfied; He neither fears God nor feels human respect; He neither forgives the father nor recognizes the mother; neither obeys his brother nor remains faithful to his friend; oppresses the widow and takes the orphan's property; He calls the freedmen back into his service and gives false testimony. Raids the property of the deceased, as if the same people who do it were not going to die. What is this madness of souls: to lose life and desire death, to acquire gold and lose heaven? Father Abraham, he said, send Lazarus - to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am tormented in the midst of these flames. But he answered him: Remember, son, that you received good things in your life, and Lazarus, on the other hand, received bad things. Riches are compensated by torments; poverty, with refreshment; the purple, with the flames; nakedness, with rest, so that the scales are kept in balance and the limit of that measure is not exceeded: With the measure with which you measure, with that you will be measured. The tormented rich man is denied mercy because in his life he did not want to be merciful; He is not heard when he begs amidst torments, because on earth he did not listen to the poor man who begged him. 3. The rich and the poor oppose each other, but they also need each other. No one would suffer need if they mutually helped each other and no one would be weary if they helped each other. The rich is made for the poor, and the poor for the rich. It is typical of the poor to ask and typical of the rich to give; God's characteristic is to reward the little with the much. A small work of mercy produces great abundance. The field of the poor is fertile; then it gives its owners the fruit. The poor is the way to heaven by which one reaches the Father. So start giving if you don't want to go astray. Break in this life the chains of your heritage that bind you, so that you can freely approach heaven; Get rid of the weight of riches, throw away the free chains.

briefly contracted; Get rid of the worries and boredom that have bothered you for so many years. Give to those who ask you so that you can receive; Give to the poor if you don't want to burn in the flames. Give to Christ on earth so that he may give it back to you in heaven. Forget what you are and consider what you are going to be. The present life is brittle and prone to death. No one can stay in it; We are all forced to leave. We go even if we don't want to; We leave reluctantly because we are bad. If we had sent something ahead of us, we wouldn't arrive at an empty hostel. In fact, what we give to the poor, we send before us; On the other hand, what we snatch, we leave everything here.

The birth of the Lord
Topic: The birth of the Lord. Place: Carthage, Restituta basilica. Date: Christmas Day.

1. Our Savior, by whom every day was made and born of the dayless Father, wanted this day that we celebrate today to be the date of his birth on earth. Whoever you are who marvels at this day, rather marvel at the eternal day that abides before every day, that creates every day, that is born in the day and delivers from the malice of the day. Admire yourself even more: the one who gave birth to him is a mother and a virgin; the born does not speak, being the Word. No wonder the heavens spoke, the angels rejoiced, the shepherds rejoiced, the wise men were transformed, the kings were troubled, and the children were crowned. Breastfeed, oh mother, our food; It suckles the bread that comes from heaven and has been placed in a manger as food for the pious donkeys. There the ox knew its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, that is, the circumcision and the foreskin, uniting in the cornerstone, whose first fruits were the shepherds and the wise men. Breastfeed the one who made you such that he could make himself into you; to whom he gave you the gift of fertility when you conceived him without depriving you of the honor at birth.

What is it like, I repeat, that birth to which the father does not give way when he dies, because he did not precede it in living? Let us raise our soul to him, as much as possible with his help, from any interval of place or time, from any spatial distance that we are accustomed to perceive either in the days, now in the bodies, in order to understand how the one who begets does not precede the begotten and how the begotten does not follow the one who begets, the Father and the Son, without both being Fathers nor both Sons, but both eternal; without both begetting, without both being born, but without one living without the other. Let us consider, if we are able, that the Father has begotten him from always and that the Son has also been born from always; If we are not capable, let us create it. Topic: The manifestation of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of the Epiphany, January 6.

1. The solemnity we celebrate today is given the Greek name of Epiphany in honor of the manifestation of the Lord. In fact, by manifesting himself today, he offers himself to the wise men, the first fruits of the Gentiles, who adore him, the one that a few days ago was given to them at birth. He is the cornerstone that united the two in their unity as walls that led in opposite directions, that is, that of the circumcision and that of the foreskin; in other words: that of the Jews and that of the Gentiles, and he became our peace, the one who made the two peoples one. To give the announcement to the Jewish shepherds, the angels came down from heaven, and for the Gentile wise men to worship him, a star shone from heaven. Now through the angels, now through the star, the heavens proclaimed the glory of God, so that by the grace of the born the apostles might also proclaim it, carrying the Lord as if they were heavens, and its sound would reach the whole earth, and its words would reach the ends of the earth. Words that also reached us; We believed them, and that is why we spoke. SERMO

The manifestation of the Lord

Topic: The manifestation of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of the Epiphany, January 6. 1. The annual celebration of this date demands from me the corresponding sermon due to your ears and your hearts. Today, the Savior led to Him the wise men, originally from a town so far away. They came to worship a child still without speech, the Word of God. Why did they come? Because they saw a new star. And how did they recognize that it was the star of Christ? They, in fact, could see the star; but could she perhaps speak to them and say to them: "I am the star of Christ"? No doubt it was revealed to them in another way through some revelation. The truth is that, in an unusual way, a king had been born who was also going to be adored by strange people. Had there not been kings previously born in Judea or in the different towns of the entire earth? Why should this one be worshiped, and worshiped by strange people, without intimidating him with any army, but rather presenting himself in the poverty of the flesh, hiding the majesty of his power? When he was born, the Israelite shepherds adored him, warned by the angels. But the wise men did not belong to the people of Israel; They worshiped the gods of the Gentiles, that is, the demons, SERMO

Christ died for us SERMON
Theme: Christ died for us. Location: Hippo. Date: Easter night.

1. We have just heard the gospel; The resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ was read. If Christ was resurrected, he died. The resurrection witnesses death, but the death of Christ means the destruction of fear. Let us not be afraid to die because Christ died for us; Let us die with the hope of eternal life, for Christ was resurrected so that we may rise again. In his death and resurrection we have the assigned task and the promised reward; The assigned task is the passion, and the promised reward is the resurrection. This task was carried out by the martyrs; Let us carry it out with piety if we cannot with the passion, since not everyone is able to suffer and die for Christ; but dying comes to everyone. Happy are those to whom what must necessarily come to them happened through Christ; Dying was a necessity for them, but dying for Christ was not. Death must come to all, but not to all death through Christ. Those whose lot it was to die for Christ, in a way, gave back to him what he had given them. The Lord had given them to die SERMO

for them; They returned it to him, dying for it. But what was a poor unfortunate man going to give back if the blessed Lord had not given it to him? Thus, Christ granted the martyrs the ability to return to him what he had given them. This is their cry: If it had not been for the Lord being with us, perhaps they would have swallowed us alive; perhaps the pursuers had swallowed us alive, he said. What does alive mean? If, despite knowing the evil we do by denying Christ, we did that great evil alive, that is, with full consciousness, in that case we would have been swallowed alive, not dead. What does alive mean? Knowing it, not in ignorance. And by what force did they not do what the persecutors forced them to do? Let's ask them; Let them tell us. See what they answer: If it had not been because the Lord was with us. So, he gave them what they were going to give him back. Let's give thanks. He was rich, and, as it is written about him, he became poor to enrich us; His poverty has enriched us, his wounds have healed us, his humility has exalted us, his death has vivified us. 2. See that our infants mix today with the faithful and in a certain sense fly out of the nest. It is necessary, therefore, that, as parents, we speak to them. As you well remember, my brothers, when the chicks of swallows and other domestic birds begin to fly out of the nest, their mothers fly noisily around it, and their pious chirps testify to the dangers that their children run. We know that many who call themselves faithful live poorly and that their customs are not in accordance with the grace they have received; who praise God with their tongues and blaspheme Him with their lives. We know, however, that there are others among those many who, like grains among abundant chaff, groan in the threshing, but console themselves with the hope of the granary. We know that these two classes of men are found in the Church. We know the era of the Lord; We wait for the winnowing of the day of judgment, we long for the ground of wheat on the day of resurrection, and we long to enter the granary into eternal life. There will be no straw there, just as in the habent octaves hodie: et isti senes, iuvenes, adolescentuli, omnes infantes. Una quippe illorum infantia pertinet ad vetustatem, alter ad novitatem. Nam quos videtis recentes a partu, veteres nascuntur. Vetus homo noster dictus est Adam, ex quo nascimur: novus homo Christus, per quem renascimur. Isti ergo et novi sunt, et renati sunt ad alliam vitam, et est in illis, si dici potest, quando nascuntur, nova vetustas. 23). Baptize them hortatur and imitate bad Christians. In Ecclesia mali bonis permixti.—Ecce miscentur hodie fidelibus infantes nostri, et tanquam de nido volant. Necesse est ergo, ut parturients eos alloquamur. Sicut enim recolitis, fratres mei, hirundinum vel domesticorum passerum pullos, quando velare de nido coeperint, matres cum strepitu circumvolant, et vocibus piis testantur pericula filiorum.

Scimus ergo multos, qui appellantur fideles, male vivere, et gratiae, quam acceperunt, moribus suis non convenire; laudare Deum lingua, blasphemare vita. hell there will be no wheat. Now, therefore, my brothers, although we know that this double class of men exists in the Church, that is, of the pious and the impious, the good and the bad, the fearful and the mocking, we do not know with whom these are going to associate. They know well what we want; As to whether our desires will be fulfilled in them, human ignorance grows tired of worry and is sometimes disturbed by false suspicions. It is a teaching for us on this earth, where we do not live without temptations. Therefore I admonish you, holy shoots; I warn you, a new plantation in the field of the Lord, so that it does not have to be said of you what was said of the house of Israel: I waited for it to bear grapes, but it gave me thorns. May I find in you a cluster who, like a cluster, was trampled on our behalf. Give grapes, live well. For, as the Apostle says, the fruits of the spirit are love, joy, peace, long-suffering, kindness, goodness, meekness, fidelity, continence, chastity. When our farmer comes to us, the one whose workers we are and who gives growth from within, then we will know how to plant and water outside, but the Apostle says: Neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but it is God who gives the growth, who already now is seeing how you listen and watching how you fear or begin to fear; So when that farmer comes, let him find in you what the Apostle had said: You are my joy and my crown, all of you who stand firm in the Lord.

Topic: The ascension of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of the Ascension.

Dear brothers: who can utter a word worthy of the eternal Word? Can the smallest be enough to speak of the great? The heavens praise her, the virtues praise her, the powers of the air praise her, the stars of heaven praise her, the stars praise her and the earth also praises her, as much as she can; such praise is not what is deserved, but it avoids condemnation for ingratitude. Who can explain, or speak, or know him who reaches out with power from one end to the other and arranges everything smoothly, and leaps for joy to run the way, leaving one end of the heavens and making his race to the other end? If it's everywhere, how does it come out? If it is everywhere, where is it headed? It neither changes place, nor varies in time, nor does it undergo advances and returns; remaining in itself, it surrounds everything in its fullness. What spaces are there that do not contain the omnipotent, that do not contain the one who is immense, that do not welcome the one who comes? If you think about the Word, I haven't said anything. But to teach the humble to say something about themselves, he humbled himself, SERMO

taking the form of a servant. In this way he descended; In this way he progressed, as the gospel says, in the desire for wisdom; In this way he was patient, in this way he fought bravely, in this way he died, in this way he defeated death and was resurrected, in this way he returned to heaven who had never left there. Blessed is, therefore, in the firmament of heaven who, according to the Apostle, became cursed for us so that the Gentiles might obtain the blessing of Abraham. He jumped for joy like a giant. Giant, why? He surpassed death with his death. Giant, why? He broke down the gates of hell, came out and ascended. Who is this king of glory by whom it was said to certain princes: Remove, O princes, your gates and rise, eternal gates? Rise, for he is great; you are narrow, you have no capacity; rise. So that? So that the king of glory may enter. They are filled with dread: Who is this king of glory? They don't recognize it. He is not only God, he is also man; He is not only man, he is also God. Suffer the passion: is it, in truth, God? Resurrected: is he really a man? Or is he God and man at the same time? For his passion and his resurrection are authentic. This is said up to twice in the same psalm: Remove, O princes, your gates; Rise up, eternal gates, and the king of glory will enter. And after these words he repeats the same thing. You might think that this is something superfluous and not necessary; But consider the purpose intended by the repetition of identical words and note why they were repeated twice. They open

twice the gates, that is, those of hell and those of heaven, for him who has risen once and has ascended once to heaven. Two novelties come together: that God appears in hell and that a man is assumed into heaven. At both times, in both places, princes tremble. Who is this king of glory? How can we know? Listen to what is answered; Their questions are answered: The Lord strong and powerful, the Lord powerful in war. In what war? In suffering death for mortals, suffering alone for all, not resisting being omnipotent, and yet conquering by dying. Great, then, is this king of glory even in hell. This same thing is repeated to the heavenly powers: Remove, O princes, your doors; Elevate, eternal doors. Or are not those doors whose keys Peter received eternal? But since he carries the man with him, he is not recognized there, and the question is asked: Who is this king of glory? But since there he no longer fights, but is victorious; no longer fights, but reaps the triumph, they are not answered: The Lord powerful in war, but: The Lord of hosts is the king of glory.

The Holy Spirit gives love

Theme: The Holy Spirit gives love and inaugurates eternal life. Location: Unknown. Date: Day of Pentecost. This solemnity is pleasing to God, in which piety regains vigor and love ardor as an effect of the presence of the Holy Spirit, as the Apostle teaches when he says: The love of God has been diffused in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. The arrival of the Holy Spirit meant that the one hundred and twenty men gathered there were filled with it. In the reading of the Acts of the Apostles we hear that one hundred and twenty people were gathered in a room waiting for the promise of Christ. They had been told to remain in the city until they were clothed with power from above. Well, the Lord said to them, I will send you my promise. He is faithful in promising and kind in fulfilling. What he promised on earth, he sent after ascending to heaven. We have a pledge of the future eternal life and the kingdom of heaven. If he did not deceive us in this first promise, is he going to disappoint us in what we hope for in the future? earnest money, which attest that later what they give as a guarantee will come. Christ gave us the earnest of the Holy Spirit; He, who could not deceive us, gave us full security when he gave us those deposits, although he would fulfill what he promised even without having left them to us. What did he promise? Eternal life, leaving us the guarantee of the Spirit. Eternal life is the possession of the inhabitants, while the earnest money is a consolation for the pilgrims. It is more appropriate to talk about a deposit than a pledge. These two things seem identical, but there is a non-negligible difference between them. If earnest money or a pledge is given, it is with a view to fulfilling what was promised; but, when a pledge is given, the man returns what was given to him; On the other hand, when the deposit is given, it is not recovered, but what is necessary is added until the agreed amount is reached. So we have the earnest money; Let us thirst for the very source from which the earnest money flows. We have a certain dew of the Holy Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee so that if anyone notices this dew, they will want to go to the source. Why, then, do we have the deposits if not to not faint from hunger and thirst on this pilgrimage? If we recognize that we are pilgrims, we will undoubtedly feel hungry and thirsty. Whoever is a pilgrim and is aware of it, desires the homeland, and, while that desire lasts, the pilgrimage is annoying. If he loves pilgrimage, he forgets his homeland and does not want to return to it. Our country is not such that anything else can be put before it. Sometimes men become rich at the time of pilgrimage. Those who suffered need dant: et arrha data fidem facit, etiam rem illam esse secuturam, cuíus arrha praecessit. What did you promise? Vitam aeternam, cuius arrham Spiritum sanctum dedit. Vita aeterna possessio habitantium: arrha consolatio est peregrinantium. Melius enim dicitur arrha quam pignus. Arrham ergo habemus: ipsum fontem, unde arrha est, sitiamus.

1. For those who are still, a little voice is enough. If you want, brothers, to listen calmly, do not have your heart in your ears, but your ears in your heart. IN NATIVITATE IOANNIS BAPTISTAE, II

1. Christum temporaliter natum praecessit Iohannes. Nativitates Christi duae. Superbia, tumor. Incarttationis causa, ut homini Deus exemplum praeberet.—Quietis et parva vox sufficit. Oportet autem hoc de ipso die credere, quod sine varietate totus orbis agnoscit: sed quia Ioannis esse diem nemo dubitat, non Ioannis qui Evangelium scripsit, sed Ioannis Baptistae praecursoris Domini, qui mucho magnus apparuit, ciuanto se humilem praebuit, they say, The Maurinos doubted his authenticity, today generally accepted for the non-interpolated form.

Christ, who was not worthy of untying the strap of the shoe of the one whom he recognized as Lord, in order to deserve to be his friend. Some think that today is the day of his passion. Thus, then, John preceded the Lord, not as the teacher preceded the disciple, but as the herald preceded the judge; not to impose his authority, but to fulfill a function. We know two births of the Lord, one divine and the other human, but both admirable; he without a mother, this one without a father; that eternal one, to create the temporal one; this temporary, to manifest the eternal. centuries before all centuries, he became so small that he was even born of a woman, but he remained so large that he was not separated from the Father. Presenting themselves before him, like lamps before the day, and offering him their testimony, all the prophets who announced him preceded him in birth, and, by believing and uniting with him, he preceded them. It was appropriate that they announce his coming and miracles; miracles that would show him as God to those who understood well, although those who limited themselves to looking with human eyes would see him as a man, small for the small, but humble for the proud, teaching man, with his smallness, to recognize himself as small and not to believe himself great because he is swollen without having grown. Pride, in fact, is not greatness, but puffiness. To heal this swelling of the human race, being himself a doctor and medicine, that is, not only showing the medicine, but also becoming it himself, he appeared before men as a man, offering his human being to those who saw him and reserving his divine being for those who believed in him. The look of his humanity healed the weak; Contemplation of his divinity requires strong people. There were still no men who could see God in man, they could only see man; However, they should not put their hope in man. What to do then? Man can see man, but he cannot follow man. It was necessary to follow God, who could not be seen, and not follow man, who could be seen. So God became man in order to show himself to man to

that the man saw him and followed him. O man, through whom God became man! You must believe yourself truly great; but he descends in order to ascend, since God also became man by descending. Adhere to your medicine, imitate your teacher, acknowledge your Lord, embrace your brother, understand your God. This was that one, so big and so small: a worm, not a man; but by him was man made. This is him; What is John but what the truthful person says about him, what the truth says about him? Indeed, if we are to believe John speaking of the truth, should we not believe the truth speaking of John? 3. How is God to grow? And glorify your Father who is in heaven. The Father is glorified, the Son is glorified, since the Father glorifies the Son and the Son the Father. Let the humble man be recognized, then; recognize that the exalted God has humbled himself for him, so that man, humbled by the confession of sin, may be exalted by the achievement of justice. There are, therefore, two realities: the Lord and John, humility and greatness; God, humble in his greatness, and man, humble in his weakness; God, humble for man, and man, humble for himself. and to justice, saying: It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife. The law that had ordained this referred to men who had died childless, and provided that brothers should take their brothers' wives and give them offspring. Where this circumstance did not exist, there was nothing but passion. This passion was what Juan recriminated; The chaste accused the dishonest, since what appeared was nothing other than this: It is appropriate that he increase and that I, on the other hand, decrease. It had already been ordered that, if someone died without issue, his closest relative would take his wife and give her to him. Why had God ordained this if not to signify in this way that offspring must be given to the brother in the name of the brother? This law had been established so that those born in this way would bear the name of the deceased. Christ died, and the apostles took his wife, the Church. Those who were engendered by her were not called Paulines or Petrines, but Christians. Thus, the passions of both indicate this reality: It is appropriate for him to increase and for me, on the other hand, to decrease. Christ grew on the tree, John diminished with the sword. Their respective passions showed this mystery; let the days also show it: Christ is born, and they increase; Juan is born, and they decrease. Topic: The dignity of Saints Peter and Paul. Location: Unknown. Date: June 29, feast of Saint Peter and Saint Paul. As witnessed by the faith of the Roman Church, today is the day on which the apostles Peter and Paul, after having defeated the devil, merited the crown of triumph. Let us offer a solemn sermon to those in whose honor this also solemn festival is celebrated. Hear our praises and pray for us. As we have known from the tradition of our ancestors and memory preserves it, they did not suffer their passion on a single day marked by the celestial spaces. Paul suffered it on the day of Peter's birth; not that in which he was thrown into the number of men from his mother's womb, but that other in which, from the chains of the flesh, he was born into the light of the angels. For this reason, a single day has been assigned to both, to celebrate them on a single date. Here I see a great sign of harmony: the last of the apostles, called on the same day and crowned on the same date, arrived and coincided with the first, an apostle like him. Peter was chosen before the passion, Paul after the ascension. Unequal in time, equal in the eternity of happiness; that one had been a fisherman, this one a pursuer. In the first one it was SERMO

Petri et Pauli apostolorüm dies, in quo triumphalem coronam, devicto diabolo, meruerunt, quantum fides Romana testatur, hodiernus est. Quibus solemnis festivitas exhibitiontur, solemnis etiam sermo reddatur. Laudes audiant a nobis, preces fundant pro nobis. Sicut traditione patrum cognitum memoria retinetur, non uno die passi sunt per caeli spatia decurrente. Natalitio ergo Petri passus est Paulus, non quo ex uterus matris in numerum fusus est hominum, sed quo ex vinculo carnis in luzem natus est Angelorum; ac per hoc ita singuli dies dati sunt duobus, ut nunc unus celebretur ambobus. Magnum hoc mihi signum videtur esse concordiae: coapostolo suo novissimus primo, qui ad eumdem diem vocatus advenit, ad eumdem diem coronatus oceurrit. Electus is ille ante Domini passionem, iste post ascensionem. Ordine temporis oddes, aeternitate felicitatis aequales: ille ex piscatore, iste ex persecutore. chosen the weak in the world to confuse the strong; In the second sin abounded so that grace might abound. In both of them shone the greatness of God's grace and the glory of the one who created, not found, their merits. Who first called the fishermen to his kingdom, having then called the emperors, what else did he want to show but that he who glories, glories in the Lord? In fact, he did not despise the salvation of the noble, the wise and the powerful who put them before the commoners, the ignorant and the weak. But if he had not first chosen the vileness of the weak, he would not have healed the swelling of the proud. If Christ had called the rich first, they could think and say that in them he had chosen nothing other than opulence, wealth, knowledge of eloquence, the splendor of science, nobility, generosity, tranquility, royal power, and thus, inflated with temporal and worldly happiness, as if they themselves offered to Christ what they are, seeming to them that what they were going to be by the grace of God, instead of a gift, was reward from Christ, they would neither understand nor retain that grace. So, how much better and how much more orderly was he who first raised the needy from the earth and raised the poor from the dung to place him among the princes of his people, so that the gift of intelligence and doctrine not only really came from God, but also that divine origin would clearly appear! With how much joy and with how much glory for God we contemplate

how the soul of the fisherman despises the riches of the emperor and how the emperor supplicates before the tomb of the fisherman! Neither the fisherman felt neglected for lacking them nor did the emperor boast of possessing them. Let the Apostle himself tell us what value it has for the salvation of men—so that no one, conscious of his evils, despairs of God's mercy—is the fact that Christ has transformed someone who was his persecutor into his preacher. It is a human word, he said, and worthy of being accepted by all, that Christ came into this world to save sinners, the first of whom is me. But for this I have obtained mercy: to show in me first of all all the magnanimity of Christ Jesus, for the instruction of those who will believe in him for eternal life. Who can lose hope in his salvation under the hand of the almighty doctor, after having known such a notable example and seeing that Paul, now a messenger of the faith that he previously persecuted, not only escaped the punishment he deserved as a persecutor, but even achieved the crown of doctor, and that, once a believer, he shed his for the name of the one whose blood he wanted to cruelly spill on his members? Rome, the head of the Gentiles, has, therefore, the two lights of the Gentiles lit by him who illuminates every man who comes into this world; one, in which he exalted abject humility, and another, in which he healed iniquity, worthy of condemnation. Let us learn in the first not to boast, and in the second, not to lose hope. In what a simple way some examples have been proposed to us!

Theme: Love of enemies. Location: Unknown. Date: Unknown. 1. Focus, my brothers, on love, which Scripture praises in such a way that it admits that nothing can compare to it. When God exhorts us to love one another, is He exhorting you to love only those who love you? This is a compensatory love, which God does not consider sufficient. He wanted us to come to love our enemies when he said: Love your enemies; Do good to those who hate you and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven, who makes his sun rise on the good and the evil, and sends rain on the just and the unjust. What do you say to this? Do you love your enemy? Perhaps you will answer me: "My weakness prevents me from doing so." Get going, do it by power, especially considering that you have to pray to the judge whom no one can deceive and who will take your case. Question, then, that judge where no messenger causes confusion, no magistrate backs down and no lawyer is sent who can intercede for you or say the words that you have not SERMO
